Continue with the same fixed $\Lambda_n$, ambient categories, and
noetherian finite-dimensional $Y,Y'$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and
finitely presented, let the square in A31 be Cartesian, and let
$K\in D_c^+(X,\Lambda_n)$. For the dense compactification $C$ of
(BA43-DENSE-DATA), construct the raw one-model map as the following
two-arrow composite:

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{BC}^{C,\mathrm{raw}}_{f,g,K}:Lg^*F_C(K)
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{BC}_{p_C,g,Rj_{C!}K}}
Rp^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,g,*}L\bar g^*Rj_{C!}K\\
&\xrightarrow{Rp^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,g,*}
(\beta^{\mathrm{open}}_{j_C,\bar g,K})}
Rp^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,g,*}Rj^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,g,!}Lg'^*K.
\end{split}
\tag{BA33-RAW-BC}
$$

Here the first arrow is the already constructed proper base-change mate and
the second is the derived open-extension exchange. By definition the name
$\operatorname{BC}^{C,\mathrm{raw}}$ denotes their composite, never the first
arrow alone. Before finite PBC is applied, the separate leaf
`CAT-GEO-BA33-OPEN-EXTENSION-CONSTRUCTIBILITY` must prove
$Rj_{C!}K\in D_c^+(\overline X_C,\Lambda_n)$.

The dense representative is

$$
\operatorname{BC}^{C,\mathrm{den}}_{f,g,K}
=\sigma_{C,g}^{-1}\circ
\operatorname{BC}^{C,\mathrm{raw}}_{f,g,K}:
Lg^*F_C(K)\longrightarrow
F_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}}}(Lg'^*K).
\tag{BA33-DEN-BC}
$$

For a refinement $q:D\to C$,
`OBL-BA33-REFINEMENT-BASECHANGE-NATURALITY` proves equality of the
two explicit composites built from $Lg^*(\rho_q)$,
$\rho_{q_g^{\mathrm{den}}}$, the two maps
(BA33-DEN-BC), and the densification comparison. The proof must
expand proper-base-change naturality, open-exchange naturality, and all four
densification diagrams; the equality is not supplied in a comparison record.

Only then may the $\kappa$ cocycle descend the representatives to

$$
Lg^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*K.
$$

Identity and horizontal/vertical pasting consume the corresponding proper,
open, densification, and $\kappa$ equations. Therefore
`OBL-BA33-FINITE-COMPACT-SUPPORT-BASE-CHANGE` remains
`OPEN/INCOMPLETE`. Geometric-fibre, Frobenius-equivariant, tower,
integral, and rational exports are outside this finite-level owner.

Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be an arbitrary morphism with both $Y$ and $Y'$ noetherian
and finite-dimensional. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ and

$$
\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{raw}}=\overline X_C\times_Y Y'.
$$

The pulled-back open need not be dense. Define the dense model by schematic
closure

$$
\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{den}}
=\overline{X'}^{\,\mathrm{sch}}
\subset\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{raw}},
\qquad
d_{C,g}:\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{den}}
\longrightarrow\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{raw}}.
\tag{BA43-DEN}
$$

The schematic-closure leaf proves that $d_{C,g}$ is the resulting closed
proper map and that it restricts to the identity on $X'$.

**Formalization note.** The *flat* case of the base change above is formalized:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Compactification.isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_i_ofIsPullback`
(`WeilConjectures/Compactification/BaseChange.lean`) proves that if $g$ is flat and
the quasi-compact open immersion $j_C$ is scheme-theoretically dominant, then so is the open
immersion of $\overline X_{C,g}^{\mathrm{raw}}$; that is, for flat $g$ the raw pullback is
already dense and no densification is needed. The base changed compactification itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Compactification.ofIsPullback`. For a general $g$ the schematic
closure (BA43-DEN) is still required and remains open; see
`GEO-BA43-SCHEMATIC-CLOSURE-DENSIFICATION`.

A raw compactification is data

$$
R=(X'\xrightarrow{j_R}\overline X_R\xrightarrow{p_R}Y',
\epsilon_R:p_R\circ j_R=f'),
\tag{BA43-RAW-DATA}
$$

with $j_R$ open and $p_R$ proper and finitely presented, but with no density
condition. Its stored equation $\epsilon_R$ is part of the type, and
$F_R^{\mathrm{amb}}=Rp_{R*}Rj_{R!}$ is a functor
$D^+(X'_{\acute et},\Lambda_n)\to D^+(Y'_{\acute et},\Lambda_n)$.
Its $D_c^+$ restriction is asserted only after a constructibility theorem.
Raw models are not objects of the dense
refinement category and have no $\kappa$ arrows.

The terminal leaf `CAT-GEO-BA43-DENSE-TO-RAW-SUPPORT` has exactly one
output:

$$
\gamma^{\mathrm{raw}}_{d_{C,g}}:
Rd_{C,g*}Rj_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}}!}
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{C_g^{\mathrm{raw}}!}.
\tag{BA43-GAMMA-RAW}
$$

It outputs neither $\sigma$, nor refinement naturality, nor identity,
iterated-base-change, or open-exchange coherence. Those are all conclusions
of the middle reassembly `OBL-BA43-BASECHANGE-DENSIFICATION`. Using
proper-direct-image composition, that middle owner first defines

$$
\sigma_{C,g}:F_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}}}
\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{C_g^{\mathrm{raw}}}.
\tag{BA43-SIGMA}
$$

It must then prove the following four separately owned diagrams. For a
refinement $q:D\to C$, let $\rho^{\mathrm{den}}_{q,g}$ and
$\rho^{\mathrm{raw}}_{q,g}$ be the proper-support comparisons already
constructed by `OBL-BA43-REFINEMENT-EXCHANGE` on the densified and raw
pullbacks. Refinement naturality is the
commutative square

$$
\begin{CD}
F_{D_g^{\mathrm{den}}} @>{\sigma_{D,g}}>> F_{D_g^{\mathrm{raw}}}\\
@V{\rho^{\mathrm{den}}_{q,g}}VV @VV{\rho^{\mathrm{raw}}_{q,g}}V\\
F_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}}} @>{\sigma_{C,g}}>> F_{C_g^{\mathrm{raw}}}.
\end{CD}
\tag{BA43-DEN-REF}
$$

After the canonical identifications
$C_{\mathrm{id}}^{\mathrm{den}}=C_{\mathrm{id}}^{\mathrm{raw}}=C$, identity
coherence is the equation

$$
\sigma_{C,\mathrm{id}_Y}=1_{F_C}.
\tag{BA43-DEN-ID}
$$

For $Y''\xrightarrow{h}Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, let
$\delta_{C;g,h}:(C_g^{\mathrm{den}})_h^{\mathrm{den}} \xrightarrow{\sim}C_{gh}^{\mathrm{den}}$ be the canonical comparison of the
two schematic closures. Let $\tau_{C;g,h}$ be the proper-support comparison
from $(C_g^{\mathrm{den}})_h^{\mathrm{raw}}$ to $C_{gh}^{\mathrm{raw}}$
induced by the base change of $d_{C,g}$. Iterated coherence is

$$
\begin{CD}
F_{(C_g^{\mathrm{den}})_h^{\mathrm{den}}}
@>{F(\delta_{C;g,h})}>> F_{C_{gh}^{\mathrm{den}}}\\
@V{\sigma_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}},h}}VV @VV{\sigma_{C,gh}}V\\
F_{(C_g^{\mathrm{den}})_h^{\mathrm{raw}}}
@>{\tau_{C;g,h}}>> F_{C_{gh}^{\mathrm{raw}}}.
\end{CD}
\tag{BA43-DEN-ITER}
$$

Finally let
$A=L\bar g_{\mathrm{raw}}^*Rj_{C!}K$ and let
$s_d:A\xrightarrow{\sim}Rd_{C,g*}Ld_{C,g}^*A$ be the closed-support
identification. Construct the raw and dense open-exchange maps independently.
Open-exchange coherence is precisely

$$
\begin{CD}
A @>{\beta^{\mathrm{raw}}_{j_C,g,K}}>>
Rj_{C_g^{\mathrm{raw}}!}Lg'^*K\\
@V{s_d}VV @VV{(\gamma^{\mathrm{raw}}_{d_{C,g}})^{-1}}V\\
Rd_{C,g*}Ld_{C,g}^*A
@>{Rd_{C,g*}(\beta^{\mathrm{den}}_{j_C,g,K})}>>
Rd_{C,g*}Rj_{C_g^{\mathrm{den}}!}Lg'^*K.
\end{CD}
\tag{BA43-DEN-OPX}
$$

None of these equations is a field of (BA43-GAMMA-RAW).

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and finitely presented. A dense
compactification is data

$$
C=(X\xrightarrow{j_C}\overline X_C\xrightarrow{p_C}Y,
\epsilon_C:p_C\circ j_C=f),
\tag{BA43-DENSE-DATA}
$$

where $j_C$ is a schematically dense open immersion and $p_C$ is proper and
finitely presented. The equality $\epsilon_C$ is stored structure data. A
refinement $q:D\to C$ is a $Y$-map with $qj_D=j_C$ and
$q^{-1}(X)=X$. Its properness is a separate geometric atom.

Before any constructible restriction, set

$$
F_C^{\mathrm{amb}}=Rp_{C*}Rj_{C!}:
D^+(X_{\acute et},\Lambda_n)\longrightarrow
D^+(Y_{\acute et},\Lambda_n).
\tag{BA43-AMBIENT-F}
$$

All $F_C$ and all selected $Rf_!$ in this fragment denote these ambient
functors. A restriction to $D_c^+$ is a separate theorem. Consequently
$Rg_!^{\mathrm{amb}}Rf_!^{\mathrm{amb}}$ is typed before any assertion that
$Rf_!K$ is constructible.

The refinement middle owner constructs

$$
\gamma_q:Rq_*Rj_{D!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{C!},
\qquad
\rho_q:R(p_Cq)_*Rj_{D!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{C*}Rj_{C!},
\tag{BA43-RHO}
$$

and proves identity, composition, and required naturality. It also constructs
the same proper-support comparison $\rho_q^{\mathrm{raw}}$ for a proper map
between typed raw models that is the identity over the source open; density is
not used for that construction. Only dense models enter the following
$\kappa$ system. For a common
dense refinement $E$, set

$$
\kappa_{C,D}=\rho_{E\to D}\,\rho_{E\to C}^{-1}.
$$

Schematic-density uniqueness, common refinement, and the equations for
$\rho$ must prove independence of $E$ and the $\kappa$ cocycle.

**Formalization note.** The comparison map of (BA43-RHO) is now constructed in Lean, in the
bounded below variant, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusComparison`
(`WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Derived/LowerShriekComparison.lean`), for a refinement
whose square over the source open is Cartesian, and both of its functoriality laws are proved in
that same file. The identity law
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusComparison_id`
says that the comparison attached to the identity refinement of a compactification is the
identity natural transformation; the composition law
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusComparison_comp`
says that for refinements `r : c.Refinement d` and `s : d.Refinement e` whose
squares over the source open are Cartesian, the comparison attached to `r.comp s`, taken
for the pasted square
`AlgebraicGeometry.Compactification.Refinement.isPullback_comp` of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/RefinementPullback.lean`, is the comparison of
`s` followed by the comparison of `r` — in that order and not the reverse, the
formalized map being contravariant in the refinement, for the reason given next. It is still
not known to be an isomorphism, and the further naturality that (BA43-RHO) asks for is
not formalized either. The isomorphism property is exactly what
`OBL-BA43-REFINEMENT-EXCHANGE` demands, it needs proper base change, and it remains open,
as does the $\kappa$ system built on it.

**The formalized arrow points the other way.** It goes from the coarser model to
the finer one, $Rp_{C*}Rj_{C!}\to R(p_Cq)_*Rj_{D!}$ in the lettering above, that is
$F_C\to F_D$, the reverse of the $\rho_q$ displayed here. (In Lean a refinement is written
`r : c.Refinement d` with `c` the finer model, so the declaration reads
$Rf_!(d)\to Rf_!(c)$, coarse to fine.) This is deliberate. Neither direction is formal: the
available adjunctions produce a *cospan*, both of whose legs point into
$Rp_{C*}Rq_*Dq^*Rj_{C!}$, so an arrow between $F_C$ and $F_D$ exists only once one leg is
inverted. Inverting the leg that yields the direction displayed above is precisely proper base
change; inverting the other leg, the base change isomorphism
$Rj_{D!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Dq^*Rj_{C!}$ coming from $q^{-1}(X)=X$, is what the Cartesian
hypothesis supplies, and it yields the opposite arrow. So the direction constructible without
proper base change is the reverse of the blueprint's. The two maps are mutually inverse as soon
as both legs are isomorphisms, so the reversal changes no mathematical content.

The declaration is the bounded below (`Plus`) comparison only. No unbounded
variant is formalized: there is no unbounded $Dq^*\dashv Rq_*$ adjunction in this repository, and
the unbounded composition isomorphism for $Rp_*$ rests on the still `sorry`ed
`HasKInjectiveResolutions`.

For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, a successive witness includes a
Cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\overline X_f&\xrightarrow{u\ \mathrm{schematically\ dense\ open}}&W\\
\mathllap{p_f}\downarrow&&\downarrow\mathrlap{\bar p\ \mathrm{proper}}\\
Y&\xrightarrow{j_g}&\overline Y_g
\end{array}
$$

and a stored equality proving that $u\circ j_f:X\to W$ is schematically
dense. The open–proper exchange

$$
Rj_{g!}Rp_{f*}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar p_*Ru_!
\tag{BA43-OPX}
$$

must satisfy refinement naturality and typed two-square and three-square
pasting. The separately constructed isomorphism

$$
Ru_!Rj_{f!}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(u\circ j_f)_!
$$

has unit, composition, and pentagon laws. Two-witness independence and triple
pasting then reassemble the choice-independent comparison
$Rg_!Rf_!\to R(gf)_!$. Thus
`OBL-BA43-RELATIVE-COHERENT-CORE` remains
`OPEN/INCOMPLETE`.

The passage from finite torsion coefficients to $\mathbb Z_\ell$, $\mathbb Q_\ell$ and $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ — derived completion, inversion of
$\ell$, and the colimit over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_\ell$ — is a
layer built on top of the finite torsion theory. It is assumed nowhere in the
chapters below, and it is not implemented in Lean: the pro-étale site does
not occur in the development, and the coefficients there are always modules
over a ring, never a completed or adic object. In the blueprint it lives
in the proper base change sections S8 (étale-to-pro-étale finite-level
transport), S9 (derived completion and inverse limits) and S10 (complete
pro-étale proper base change) of [chap-proper-base-change], and in the
sketch articles 40–42 (`40_finite_torsion_proetale.tex`,
`41_adic_rational_coefficients.tex`,
`42_qbarl_triangulated_colimit.tex`). A statement in one of those
places is therefore not a statement about the objects the earlier chapters
formalise, and should not be cited as one.

attrs.title: Adic coefficients are a later layer

objects.body:
The formal development (`AlgebraicGeometry.StrictTransform`,
specialized to blow-ups as
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.strictTransform`) works with this
scheme-theoretic-closure definition directly, and proves the identification
over the preserved open ([lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement])
by scheme-image flat base change for a quasi-compact flat monomorphism
(`Nagata.ker_comap_self`), not through the torsion-quotient chart
model. The chart-by-chart infrastructure below
([def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-ring] through
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product]) is accordingly
not formalized — with the exception of the chart surjectivity
([lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective]), which is proved in the
subring-generation form used by the formalized Tag 080E route; of the
power-torsion material only the affine algebraic layer
(`Submodule.powTorsion` and its localization/exactness lemmas) is.
The identification of the strict transform with the blow-up of the
extended ideal ([thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup],
Stacks Tag 080E) *is* formalized, but by the universal-property route
recorded in [def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison] and the
revised proof of [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] — a
comparison morphism into the fibre product which is a closed immersion by
a chart-wise surjectivity computation, together with schematic density of
the exceptional complement — rather than by gluing the chart-ring
isomorphisms.

attrs.title: Affine blow-ups and their standard charts

objects.body:
The product-ideal theorem treats a second center pulled back from the original
scheme. Stability of admissible blow-ups under composition needs the more
general statement in which the second center is an arbitrary finite-presentation
closed subscheme of the first blow-up.

attrs.title: An arbitrary composition of two blow-ups

objects.body:
The formal statement
(`exists_finiteDegree_center_le_blowup`) recasts Tag 0803 purely
in ideal-sheaf terms: $Z'$ is replaced by a finite-type ideal sheaf
$\mathcal J$ on the blow-up and the conclusion is the inverse-image
equality $\mathcal L\cdot\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I_E^d\cdot\mathcal J$ for
a finite-type $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal I^d$; no relative-Proj quotient
is formed, and the support bound is recovered downstream
(`coe_support_eq_of_comap_pow_mul`). The choice-packaged
[def-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree] is replaced by the bare
existential.

**Status.** Every entry in this appendix remains OPEN. The middle entries are reductions; the leaf entries are the exact terminal proof obligations. No entry is discharged by the extracted prose alone. The eight obligations `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-SERRE`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-FINITE-DIRECT-IMAGE`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-SEED-LEAVES`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-AFFINE-LINE-DEVISSAGE`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-AFFINE-SPACE`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-CLOSED-IMMERSION`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-AFFINE-MORPHISM`, `OBL-A4-RC-FORMAL-PROPER-CECH` and the obligation `OBL-SIX-FUNCTOR-ADIC` are referenced in the extracted prose but own no entry in this chapter: they lie outside the extracted S0–S10 block, and this chapter states no interface for them.

attrs.title: Case 1: extending a map to relative affine space

objects.body:
This is the relative form of quasi-affineness, and it is the hypothesis Cases
1–3 below actually use. Over an affine base it says exactly that $Y$ is a
quasi-affine scheme, so the reduction in Case 1 to an absolutely quasi-affine
$Y$ loses nothing. Conversely a quasi-compact morphism whose source is a
quasi-affine scheme is quasi-affine, since a quasi-compact open subscheme of a
quasi-affine scheme is quasi-affine, and an affine morphism is quasi-affine.
