The goal of this chapter is Chow's lemma in its general form: for a separated
morphism of finite type $f\colon X\to S$ with $S$ noetherian there is a proper
surjective morphism $\pi\colon X'\to X$, an isomorphism over a dense open
subscheme of $X$, such that $X'$ admits an immersion into some
$\mathbf P^n_S$. This is [thm-chow-lemma]. The form in which it enters
the projective reduction step of proper base change is
[cor-chow-lemma-proper]: a proper $S$-scheme is dominated by a projective
one.

The chapter follows the proof of 0200. The auxiliary
statements are collected first, so that every theorem-like environment is
immediately followed by its own proof; the main statement and its proof are in
[sec-chow-lemma-proof].

**Status.** Ordinary proper base change is used here only as the proper part of the raw compact-support comparison. Densification, open exchange, refinement independence, and all four displayed coherence diagrams are additional inputs.

**Formalization note.** The *geometric* inputs of § A43 are now formalized: existence of a
dense compactification of a separated finite-type morphism, refinements together with their
properness and their uniqueness out of a dense model, common dense refinements of two
compactifications, and flat base change of a dense compactification. What remains open in
§ A43 is the derived-categorical layer: the refinement comparison $\rho$ of
(BA43-RHO) being an isomorphism, the resulting $\kappa$ system and its
independence, the open–proper exchange (BA43-OPX), and densification after a
non-flat base change. Finite presentation of the constructed compactifications is also not
yet formalized.

This chapter sets up the constructible sheaves on the small étale site of
a scheme: the definitions, their stability under pullback, pushforward along
a closed immersion and extension by zero along an open immersion, the
open–closed dévissage, and the closure under kernels, cokernels and
extensions. Everything is classical; the references are
[SGA4] and the Stacks Project (Tags `03RW`–`03RZ`,
`05BE`, `095K`, `09YJ`). The statements are arranged
in the order in which they are formalised, and the proofs are written at
the level of detail of the Stacks Project.

**Status.** This chapter is the authoritative typing boundary for the ordinary finite-level proof. It replaces the ill-typed historical sectionwise S0 formula. Every named S0–S7 middle owner remains OPEN/INCOMPLETE, and every atomic input is listed in Appendix [app-gap-ledger].

For a Cartesian square of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
\mathllap{f'}\downarrow&&\downarrow\mathrlap{f}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y,
\end{array}
$$

and $K\in D_c^+(X,\Lambda_n)$, first construct in the ambient category the
single derived morphism

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{BC}_{f,g,K}:Lg^*Rf_*K
&\xrightarrow{\eta_{f'}}Rf'_*Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{cart}}Rf'_*Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*(Lg'^*\varepsilon_f)}Rf'_*Lg'^*K.
\end{split}
\tag{BA31-MATE}
$$

Replacement independence and naturality concern this fixed map. Its identity,
horizontal-pasting, and vertical-pasting equations must be proved by adjunction
and mate calculus.

Two stalk facts have disjoint types and disjoint uses:

1. `CAT-BA31-SHEAF-STALK-FAITHFULNESS`: if
$u,v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ are maps in the abelian category of
$\Lambda_n$-sheaves and $u_{\bar y}=v_{\bar y}$ at every geometric
point, then $u=v$. It is consumed only in S5, after the maps of
cohomology sheaves have already been constructed.
1. `CAT-BA31-DERIVED-STALK-ISO-CONSERVATIVITY`: if
$u:A\to B$ is an already constructed morphism in
$D^+(Y'_{\acute et},\Lambda_n)$ and every
$H^i(u)_{\bar y}$ is invertible, then $u$ is invertible. It is consumed
only in S6.

No stalk principle in this fragment detects equality of arbitrary derived
morphisms or constructs a derived inverse from pointwise inverses.

**S0–S7 middle interfaces.**

The following are literal middle owners and all remain
`OPEN/INCOMPLETE`.

- `OBL-BA31-S0-GLOBAL-MATE` constructs (BA31-MATE) and
proves replacement independence, naturality, identity, and both pasting
laws from the three named categorical atoms.
- `OBL-BA31-S1-FINITE` proves exact finite pushforward and the
finite geometric-fibre product formula, then identifies the latter with
the stalk of the already constructed mate.
- `OBL-BA31-S2-STABILITY` proves typed composition and
proper-surjective cancellation diagrams for the actual $Rf_*$
pseudofunctor; no inverse is supplied as input data.
- `OBL-BA31-S3-PROJECTIVE-REDUCTION` states a proper finitely
presented Chow datum and a finite-surjective retract/cancellation theorem
reducing projective space to products of projective lines.
- `OBL-BA31-S4-HENSELIAN-P1` assembles independently owned
degree-zero, affine, and torsor/degree-one theorems into the strict-henselian
projective-line comparison.
- `OBL-BA31-S5-STALK-COMPARISON` combines the strict-henselization
stalk formula and proper-curve field invariance and identifies their
comparison with $H^i(\operatorname{BC}_{f,g,K})$. Sheaf-stalk
faithfulness is used only for this equality of maps of $H^i$-sheaves.
- `OBL-BA31-S6-SHEAF-ASSEMBLY` applies only derived-stalk
isomorphism conservativity to the fixed mate after S1–S5 have proved all
its cohomology-stalk maps invertible.
- `OBL-BA31-S7-BOUNDED-BELOW` uses the selected bounded-below
Postnikov/Cartan–Eilenberg leaf, including convergence and identification
of the filtered comparison with (BA31-MATE).

The root `OBL-BA31-FINITE-PBC` remains
`OPEN/INCOMPLETE` until these middle nodes and every listed atom are
actually proved. The historical finite stalk-descent certificate is retired
and has no edge into this graph.

Let $X$ be a scheme, let $j\colon U\to X$ be an open immersion and let
$i\colon Z\to X$ be a closed immersion whose range is the complement of the
range of $j$. The goal of this chapter is the short exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal F
\longrightarrow i_*i^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow0
$$

of sheaves on the small étale site of $X$, for an arbitrary sheaf
$\mathcal F$ with values in a Grothendieck abelian category of coefficients.
It is the statement [thm-openclosed-exact] at the end of the chapter, and
everything before it is a step of its proof.

The sequence is classical — it is the excision sequence of étale
cohomology; see [MilneEtale] or [SGA4]. What this chapter
adds is a proof organised so that every step is a statement one can formalise,
and in particular a substitute for the dense-subsite argument that does not
work here ([rmk-openclosed-no-dense-subsite]).

**Status.** The following block preserves the mathematical S0–S10 body and every original
`\\ uses` declaration. The sole source-level correction is the ill-typed S0
sectionwise formula, replaced in place by the categorical mate and an explicit erratum. The
remaining propositions are conditional reassembly steps whenever their gap-ledger inputs are
OPEN.

This chapter is the purely algebraic endgame of the Weil conjectures: what one
can deduce about a power series

$$
Z(T)=\operatorname{Exp}\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
$$

from the sole knowledge that its counting numbers $N_n$ are the alternating
sums of the traces of the iterates of an endomorphism on a finite family of
finite-dimensional vector spaces. No geometry and no cohomology enter here; the
input is a *trace datum* ([def-zla-trace-datum]), which is what the
Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula will eventually supply.

The two statements this material serves are

- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zetaSeries_rational` of
`WeilConjectures/Statement.lean`: the zeta series of a scheme of
finite type over a finite field is $P/Q$ with $P,Q\in\mathbf Z[T]$ and
$Q(0)=1$. The chain that produces it is
[prop-zla-cohomological-factorization] (rationality after scalar
extension), [thm-zla-hankel-descent] together with
[cor-zla-rationality-counting-field] (descent of rationality to
$\mathbf Q$), and [thm-zla-integral-fatou] (integrality of the
reduced fraction).
- `AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeilFactorization` of
`Comparator/Weil/Definitions.lean`: the factorization
$Z\cdot\prod_{i\text{ even}}P_i=\prod_{i\text{ odd}}P_i$ with
$P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $P_i(0)=1$. Its factorization identity comes from
[prop-zla-cohomological-factorization], and the integrality of the
individual $P_i$ from
[prop-zla-parity-identification],
[prop-zla-unique-recovery] and
[prop-zla-factor-integrality], which separate the factors by
weight. The last section prepares the functional equation by computing
the reciprocal characteristic polynomial of the partner of a Frobenius
under a perfect similitude pairing
([thm-zla-degreewise-reciprocal]).

The source is the sketch article
`blueprint/src/version/sketch/49_zeta_linear_algebra.tex`, and only
the statements that are to be formalised in this subtree are reproduced here:
its sections on formal power series at the origin, locally finite products,
periodic permutations, closed points and the Hasse–Weil series, compatible
realizations, the middle pairing and its determinant sign, bounded graded
duality systems, the raw and normalized functional equations,
realization-independent constants and the final arithmetic theorem are
deliberately omitted, as are the derived-category formulation of a trace datum
and the statements about perfect complexes that go with it.

Throughout, $R[[T]]$ is the ring of formal power series over a commutative
ring $R$, identities in it are coefficientwise, and for a commutative
$\mathbf Q$-algebra $R$ we write

$$
\operatorname{Exp}(U)=\sum_{r\geq0}\frac{U^r}{r!}\in1+TR[[T]],
\qquad
\operatorname{Log}(1+V)=\sum_{r\geq1}(-1)^{r+1}\frac{V^r}{r}\in TR[[T]]
$$

for $U,V\in TR[[T]]$; both sums are coefficientwise finite.

The formal proof (`Nagata.schemeImageFlatBaseChange`) does not run
the affine kernel computations of
[lemma-nagata-affine-image-kernel-localization] and
[lemma-nagata-affine-image-kernel-flat]: it factors the base-changed
morphism through $\operatorname{SIm}(g)\times_YY'$ and applies Mathlib's
`IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_isPullback`, which encapsulates
those computations. Only quasi-compactness of $g$ is needed, and
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] is obtained in Lean as the
special case of flat base change along an open immersion, reversing the
order of these two lemmas.

The formal proof (`isProper_blowupMap`) follows this target-local
reduction and settles the affine case
([lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper]) by identifying
$\operatorname{Bl}_I(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with
`Proj.toSpecZero` of the Rees algebra and invoking Mathlib's
properness of $\operatorname{Proj}$ over its degree-zero part, fed by
[prop-nagata-rees-finite-generation]. The projective-embedding chain
([def-nagata-rees-polynomial-map],
[lemma-nagata-rees-polynomial-surjection],
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-projective],
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-projective]) is therefore not formalized.

The formal statement (`extendedToBlowup_isEffectiveCartier`) proves
the effective-Cartier form only, directly from
[lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] and
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]: being effective Cartier is a
local condition, so the gluing step through
[lemma-nagata-chart-generators-associated] and the invertible-sheaf
half ([def-nagata-invertible-ideal],
[lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible],
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-is-effective-cartier]) are not needed
and are not formalized. The Lean theorem also requires no finite-type
hypothesis on the center.

Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$ be a proper morphism.
Then there are an integer $n\geq0$, a proper surjective morphism
$\pi\colon X'\to X$ and a *closed* immersion
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ of $S$-schemes; moreover $\pi$ is an isomorphism
over a dense open subscheme of $X$. In particular every proper $S$-scheme is
dominated by a projective $S$-scheme through a proper surjective morphism.

## Proof

A proper morphism is separated and of finite type, so [thm-chow-lemma]
applies and yields $\pi\colon X'\to X$ and an immersion
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with the stated properties. Both $f$ and $\pi$
are proper, hence so is $f\circ\pi\colon X'\to S$. Since $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$
is separated, 01W6 shows that $i$ is universally closed; in
particular $i(X')\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$ is closed, and an immersion with
closed image is a closed immersion by 01IQ. Thus $f\circ\pi$
is the composition of the closed immersion $i$ with the structure morphism
$\mathbf P^n_S\to S$, so $X'$ is projective over $S$.

Let $X$ be a scheme. If $\mathcal I$ is an invertible ideal on $X$, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The identity of $X$ lifts to the blow-up by the universal property. Compose
this lift with the blow-up map in both orders and use uniqueness.

attrs.title: Blow-up of an effective Cartier center

objects.body:
The constructed $d_{\mathcal I}$ and $d_{\mathcal J}$ are morphisms over
$X$. If both ideals restrict to the unit ideal on an open $U$, the product
blow-up and both maps restrict to the identity over $U$.

## Proof

The maps are composites over $X$ by definition. On $U$, all three ideals
are the unit ideal, so all three blow-ups are identified with $U$ by the
complement theorem. The universal maps are unique over $U$, hence become
the identity under these identifications.

attrs.title: Common refinement by the product ideal

objects.body:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $X$ be a qcqs $S$-scheme, let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense
quasi-compact open subscheme, and let $Y\to S$ be proper and of finite type.
Every $S$-morphism $f\colon U\to Y$ extends to an $S$-morphism
$\widetilde f\colon\widetilde X\to Y$ on some $U$-admissible blow-up
$\widetilde X\to X$.

## Proof

Take $V=U$. By
[lemma-nagata-conrad-morphism-is-quasi-domination], $(U,f)$ is a
quasi-domination of $U$ over $Y$, because a proper morphism is separated.
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] gives a $U$-admissible blow-up
$\widetilde X\to X$ and a quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde f)$ of
$\widetilde X$ over $Y$ extending $f$. Since $Y\to S$ is proper,
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination-proper-target] forces $W$ to be
all of $\widetilde X$.

attrs.title: Extension of a rational map to a proper target, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: flat base change of strict
transforms is not used. The only strict-transform base-change fact the
route needs is the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` over the
preserved open.

Let $f\colon Y\to X$ and let $\mathcal I$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent
ideal on $X$. If $f$ is flat, the strict transform in
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ is all of
$Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$.

## Proof

On every affine blow-up chart the quotient is by the zero ideal, so the
closed immersion in
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-closed-fiber-product] is an isomorphism.

attrs.title: Flat strict transform equals ordinary base change

objects.body:
If $Z(T)\in\mathbf Q[[T]]$ becomes the Taylor series of a normalized rational
germ after coefficientwise extension to a characteristic-zero field $E$, then
$Z(T)\in\mathbf Q(T)_0$: there are $A,B\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ and
$B(T)Z(T)=A(T)$.

## Proof

Apply [thm-zla-hankel-descent] to the extension $\mathbf Q\subseteq E$,
which is an extension of fields because $E$ has characteristic zero.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, put
$K_n=\operatorname{red}_{X,n}(K)$ and define

$$
Rf_!K=
R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n} Rf_{!,n}K_n
\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}).
$$

For $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$, choose an integral lattice
$K_{\mathcal O_E}$ supplied by
Theorem [thm-rational-lattice-localization] and define

$$
Rf_!K_E=(Rf_!K_{\mathcal O_E})\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E
\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y).
$$

The localization theorem makes this independent of the lattice. For a
finite extension $E\subset L$, its
scalar-extension comparison is represented by the finite-level
comparisons over $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$. Passing to the
common finite coefficient stage defines the ambient $\Qlb$-coefficient
functor

$$
Rf_!:D^b_c(X,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Qlb).
$$

attrs.title: Integral, rational, and algebraically closed compact-support functors

objects.body:
For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ and
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
b_i(\mathscr X)=\deg P_i(\mathscr X).
$$

Inside a statement that has fixed $\mathscr X$, write this integer simply
as $b_i$.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ and
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define $P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$ to be the $i$-th
member of the unique tuple supplied by
Proposition [prop-integral-factor-existence]; thus

$$
P_i(\mathscr X)\in\mathbf Z[T],\qquad P_i(\mathscr X)(0)=1.
$$

Let $S$ be a scheme and let $n$ and $m$ be index sets for the homogeneous
coordinates of $\mathbf P^{n}_S$ and $\mathbf P^{m}_S$. The *Segre
embedding* is the morphism of $S$-schemes

$$
s\colon\mathbf P^{n}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{m}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n\times m}_S,
\qquad
\bigl((x_k)_{k\in n},(y_l)_{l\in m}\bigr)
\longmapsto
\bigl[x_k\,y_l\bigr]_{(k,l)\in n\times m} .
$$

In the classical indexing this is
$\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\to\mathbf P^{N}_S$ with
$N=(n_1+1)(n_2+1)-1$; iterating it $m-1$ times embeds an $m$-fold product
into $\mathbf P^{N}_S$ with $N=\prod_{i=1}^m(n_i+1)-1$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. For every
$m\geq1$, the pro-etale sheaf $\mu_{\ell^m,S}$ sends $U\to S$ to

$$
\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times):u^{\ell^m}=1\}.
$$

With transition map $u\mapsto u^\ell$, define

$$
\Zl(1)_S=\varprojlim_m\mu_{\ell^m,S},\qquad
\mathcal O_E(1)_S=\Zl(1)_S\otimes_{\Zl}\mathcal O_E,
$$

and, for every $n\geq1$,

$$
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)(1)_S
=\mathcal O_E(1)_S\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n),
\qquad E(1)_S=\mathcal O_E(1)_S\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.
$$

The $\Qlb$-twist is represented by $E(1)_S$ at any finite coefficient
stage and is compatible with scalar extension. For every displayed
coefficient ring $\Lambda$, set $\Lambda(0)_S=\Lambda_S$, and for
$m\geq1$ put

$$
\Lambda(m)_S=\Lambda(1)_S^{\otimes m},\qquad
\Lambda(-m)_S=
\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_S}(\Lambda(m)_S,\Lambda_S).
$$

For every $t\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D^b_c(S,\Lambda)$, define
$K(t)=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_S}\Lambda(t)_S$. Each $\Lambda(t)_S$ is an
invertible locally constant rank-one sheaf, so twisting preserves
bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ and a prime
$\ell\neq p$ and every pair of integers $i,j$, the
derived tensor product and multiplication
$(\Ql)_X\otimes^L(\Ql)_X\to(\Ql)_X$ define cup products

$$
\smile:H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}H^j(X,\Ql)
\longrightarrow H^{i+j}(X,\Ql).
$$

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case. Let $Y$ be separated and of finite type
over $k$, with structure map
$a_Y:Y\to s=\Spec k$. For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define

$$
\RGamma(Y,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(Ra_{Y*}K),\qquad
\RGammac(Y,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}(Ra_{Y!}K),
$$

and, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$,

$$
H^i(Y,K)=\mathrm H^i\RGamma(Y,K),\qquad
H_c^i(Y,K)=\mathrm H^i\RGammac(Y,K).
$$

Finite-dimensionality and the proper comparison are theorem-level
statements recorded below, not part of this definition.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, let $Y_0$ be of finite type
over $k_0$ with geometric fiber $Y$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For a derived Weil object
$(K,\theta_K)$ with $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, and every
$i\in\mathbf Z$,
define the Frobenius isomorphism
on its $i$-th cohomology sheaf by the composite in the constructible heart

$$
\theta_{\mathcal H^iK}:
Lg_Y^*\mathcal H^i(K)
\xrightarrow{c_i(K)}\mathcal H^i(Lg_Y^*K)
\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^i(\theta_K)}\mathcal H^i(K).
$$

Thus $\mathcal H^i(K)\in\Sh_c(Y,\Lambda)$ carries a specified
object-level Frobenius structure without passing to a derived category of
Frobenius sheaves.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type, let $n\geq1$, let
$c=(j,\bar f)\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$, and set

$$
Rf_{!,n}^{c}=R\bar f_{*,n}\,j_{!,n}:
D\bigl(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr).
$$

Here $R\bar f_{*,n}$ is the K-injective derived direct image and
$j_{!,n}$ is the finite-level exact functor of extension by zero.

attrs.title: Compact-support candidate attached to a compactification

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type, let $n\geq1$, and choose
$c\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$. Define

$$
Rf_{!,n}=Rf_{!,n}^{c}:
D^b_c\bigl(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr),
$$

equipped with the canonical comparison isomorphisms of
Proposition [prop-compactification-coherence]. The cocycle condition
makes this an exact triangulated functor independent of $c$ up to the
specified unique coherent isomorphism.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case. In the Cartesian square of
Definition [def-direct-image-exchange], choose
a compactification $f=p\circ j$,

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y,
$$

and pull it back to
$X'\xrightarrow{j'}\overline X'\xrightarrow{p'}Y'$, with
$\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$. For
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, where $\Lambda$ denotes one of the explicitly
constructed coefficient levels, define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_!(K):Lg^*Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*K
$$

to be the following displayed composite in the ambient category

$$
\begin{cases}
D\bigl(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_{Y'}\bigr),
&\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\\
D\bigl(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y'}\bigr),
&\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,\\
D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},E_{Y'}),&\Lambda=E,\\
D(Y',\Qlb),&\Lambda=\Qlb,
\end{cases}
$$

where the last category is the ambient category of
Definition [def-qbar-ambient-derived-category]:

$$
\begin{aligned}
Lg^*Rf_!K
&\xrightarrow{\sim} Lg^*Rp_*j_!K\\
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_*(j_!K)}
Rp'_*L\bar g^*j_!K\\
&\xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\operatorname{Ex}_{j,\bar g}(K))}
Rp'_*j'_!Lg'^*K
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!Lg'^*K.
\end{aligned}
$$

The middle first arrow is the direct-image exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*$
for the proper map $p$, and the middle second arrow is the open-extension
exchange of Definition [def-open-extension-exchange]. At finite level,
the first and last arrows are the defining compactification identifications.
At the integral, rational, and $\Qlb$ levels they are induced from those
finite identifications by coefficient passage for extension by zero and by
the all-coefficient compact-support construction. Constructible
landing, invertibility, independence of the chosen compactification,
pasting, and coefficient compatibility are asserted only in
Proposition [prop-compact-support-base-change].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type. A
*compactification* $c=(j,\bar f)$ of $f$ is a factorization

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y
$$

with $j$ an open immersion, $\bar f$ proper, and
$\bar f\circ j=f$. A *refinement*
$u:c_1\to c_2$ is a proper $Y$-morphism

$$
u:\overline X_1\longrightarrow\overline X_2
$$

such that $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Compactifications and refinements form a
category $\operatorname{Comp}(f)$.

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
The completed coefficient sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the inverse
limit in sheaves of rings

$$
\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}
=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y.
$$

Write
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$ for the derived
category of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules. Thus the
coefficient in this notation is a ring sheaf, not the discrete ring
$\mathcal O_E$.

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is *constant* if it lies in the
essential image of the constant-sheaf functor
$\mathcal A\to\shv{\et X}$, $M\mapsto M_X$, the left adjoint of global
sections (sheafification of the constant presheaf).

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is *constructible* if there is a
stratification $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ of $X$ such that each
pullback $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant.

A sheaf $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ (with $\mathcal A$ concrete) is
*finite* if for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the underlying
set of the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ is finite.

A sheaf is *finite locally constant* if it is locally constant and
finite.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum] and a scheme $Y$.
For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
D^{\leq0}_c(Y,\Lambda)&=
\{K:\tau^{\geq1}K=0\},\\
D^{\geq0}_c(Y,\Lambda)&=
\{K:\tau^{\leq-1}K=0\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Using the bounded $t$-structure of
Proposition [prop-constructible-t-structure], define its constructible
heart by

$$
\Sh_c(Y,\Lambda)=D^{\leq0}_c(Y,\Lambda)
\cap D^{\geq0}_c(Y,\Lambda).
$$

Its objects are the constructible $\Lambda$-adic sheaves.

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For integers $a\leq b$ and $n\geq1$, let

$$
D_c^{[a,b]}\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)=
\left\{K\in D^b_c\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr):
\mathcal H^r(K)=0\text{ for }r\notin[a,b]\right\}.
$$

A *trivialising datum* for $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ is an étale
cover $(U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ — a jointly surjective family of étale
morphisms — such that for every $i$ the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to
$\et{U_i}$, that is, the sheaf induced by $\mathcal F$ on the site
$\et X$ localised at $U_i$, is constant. The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is
*locally constant* if a trivialising datum exists.

A stratification $(T_l)_{l<m}$ of $T$ *refines* a stratification
$(T_k)_{k<n}$ if every $T_l$ is contained in some $T_k$.

A *stratification* of a topological space $T$ is a finite family
$(T_k)_{k<n}$ of pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets covering $T$
(Stacks Project, Tag `09XZ`, with finiteness added). A
*stratification* of a scheme $X$ is a stratification $(X_k)_{k<n}$ of
its underlying space together with, for each $k$, a scheme $Z_k$ and an
immersion $\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X$ with set-theoretic image $X_k$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum] and a scheme $Y$.
For every $E'\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and every $m\in\mathbf Z$, take the
ordinary constructible truncation functors on $D^b_c(Y,E')$. If an object
of $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ is represented by $(E',K_{E'})$, define its
representative-level candidates
to be

$$
(E',\tau^{\leq m}K_{E'}),\qquad
(E',\tau^{\geq m}K_{E'}).
$$

For every $i\in\mathbf Z$, the corresponding representative-level
cohomology candidate is

$$
\left(E',\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K_{E'}\bigr)[i]\right).
$$

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, a scheme $Y$, and
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. By
Proposition [prop-constructible-truncations], the candidates of
Definition [def-constructible-truncation-candidates] are independent of
the common-stage representative. Define
$\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$
for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ to be the descended functors, and for every
$i\in\mathbf Z$ define

$$
\mathcal H^i(K)=\bigl(\tau^{\geq i}\tau^{\leq i}K\bigr)[i]
\qquad\bigl(K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\bigr).
$$

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
An object
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$ is
*derived complete* if
the canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n
\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}(K)
$$

is an isomorphism, where the reductions are represented by a strict tower as
in Definition [def-strict-reduction-tower].

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For $f:X\to Y$, the direct-image functor on sheaves is left exact. For
every $n\geq1$, its finite-level total right-derived functor is

$$
Rf_{*,n}:
D\bigl(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr),
$$

computed by applying $f_*$ to a K-injective resolution. For a
derived-complete integral complex $K$, define

$$
Rf_*K:=
R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}
Rf_{*,n}\operatorname{red}_{X,n}(K)
\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}).
$$

The limit is derived in the abelian category of all inverse systems. Its
definition does not require the image system already to be a strict
reduction tower. The finite-reduction comparison, and hence strictness on
the constructible subcategory, is a conclusion of
Proposition [prop-direct-image-constructibility] rather than an input to
this definition.
The rational functor is derived direct image of $E_X$-modules to
$E_Y$-modules. Common-stage descent defines the ambient functor

$$
Rf_*:D(X,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Qlb).
$$

Reduction and scalar-extension
comparison maps are stated in Proposition
[prop-direct-image-constructibility]; they are not part of this
definition.

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For every $n\geq1$, the finite-coefficient bifunctor is

$$
R\mathcal Hom_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y}(-,-):
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}}
\times D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr).
$$

A K-injective replacement of the second variable computes this object. For
derived-complete integral $K,L$, define

$$
R\widehat{\mathcal Hom}(K,L):=
R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}
R\mathcal Hom_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y}
\bigl(\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}K,\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}L\bigr).
$$

This derived-complete object is denoted $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ in the
integral constructible category. The rational version is formed over
$E_Y$. Common-stage descent defines the ambient bifunctor

$$
R\mathcal Hom:D(Y,\Qlb)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(Y,\Qlb)
\longrightarrow D(Y,\Qlb),
$$

computed over a finite coefficient field containing both inputs and the
finite diagram under consideration.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For $f:X\to Y$ and $n\geq1$, the canonical identification

$$
f^{-1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y
\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X
$$

shows that no change of coefficient rings is involved. Since inverse image
for the associated morphism of topoi is exact, define the finite-level
pullback by

$$
f_n^*=f^{-1}:
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X\bigr),
$$

applied degreewise to complexes.

For a derived-complete
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$, its
*derived-complete pullback* is

$$
Lf^*K:=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}
f_n^*\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}(K)
\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}).
$$

The reductions are taken in a strict compatible tower; hence the displayed
object is derived complete by construction. This completion is essential:
the uncompleted inverse image of a
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-complex is not used as the integral
pullback. For rational coefficients and
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y)$, define the typed derived pullback by

$$
Lf^*K:=E_X\otimes^L_{f^{-1}E_Y}f^{-1}K.
$$

For $\Qlb$, common-stage descent defines the ambient functor

$$
Lf^*:D(Y,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(X,\Qlb).
$$

Proposition [prop-pullback-constructibility] states
the constructible landing and the reduction comparisons; they are not part
of this definition.

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For every $n\geq1$, the finite-coefficient bifunctor is

$$
-\otimes^L_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y}-:
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr)^2
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr).
$$

If $K,L$ are derived-complete integral objects, define their completed
tensor product by

$$
K\widehat\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}L
:=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}
\bigl(\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}K\otimes^L_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y}
\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}L\bigr).
$$

This completed object, abbreviated $K\otimes^L L$ inside the integral
constructible category, replaces the possibly noncomplete naive tensor
product. The rational bifunctor is the ordinary derived tensor over
$E_Y$. K-flat replacements compute every finite or rational stage.
Common-stage descent defines the ambient bifunctor

$$
-\otimes^L-:D(Y,\Qlb)\times D(Y,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(Y,\Qlb),
$$

computed after moving both objects and their finite diagram to one
coefficient field.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let $Y_0$ be of
finite type over $k_0$, with geometric fiber $Y$, and
let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. A
*derived Weil object* is precisely an object
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ together with a specified isomorphism in that
underlying derived category

$$
\theta_K:Lg_Y^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K.
$$

For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, the finite diagram consisting of $K$, $\theta_K$,
and $\theta_K^{-1}$ is represented after one finite coefficient-field
extension. This definition introduces no new category of objects, no Hom
theory, and no triangulated structure: all objects, arrows, and triangles
remain in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ and
$0\leq i\leq2d$, set

$$
D_i(\mathscr X)=
(-1)^{b_i(\mathscr X)}
[T^{b_i(\mathscr X)}]P_i(\mathscr X)(T)\in\mathbf Z.
$$

Since $b_i(\mathscr X)=\deg P_i(\mathscr X)$, this is a nonzero integer.
Once $\mathscr X$ is fixed, write it simply as $D_i$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
Consider a Cartesian square

$$
\begin{CD}
X' @>{g'}>> X\\
@V{f'}VV @VV{f}V\\
Y' @>{g}>> Y.
\end{CD}
$$

The direct-image exchange transformation

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_*:\;Lg^*Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*
$$

is adjoint to the composite

$$
Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*
\xrightarrow{\ (c^*_{f',g})^{-1}c^*_{g',f}\ }
Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*
\xrightarrow{Lg'^*(\epsilon_f)} Lg'^*,
$$

whose second arrow is the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. For every
$n\geq1$, at finite coefficients its component at
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X)$ has source and
target in
$D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_{Y'})$.
The counit is the one fixed in
Proposition [prop-pullback-direct-image-adjunction]. The integral
transformation uses the derived-complete pullback of
Definition [def-derived-pullback]; the rational and $\Qlb$
transformations are obtained at a common finite coefficient field.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$, define

$$
\chi(\mathscr X)=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i(\mathscr X).
$$

Once $\mathscr X$ is fixed, write this integer simply as $\chi$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let $n\geq1$, let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type, and
choose a compactification
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$. Say that $f$ is
*exceptional-adjoint admissible at
$\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$* if:

1. $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n;c)$ holds for some
integer $c\geq0$, and
$Rf_n^{\times}$ is the ambient right adjoint furnished by
Proposition [prop-ambient-exceptional-adjoint];
1. there is an integer $c_f$ such that, for every pair of integers
$a\leq b$ and
every $L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)$,
$$
Rf_n^{\times}L\in
D_c^{[a-c_f,b]}\bigl(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
$$
;
1. for every
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)$, one has
$$
Rf_n^{\times}L\in
D^b_{ctf}\bigl(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr).
$$
1. for any two compactifications satisfying the preceding conditions,
the mate of the constructible coherence isomorphism in
Proposition [prop-compactification-coherence] identifies the restrictions
of their ambient right adjoints to $D^b_c$, and these identifications
satisfy the cocycle condition.

At the $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\Qlb$ stage, admissibility means that
these hypotheses hold at the finite stages with uniform bounds and that the
finite-reduction and scalar-extension comparisons for the representing
objects are isomorphisms. Admissibility is always an explicit hypothesis;
it is not inferred from separated finite type alone.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type. For every $n\geq1$, at a finite stage at which
$f$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible, set

$$
Rf_n^!=Rf_n^{\times}|_{D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)}:
D^b_c\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
\longrightarrow D^b_c\bigl(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr).
$$

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, at a stage at which $f$ is
admissible, the compatible finite-reduction right adjoints, followed
respectively by derived inverse limit, rationalization, or the common-stage
construction, define

$$
Rf^!:D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^b_c(X,\Lambda).
$$

At finite level, for
$K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)$ and
$L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)$, this right adjoint is
characterized by

$$
\Hom_Y(Rf_{!,n}K,L)\cong\Hom_X(K,Rf_n^!L).
$$

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, every
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, and every $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, the
higher-coefficient right adjoint is characterized by

$$
\Hom_Y(Rf_!K,L)\cong\Hom_X(K,Rf^!L).
$$

Its restriction to finite-Tor objects is part of admissibility. Smooth
purity and Poincare duality for smooth proper structure morphisms are stated
independently below.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case. Assume that $f$ and $f'$ in the
Cartesian square of Definition
[def-direct-image-exchange] are exceptional-adjoint admissible and that
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is invertible. The mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}:Rf'_!Lg'^*\to Lg^*Rf_!$ under
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ and $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ is

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{!}:Lg'^*Rf^!\longrightarrow Rf'^!Lg^*.
$$

Its component at $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ is the unique arrow whose
adjoint is

$$
Rf'_!Lg'^*Rf^!L
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}}
Lg^*Rf_!Rf^!L
\xrightarrow{Lg^*(\epsilon_f)}Lg^*L.
$$

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and a
derived-complete integral complex
$K\in D^b_c(U,\mathcal O_E)$, define the
derived-complete extension

$$
j_!K:=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{\overline X,n}
j_{!,n}\operatorname{red}_{U,n}(K).
$$

For $E$-coefficients the same section formula defines the exact functor
$j_!$, and common-stage descent defines the ambient functor

$$
j_!:D(U,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(\overline X,\Qlb).
$$

Thus $j_{!,n}$ always denotes the finite-level
operation, whereas $j_!$ denotes the integral, rational, or
algebraically closed coefficient operation.

attrs.title: Extension by zero at completed and field coefficients

objects.body:
For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, and let $\mathcal B_E(Y)$ be either the constructible
diagram $\mathcal C_E(Y)$ of Definition [def-qbar-finext-diagram] or
the ambient diagram $\mathcal A_E(Y)$ of
Definition [def-qbar-ambient-finext-diagram], with its specified
transition functors; write $T_{L/E}$, $\eta_E$, and $a_{M,L,E}$ for
the transition functor, unit, and associativity isomorphism of the selected
diagram. An object is a pair $(E,K)$, where
$E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $K\in\mathcal B_E(Y)$. A morphism representative

$$
(M,u):(E,K)\longrightarrow(F,L)
$$

consists of a finite coefficient field $M$ containing $E$ and $F$
and a morphism

$$
u:T_{M/E}K\longrightarrow T_{M/F}L
\quad\text{in }\mathcal B_M(Y).
$$

If $M\subset N$, its transport $u_N$ is

$$
T_{N/E}K\xrightarrow[\sim]{a^{-1}_{N,M,E}}
T_{N/M}T_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{T_{N/M}(u)}
T_{N/M}T_{M/F}L\xrightarrow[\sim]{a_{N,M,F}}T_{N/F}L.
$$

Representatives $(M,u)$ and $(N,v)$ are equivalent when a finite
coefficient field $P\supset M,N$ satisfies $u_P=v_P$. Thus

$$
\Hom((E,K),(F,L))=
\varinjlim_{M\supset E,F}
\Hom_{\mathcal B_M(Y)}(T_{M/E}K,T_{M/F}L),
$$

where the filtered colimit is taken in abelian groups and the displayed
equivalence relation is its representative description.

The identity is represented by the identity at stage $E$, with the unit
isomorphism inserted. Given $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ and
$[N,v]:(F,L)\to(G,Q)$, choose $P\supset M,N$ and define

$$
[N,v]\circ[M,u]=[P,v_P\circ u_P].
$$

Addition is defined by transporting two representatives to one common
stage and adding them there. The zero object is $(\Ql,0)$; a biproduct of
$(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$ is represented over a common $M$ by
$(M,T_{M/E}K\oplus T_{M/F}L)$.

The resulting additive category is denoted

$$
\underset{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}{\operatorname{2-colim}^{\mathrm{pair}}}
\mathcal B_E(Y).
$$

In this lecture the symbol $\operatorname{2-colim}$ denotes this explicit
ordinary common-stage category. It is not an infinity-categorical colimit
and it is not a union of the object sets of the finite-stage categories.

attrs.title: Common-stage pair category and the symbol $2$-colimit

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $n\geq1$,
define

$$
j_{!,n}:D\bigl(U_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_U\bigr)
\longrightarrow
D\bigl(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_{\overline X}\bigr)
$$

by applying $j^{\mathrm{sh}}_{!,n}$ degreewise to complexes. The exactness
asserted in Proposition [prop-finite-extension-by-zero-properties]
ensures that this degreewise construction sends quasi-isomorphisms to
quasi-isomorphisms; the notation $j_{!,n}$ is reserved for this derived
finite-level operation.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For $n\geq1$ and an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, put
$V_U=V\times_{\overline X}U$ for
$V\to\overline X$ in $\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For a sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of $(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_U$-modules, first define the
presheaf

$$
P_{j,!,n}(\mathcal F)(V)=
\left\{s\in\mathcal F(V_U):
\operatorname{Supp}_{V_U}(s)\text{ is closed in }V\right\}.
$$

Here $\operatorname{Supp}_{V_U}(s)$ is the set of geometric points of
$V_U$ at which the germ of $s$ is nonzero, viewed as a subset of
$|V|$. Thus the condition says precisely that the section vanishes on a
neighborhood of the boundary $V\setminus V_U$. Define the heart-level
extension by zero to be its sheafification

$$
j^{\mathrm{sh}}_{!,n}\mathcal F:=aP_{j,!,n}(\mathcal F).
$$

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For $n\geq1$, restriction of scalars along

$$
\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y
$$

is denoted $\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}$. For
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$, its
$n$-th derived reduction is the explicitly typed object

$$
\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}(K):=
K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y
\in D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr).
$$

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For $n\geq1$, an object

$$
K\in D^b_c\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
$$

has *finite Tor amplitude* if there are
integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every sheaf $M$ of
$(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y$-modules placed in degree zero,

$$
\mathcal H^r\!\left(
K\otimes^L_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y}M\right)=0
\qquad\text{for }r\notin[a,b].
$$

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, define finite Tor amplitude to mean that every
finite reduction has finite Tor amplitude in this sense, with one interval
independent of $n$. Write
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ for the resulting full triangulated subcategory.
For field coefficients, define instead

$$
D^b_{ctf}(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,E),
\qquad
D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Qlb)=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb).
$$

For integral coefficients and for
$\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, finite Tor amplitude is an additional condition
and is never inferred merely from bounded constructibility.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$, every prime
$\ell\neq p$, and every $0\leq i\leq2d$, use the cohomological family
of Definition [def-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] and define

$$
P_{i,\ell}(T)=
\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})\in\Ql[T].
$$

Every displayed symbol is a function of $\mathscr X$, even when that
argument is suppressed.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
The coefficient twists of Definition [def-coefficient-twists] on
$\Spec k_0$, pulled back to a geometric fiber, are derived Weil objects in
degree zero. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, their specified isomorphisms make
geometric Frobenius act on $E(m)$ by $q^{-m}$. This formula commutes
with finite reduction and extension to $\Qlb$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let $n\geq1$, and
let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper. Write
$\operatorname{FullCD}(p,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n;c)$ if an integer
$c\geq0$ satisfies

$$
R^qp_*\mathcal F=0\qquad\text{for every integer }q>c
$$

for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of
$(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_{\overline X}$-modules. For every
$U\to Y$ in the small pro-etale site and every integer $q>c$, the same
integer gives $R^q(p_U)_*\mathcal F_U=0$ for every sheaf on
$\overline X\times_YU$.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$, Proposition
[prop-functional-equation-parity] shows that $d\chi(\mathscr X)$ is
even. Define

$$
\varepsilon(\mathscr X)=
(-1)^{\chi(\mathscr X)}q^{-d\chi(\mathscr X)/2}
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i(\mathscr X)^{(-1)^i}
\in\mathbf Q^\times.
$$

Negative exponents denote multiplicative inverses in $\mathbf Q^\times$.
Once $\mathscr X$ is fixed, write this sign candidate simply as
$\varepsilon$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, let $Y_0$ be separated and of
finite type over $k_0$, with geometric fiber $Y$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For a derived Weil object
$(K,\theta_K)$ with $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define the ordinary geometric
Frobenius endomorphism by

$$
\RGamma(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*K)
\xrightarrow{\RGamma(\theta_K)}\RGamma(Y,K),
$$

and define the compactly supported operator from the specified structure on
$Ra_{Y!}K$ of Definition [def-weil-compact-support-object]. Their
actions on cohomology are also denoted $F$.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum]. Let $Y_0/\Fq$ be
of finite type, let $Y=Y_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, and let $(K,\theta_K)$ be a derived Weil
object in $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$. Let $y\in|Y_0|$ be a closed point of degree
$r=[\kappa(y):\Fq]$. Choose an embedding
$\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ and the associated geometric point
$\bar y\to Y$. Compose the Weil isomorphism with its Frobenius pullbacks
$r$ times. The resulting return map at $\bar y$ defines the geometric
Frobenius operator
$F_y$ on every stalk
$\mathcal H^j(K)_{\bar y}$, for $j\in\mathbf Z$; its conjugacy class is
independent of the chosen embedding.

More generally, for every $n\geq1$ and
$x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, the $n$-fold iterate
at the associated geometric point defines $F_x^{(n)}$. Put

$$
\Tr(F_x^{(n)}\mid K_{\bar x})=
\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\Tr\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid
\mathcal H^j(K)_{\bar x}\bigr).
$$

attrs.title: Local Frobenius and local alternating trace

objects.body:
Let $U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion. A
*$U$-admissible blow-up datum* consists of a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with
$\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, a morphism
$\pi\colon X'\to X$, and a specified isomorphism
$X'\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ over $X$. A morphism equipped
with such data is called a $U$-admissible blow-up. The definition records
the ideal and the identification with its blow-up; the equivalent
finite-presentation closed-center formulation is stated separately once
the required ideal/closed-immersion comparison is available.

For an ideal $I\subseteq A$, define

$$
\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)
=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I)).
$$

Its structure morphism is induced by the canonical degree-zero map
$A\to\mathcal R_A(I)_0$.

Define

$$
\chi_a\colon \operatorname{Spec}(A[I/a])\longrightarrow D_+(at)
$$

to be the affine morphism induced contravariantly by $\theta_a$ after the
standard identification of $D_+(at)$ with the spectrum of the degree-zero
homogeneous localization.

Under the data of [def-nagata-rees-polynomial-map], define

$$
e_I\colon\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^r_A
$$

to be the contravariant relative-Proj morphism supplied by
[prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality], induced by $\rho_I$.

attrs.title: Projective-space map of an affine blow-up

objects.body:
Define

$$
r_s\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{IA_s}(\operatorname{Spec}A_s)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)
\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A_s
$$

by applying the relative-Proj morphism of
[prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to $\rho_s$ and the
canonical degree-zero identifications.

Let $U\to S$ be quasi-compact and of finite type and let
$\iota_U\colon U\to\mathbb A^n_S$ be an immersion over $S$, as supplied by
[def-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space] when $U$ is
quasi-affine. Compose $\iota_U$ with the standard open immersion
$\mathbb A^n_S\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_S$ and define

$$
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{aff}}(U/S)
=\mathsf C\bigl(U\longrightarrow\mathbb P^n_S\bigr)
$$

using [def-nagata-immersion-compactification].

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Suppose $S_{\lambda_0}=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{\lambda_0})$,
$S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and fix a finite presentation

$$
B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m).
$$

Select finite-stage lifts of every coefficient of every $r_j$, let
$\lambda_B$ be their selected common upper bound, let
$r_{j,\lambda_B}$ be the lifted polynomials, and define

$$
B_{\lambda_B}
=A_{\lambda_B}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/
(r_{1,\lambda_B},\ldots,r_{m,\lambda_B}).
$$

Define $\beta_B$ to be the comparison from
$B_{\lambda_B}\otimes_{A_{\lambda_B}}A$ to $B$ induced by the presentation.

attrs.title: Finite-stage model of a finitely presented affine algebra

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Start with the finite lists of basic-open elements in $\mathsf G_S$.
Close these lists under the finitely many overlap maps and proposed
inverses, recording the finitely many coefficients occurring when the
images are expressed in the selected localizations. The identity and
cocycle paths in the finite gluing groupoid show that one such finite
closure suffices. For each chart, take the finitely generated
$\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by its resulting finite list. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ to be the selected finite upper bound of all
chartwise coefficient indices, and denote the resulting finite-stage raw
gluing datum by
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}$.

attrs.title: Coefficient stage of an affine gluing presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

For every identity, inverse, open-preservation, and triple-cocycle equation
in $\mathsf G_S$, select a finite stage at which that equation holds on the
chosen generators after localization. Define
$\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$ to be the selected upper bound of
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ and these finitely many witness stages. Let
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ be the pullback of the raw datum to
this stage.

attrs.title: Cocycle-valid stage of an affine gluing presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine cover meeting the
selected generic points is produced in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_iSup_eq_top_and_genericPoints_subset_iInter`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteAffineOpenCoverDenseIInter`.

Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $x\in X$, and let
$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$ be generic points of distinct irreducible
components. Choose one witness from
[lemma-nagata-affine-neighbourhood-generic-points-exists] and denote
its affine open by $A(x;\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)$.

attrs.title: Affine neighbourhood containing selected generic points

objects.body:
For an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring $R$, use the Mathlib scheme
$\operatorname{Proj}(R)$, with its structural morphism to the degree-zero
spectrum. On a homogeneous element $f$ of positive degree, its standard
open is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_{(f),0})$ by
`Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`; a homogeneous family generating the
irrelevant ideal gives the cover through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Fix $\lambda_0\in I$ and a scheme $Y_{\lambda_0}$ equipped with a morphism
to $S_{\lambda_0}$. On the cofinal directed subsystem
$I_{\lambda_0}=\{\lambda\mid\lambda_0\leq\lambda\}$, define

$$
Y_\lambda=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S_\lambda,
\qquad
Y=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S.
$$

The transition morphisms $Y_\mu\to Y_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\leq\mu$ are the canonical base changes of the inverse-system
transitions $S_\mu\to S_\lambda$, and the maps $Y\to Y_\lambda$ are the
projections induced by $S\to S_\lambda$.

attrs.title: Base-changed system over a chosen stage

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

Let $a\in I$. Define $A[I/a]$ to be the $A$-subalgebra of $A_a$
generated by the fractions $x/a$ with $x\in I$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: blow-ups are never
base-changed along a flat morphism. Every base-change step the route takes
goes through the universal property
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
the chart pullback squares
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPullback_blowup$\iota$`
instead.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be flat and let
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal. With
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ defined in
[def-nagata-extended-ideal], define

$$
\operatorname{bc}_g\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)
\longrightarrow
Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

by applying relative Proj to $\beta_g$ on affine opens and gluing. The
degreewise graded equivalence used in this construction is
[lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees].

Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal I,\mathcal J$ be finite-type
quasi-coherent ideals on $X$. Let $X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ be the
scheme obtained by first blowing up $\mathcal I$ and then the extended
ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$ from
[def-nagata-extended-ideal].
The first exceptional ideal is Cartier after the first blow-up. Applying
[lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] on the second blow-up
(chartwise, where the pulled-back local equation remains regular) shows
that its total transform is invertible. This is the special total-transform
input; no assertion about arbitrary images of invertible ideals is used.
On this iterated blow-up, the total transform
of the first exceptional ideal is invertible, and the second exceptional
ideal is invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center].
Hence their product, which is the extension of
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$, is invertible by
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-mul]; define

$$
\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\colon
X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
$$

by the universal-lift construction for their product. On
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)$, factor the invertible
product first through the $\mathcal I$-blow-up. The extension of
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$ is an effective Cartier ideal, so
[lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor] and
[lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible] make the extensions
of both factors invertible. The universal lift for $\mathcal I$, followed
by the universal lift for the extended $\mathcal J$, defines the resulting
map

$$
\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
\longrightarrow X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}.
$$

attrs.title: Comparison maps for the product-ideal blow-up

objects.body:
Define

$$
d_{\mathcal I}\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

as $\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ followed by the first blow-up
projection. Define $d_{\mathcal J}$ symmetrically after interchanging
$\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$.

attrs.title: Domination maps from the product blow-up

objects.body:
Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a
quasi-coherent ideal, and let
$\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ be an invertible ideal together with
a surjection $q\colon f^*\mathcal I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ such that
the composite $\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ after $q$ is the
canonical map whose image is the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ of
[def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Define $\alpha_f$ degreewise by the
tensor powers of this quotient:

$$
\alpha_f\colon
f^*\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n\Bigr)
\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}.
$$

attrs.title: Graded map induced by an invertible quotient

objects.body:
Under the data of
[def-nagata-blowup-universal-graded-map], use the inverse of the canonical isomorphism in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers], apply the
contravariant relative-Proj map induced by $\alpha_f$. Then use the
arbitrary base-change comparison in
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to identify the
resulting target with $Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Here
$\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I))$ is identified with
[def-nagata-global-blowup]: both are obtained by gluing the same affine
Rees-algebra Proj schemes, and the comparison respects the restriction
cocycles. Compose
the resulting map with the second projection
$Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, and
define

$$
\widetilde f\colon Y\longrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)
$$

to be the resulting composite. The affine maps and their gluing data are
part of the relative-Proj interface; no identification of $Y$ with a Proj
is left implicit.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Let $g_\lambda\colon Z_\lambda\to Y_\lambda$ be of finite presentation
between finite-presentation $S_\lambda$-schemes, and assume its base change
to $S$ is a closed immersion. Define $\mu_{\mathrm{cl}}(g)$ by classical
choice from the witness type supplied by
[lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists]. Only the index component
is part of this definition; its eventual property is stated below.

attrs.title: Stage at which a finite-presentation map is closed

objects.body:
Let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow X'$ be closed over $S$ and fix a
compactification $C'=(X'\to\overline X'\to S)$. Define
$\mathsf{Closed}(i,C')$ by taking the scheme-theoretic image
$\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(X\to\overline X')$ and the factorization

$$
X\longrightarrow\overline X\hookrightarrow\overline X'\longrightarrow S.
$$

Let $X=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed with $Y$ qcqs. Let
$A_{X/Y}$ be the directed set of finite type quasi-coherent subideals
$\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I$, ordered by inclusion. Define

$$
X_\alpha=V(\mathcal I_\alpha)\hookrightarrow Y,
$$

and for $\alpha\leq\beta$ define the transition
$X_\beta\hookrightarrow X_\alpha$ from
$\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I_\beta$.

Let $U\hookrightarrow X_i$ be open immersions over $S$, with
$U,X_1,X_2$ separated and of finite type over the qcqs scheme $S$.
Construct the following objects in order.

1. Let
$$
X_{12}=\operatorname{SIm}
\bigl(U\longrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2\bigr)
$$
and write $p_i\colon X_{12}\to X_i$ for the projections.
1. Apply [def-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] to $(p_i,U)$.
Denote the resulting blow-ups by
$X_i^i= X^{\mathrm{el}}(p_i,U)$, their center ideals by
$\mathcal I_i$, and the open strict transforms by
$X_{12}^i\subseteq X_i^i$.
1. On $X_{12}$ define
$$
\mathcal K_{12}
=p_1^{-1}\mathcal I_1\mathcal O_{X_{12}}\,
p_2^{-1}\mathcal I_2\mathcal O_{X_{12}},
\qquad
X'_{12}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_{12}}(X_{12}).
$$
1. The product-center blow-up maps to each $X_{12}^i$. Extend
$X'_{12}\to X_{12}^i$ across the open
$X_{12}^i\subseteq X_i^i$ by
[def-nagata-extended-admissible-blowup]; call the resulting
ambient schemes $X'_i$.
1. Define
$$
\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)=X'_1\amalg_{X'_{12}}X'_2
$$
using the two constructed open immersions of $X'_{12}$.

The construction includes the maps $X'_i\to X_i$, the two open maps
$X'_i\to\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$, and the identified copy of $U$.

*Packaged interface.* What is recorded as data — and what the
formalised structure `CommonModification` carries — is only: the two
$U$-admissible blow-ups $X'_i\to X_i$, the two open immersions
$X'_i\to\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$ together with the fact that they cover
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$, the two lifted copies of $U$ and their agreement in
the glued scheme, and separatedness and finite type of
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)\to S$. The stronger overlap identification of step 5
— that the two opens glue along *exactly* $X'_{12}$ and not merely along
their topological intersection — is an internal step of the construction: it is
used in the proof of [lemma-nagata-common-modification] to obtain
separatedness of the glued scheme, and separatedness is part of the packaged
interface. The downstream consumers
([def-nagata-two-open-final-modification] and
[lemma-nagata-two-open-density-transport]) use only the packaged
interface: density transport needs the two charts to cover and the copies of
$U$ to agree, and the valuative lifting argument needs only separatedness of
$\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)\to S$.

A morphism $f\colon X\to S$ is *compactifiable* if the type of
compactifications of $f$ is nonempty.

Let $f\colon X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. A *compactification*
of $f$ consists of a scheme $\overline X$, morphisms

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S,
$$

and an equality $j;p=f$, such that $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and
$p$ is proper.

Given a compactification $C=(X\to\overline X\to S)$ and $S'\to S$, define
$C_{S'}$ to be

$$
X\times_SS'\longrightarrow\overline X\times_SS'\longrightarrow S'.
$$

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a finite-type
quasi-coherent ideal, put
$X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ with structure map
$b\colon X'\to X$, and let $Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be a
finite-presentation closed immersion. Write
$Z=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow X$. With
$\mathsf{FD}(Z')=(d,\mathcal F)$, define

$$
\mathcal J(Z')=\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^d\subseteq\mathcal O_X,
\qquad
\mathcal K(Z')=\mathcal I\mathcal J(Z'),
\qquad
Y(Z')=V(\mathcal K(Z')).
$$

attrs.title: Center ideal representing a second blow-up

objects.body:
Let $X$, $\mathcal I$, $X'$, $b$, $Z'$, $d$, and $\mathcal J(Z')$ be as in
[def-nagata-composition-center-ideal], and let the second blow-up be
centred at $Z'\hookrightarrow X'$. Let $E$ be the exceptional divisor of
$b$ and let $\mathcal I_E$ be its invertible ideal; write
$\mathcal I_{Z'}$ for the ideal defining $Z'$. Form the explicit ideal
$\mathcal K(Z')=\mathcal I\mathcal J(Z')$ on $X$. The extended ideal on
$X'$ is $\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}$. Define

$$
\Omega_{Z,Z'}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_{Z'}}(X')
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K(Z')}(X)
$$

as the product-blow-up comparison followed by the comparison which removes
the invertible factor $\mathcal I_E^d$. Define the reverse map by the
corresponding universal lifts.

attrs.title: Comparison for a composite of arbitrary blow-ups

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: Deligne's disjointness blow-up
is formalized as the single statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup`,
which absorbs this step.

Consider open immersions $i\colon U\to V$ and $j\colon V\to X$, a morphism
$p\colon Z\to X$, a scheme $Y$ over $U$, and a quasi-compact immersion
$f\colon Y\to Z$ over $X$, so that the square

$$
(Y\xrightarrow{f}Z\xrightarrow{p}X)
\;=\;(Y\to U\xrightarrow{j\circ i}X)
$$

commutes; in particular $Y$ lies over $U$. Write $\overline Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image of $Y$ in $Z$
under $f$. Fix the following data.

1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_1$ on $X$ with
$\overline{V\setminus U}\subseteq V(\mathcal I_1)\subseteq X\setminus U$
as sets, and $T_1=V(\mathcal I_1^2)$, a square-zero thickening of
$V(\mathcal I_1)$.
1. A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_2$ on $X$ whose zero scheme
$T_2=V(\mathcal I_2)$ satisfies $T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$ as
sets.
1. The hypothesis that the closed subscheme
$p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y$ of $Z$ factors through the closed
subscheme $p^{-1}(T_2)$. Loosely: $p(p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y) \subseteq T_2\subseteq T_1\cap(X\setminus V)$, the first inclusion as
schemes and the second as sets.

Let $q\colon X'\to X$ be the blow-up of $X$ along $\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2$
and let $Y',Z',p'$ denote the base changes of $Y,Z,p$ along $q$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: quasi-dominations are not
introduced in Lean. The extension statements are proved directly from
scheme-theoretic dominance and separatedness, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated`.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be $S$-schemes with $Y\to S$ separated. A
*quasi-domination of $X$ over $Y$* is a pair $(U,f)$ consisting of a
dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ and an $S$-morphism $f\colon U\to Y$
whose graph subscheme

$$
\Gamma_f\hookrightarrow U\times_SY
$$

is closed when viewed as a subscheme of $X\times_SY$. If $U'\subseteq X$ is
an open subscheme and $f'\colon U'\to Y$ an $S$-morphism, a
*quasi-domination of $X$ over $Y$ extending $f'$* is a quasi-domination
$(U,f)$ with $U'\subseteq U\subseteq X$ and $f|_{U'}=f'$.

Let $T\subseteq U$ be constructible and closed, with $U$ qcqs. Its
complement $W=U\setminus T$ is a quasi-compact open. Define

$$
\mathcal J_U(T)=\mathcal I_U(W).
$$

attrs.title: Ideal whose support is a constructible closed subset

objects.body:
Under the hypotheses of
[lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists], choose one witness and denote
its finite family and its total intersection by

$$
\mathcal U_X=(U_1,\ldots,U_n),
\qquad D_X=\bigcap_{i=1}^nU_i.
$$

attrs.title: Finite affine cover with selected dense intersection

objects.body:
A compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\to S$ is
*scheme-theoretically dense* when its first map has the predicate
introduced in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]; explicitly,
this means that

$$
\mathcal O_{\overline X}\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_X
$$

is injective.

For a compactification $C=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\to S)$, define
$\mathsf{Dense}(C)$ by replacing $\overline X$ with
$\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ and using $j^{\mathrm{im}}$ as its first map.

Let $h\colon T\to P$ be quasi-compact, assume its image
inclusion $\operatorname{SIm}(h)\hookrightarrow P$ is an isomorphism, assume
$P$ is affine, and let $z\in P$.
Select a witness from
[lemma-nagata-dense-valuation-probe-exists] and denote it by

$$
\mathsf{VP}(h,z)=
(A'_{h,z},K'_{h,z},\eta_{h,z},\alpha_{h,z}),
$$

where $A'_{h,z}$ is the selected valuation ring, $K'_{h,z}$ its fraction
field, $\eta_{h,z}\colon\operatorname{Spec}(K'_{h,z})\to T$ the selected
generic lift, and
$\alpha_{h,z}\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A'_{h,z})\to P$ the selected centred
valuation map.

attrs.title: Valuation probe through a schematically dense source

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by

Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder. Fix a base point $i_\varnothing$
and, for each pair $(i,j)$, fix a selected common upper bound $d(i,j)$
together with proofs $i\leq d(i,j)$ and $j\leq d(i,j)$. Define
$u(F)\in I$ by Finset induction, inserting only an element $i\notin F$:

$$
u(\varnothing)=i_\varnothing,
\qquad
u(F\cup\{i\})=d(u(F),i)\quad(i\notin F).
$$

attrs.title: Selected upper bound of a finite set

objects.body:
A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is an
*effective Cartier ideal* if, on an open cover, it has a generator
which is a non-zero-divisor in the corresponding ring. Invertibility is
a consequence recorded separately below.

Let $q\colon Z\to X$ be separated and of finite type, let $X$ be qcqs, and
let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact. Fix an isomorphism
$e_U\colon q^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ over $U$.
Let $\mathcal F_U(q)$ be the selected flattening ideal of
[def-nagata-flattening-ideal]. Define

$$
X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal F_U(q)}(X),
\qquad
Z^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)=
\operatorname{ST}_{X^{\mathrm{el}}/X}(Z),
$$

together with the strict-transform projection
$q^{\mathrm{el}}\colon Z^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)\to X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)$ and
the transported open identification induced by $e_U$.
Thus $\mathcal F_U(q)$ is a labelled selected object rather than an
unspecified existential variable.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $U,W\subseteq X$ be
quasi-compact opens. Write a given $(U\cap W)$-admissible blow-up of $W$
as $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(W)\to W$. Its center ideal restricts
to the unit ideal on $U\cap W$, so glue $\mathcal J$ on $W$ with the unit
ideal on $U$ to an ideal $\mathcal J^+$ on $U\cup W$ using
[lemma-nagata-glue-finite-type-ideals], and set

$$
\mathcal I_{X}(\mathcal J)
=\operatorname{Ext}_{X,U\cup W}(\mathcal J^+),
$$

and define

$$
\mathsf{ExtBl}_{X,W,U}(\mathcal J)
=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_X(\mathcal J)}(X)\longrightarrow X.
$$

attrs.title: Extension construction for an admissible blow-up

objects.body:
For $f\colon Y\to X$ and a quasi-coherent ideal
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, define
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ to be the image ideal of the composite

$$
f^*\mathcal I\longrightarrow f^*\mathcal O_X
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Y.
$$

$j_{f,\lambda_f}\colon X_{f,\lambda_f}^{\mathrm{fp}} \hookrightarrow\overline X_{f,\lambda_f}$ be its open immersion. Base

map of the resulting factorization to be

factorization to be

=\bigl(X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\hookrightarrow
\overline X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\longrightarrow S\bigr).

X^{\mathrm{desc}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}

X^{\mathrm{desc}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}
\times_{S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}}S

$$
\mathsf{FP}(X/S)=(A_{X/S},(X_\alpha)_\alpha).
$$

Apply [def-nagata-fixed-base-separated-stage] to this system and
define

$$
\alpha^{X/S}_{\mathrm{sep}}
=\alpha_{\mathrm{sep}},
\qquad
X^{\mathrm{fp}}=X_{\alpha^{X/S}_{\mathrm{sep}}},
\qquad
i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S}
=i_{\alpha^{X/S}_{\mathrm{sep}}}\colon X\hookrightarrow X^{\mathrm{fp}}.
$$

Denote the resulting explicit pair by
$\mathsf{Env}_{\mathrm{fp}}(X/S)=(X^{\mathrm{fp}},i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S})$.

For $X\to S$ locally of finite type with $X$ qcqs and $S$ qcqs, form
$i^{\mathrm{imm}}\colon X\to Y^{\mathrm{imm}}$, set
$Y^\circ=Y^{\mathrm{cl}}(i^{\mathrm{imm}})$, and apply
[def-nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system] to
$X\hookrightarrow Y^\circ$. Denote the resulting system by

$$
\mathsf{FP}(X/S)=(A_{X/S},(X_\alpha)_\alpha),
$$

with structural maps $i_\alpha\colon X\to X_\alpha$.

objects.body:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $W\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open, and let
$\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal.
By classical choice from
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension-exists], select a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal on $X$ restricting to $\mathcal J$, and define

$$
\operatorname{Ext}_{X,W}(\mathcal J)\subseteq\mathcal O_X
$$

to be this selected ideal.

g^*(\mathcal I^n)\longrightarrow

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the Raynaud–Gruson flattening
chain is not formalized. Elimination of indeterminacy is obtained instead
by the route of the chapter *Elimination of indeterminacy after Deligne
and Conrad*, whose output is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`.

Under the hypotheses of
[lemma-nagata-flattening-ideal-exists], choose one witness and define
$\mathcal F_U(q)$ to be its ideal component. The accompanying finite-type,
unit-on-$U$, and strict-transform fields are not part of this definition;
they are recorded in the specification lemma below.

Let $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ be the scheme produced by applying
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued` to the valid datum of
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data-valid].

If $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ and $I_V$ represents
$\mathcal I|_V$, define

$$
q_V\colon b_{X,\mathcal I}^{-1}(V)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_{I_V}(\operatorname{Spec}A)
$$

by gluing the affine restriction maps on the basic intersections of $V$
with the chosen affine cover of $X$.

attrs.title: Affine-restriction comparison for the global blow-up

objects.body:
Given two affine covers of $X$, choose their intersection refinement. On
every refined affine chart use the two affine-restriction isomorphisms to
define a comparison, and glue these comparisons after transporting them to
the original charts. The overlap equalities are those of
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-cocycle].
The refinement maps are independent of the selected basic chart by the
overlap cocycle, so the glued comparison is well-defined as a morphism of
the two gluing data.

Fix an affine cover $(V_i)_i$ of $X$. Define
$\mathsf G(X,\mathcal I,(V_i))$ to consist of the local schemes
$\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)$, their inverse images of $V_i\cap V_j$, and
the overlap maps obtained by gluing the maps $\omega_{ij,s}$ on a chosen
basic affine cover of every intersection. The equality on intersections
required to glue these local maps is
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-independent].

Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be quasi-coherent and let
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ be affine. Put
$I_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)\subseteq A$ and define the local model

$$
\mathsf B_V(\mathcal I)=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_V}(V)\longrightarrow V.
$$

attrs.title: Local blow-up model on an affine open

objects.body:
Define

$$
b_{X,\mathcal I}\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\longrightarrow X
$$

by gluing the local structure maps
$\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)\to V_i\to X$. Their overlap equality is
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-local-maps-agree], so the morphism-gluing
interface applies.

If a basic affine open $D(s)$ lies in $V_i\cap V_j$, define

$$
\omega_{ij,s}\colon
\mathsf B_{V_i}(\mathcal I)|_{D(s)}
\longrightarrow
\mathsf B_{V_j}(\mathcal I)|_{D(s)}
$$

as $r_{j,s}\circ r_{i,s}^{-1}$: first use the inverse of the restriction
isomorphism $r_{i,s}$ to move from the first local model to the blow-up of
the localized ideal, and then use $r_{j,s}$ to reach the second local model.
Both restriction maps have the blow-up of the same localized ideal as their
common source.

blow-up is needed, and it is proved directly as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isProper_blowupMap`; the
global blow-up is never exhibited as a projective morphism.

A quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ has a
*finite global free presentation* if there are $r\in\mathbb N$ and
a surjective $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism
$q\colon\mathcal O_X^{r+1}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I$.
Equivalently, $\mathcal I$ is generated by finitely many global sections.
