algebra give compatible maps $S\to S_\lambda$. Define

$$
\kappa_S\colon S\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{\lambda\in I_S}S_\lambda
$$

by the universal property of the inverse limit.

attrs.title: Comparison from the original scheme to the inverse limit

objects.body:
Let $U\to S$ be separated and of finite type, let $V\subseteq U$ be
quasi-compact, and fix a compactification
$V\hookrightarrow Y\to S$. Define

$$
Z_V=\operatorname{SIm}
\bigl(V\xrightarrow{(j,\,\mathrm{incl})}Y\times_SU\bigr).
$$

Apply [def-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] to the first projection
$Z_V\to Y$ over $V$. Denote the resulting blow-up by
$Y^{\mathrm{gr}}\to Y$ and the open strict transform by
$Z_V^{\mathrm{st}}\hookrightarrow Y^{\mathrm{gr}}$. Define

$$
V^{\mathrm{gr}}\subseteq Y^{\mathrm{gr}}
\quad\text{to be the represented open subscheme }Z_V^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
\psi^{\mathrm{gr}}\colon V^{\mathrm{gr}}\longrightarrow U
$$

by transporting the second projection
$Z_V^{\mathrm{st}}\to U$ across the open-immersion identification.

\theta_a\!\left(\frac{xt^n}{(at)^n}\right)=\frac{x}{a^n},

$$

\frac{x}{f^m},\qquad x\in R_{md},\quad m\geq0,
$$

used by the chart statements; it does not introduce a second localization

attrs.title: Quasi-compact open on which an immersion is closed

objects.body:
A quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is
*invertible* if it is locally free of rank one as an
$\mathcal O_X$-module. The inclusion $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$
is part of the ideal data; regularity of a local generator is not included
in this definition.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $q\colon Z\to X$ be proper, let $V\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open, set
$U=q^{-1}(V)$, and let $T\subseteq V$ be closed. Assume $U\to V$ is an
isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of $T$. Let $E\subseteq V$ be
the complement of $\operatorname{IsoOpen}(U\to V)$ from
[def-nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open].
Apply [def-nagata-spectral-constructible-separation] to $(T,E)$ and
denote the output by $(T_c,E_c)$. Perform the explicitly constructed
$V$-admissible separation blow-up

$$
X_1=\mathsf{CSepBl}_V(T_c,E_c).
$$

Let $\overline E_c$ denote the topological closure of the underlying subset
of $E_c$ in $X_1$, and let
$X_0=X_1\setminus\overline E_c$ and let $q_0\colon Z_0\to X_0$ be the
restriction of the strict transform of $q$. Form
$X_0^{\mathrm{el}}(q_0,V\setminus E_c)$ and extend this admissible blow-up
to $X_1$ by [def-nagata-extended-admissible-blowup]. Define
$\mathsf{IsoBl}_{V,T}(q)\to X$ to be the composite of these two
$V$-admissible blow-ups, represented as one blow-up by the composition
construction.

attrs.title: Modification making a proper map an isomorphism near a closure

objects.body:
For a morphism $q\colon Z\to X$, define $\operatorname{IsoOpen}(q)$ to be
the union of all open subschemes $W\subseteq X$ for which
$q^{-1}(W)\to W$ is an isomorphism.

by the route of the chapter *Elimination of indeterminacy after Deligne
and Conrad*, whose output is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`.

For a morphism $f\colon Y\to X$, a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal F$, a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, and its blow-up
$X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, define the pullback center ideal on
$Y\times_XX'$ to be the image of
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'}$ in $\mathcal O_{Y\times_XX'}$. The strict
transform of $\mathcal F$ is its pullback to $Y\times_XX'$ modulo the
subsheaf of sections killed locally by a power of this named ideal.

objects.body:

attrs.title: Stage of equality for two descended morphisms

objects.body:
Let $S$ be Noetherian and let $X\to S$ be separated and of finite type.
Then $X$ is Noetherian, hence qcqs, and the finite generic-point argument
supplies the selected dense affine cover
$\mathcal U_X=(U_1,\ldots,U_n)$ from
[def-nagata-dense-affine-cover]. Define pairs $(\mathsf C_r,h_r)$
recursively along the partial unions of
[def-nagata-partial-affine-unions], where $h_r$ is an explicit proof
that $\mathsf C_r$ is a compactification of $X_r\to S$. Since
$X_0=\emptyset$, the morphism $X_0\to S$ is proper, so set

$$
(\mathsf C_0,h_0)
=\bigl(\emptyset\hookrightarrow\emptyset\to S,
\text{the witness that a proper morphism compactifies itself}\bigr).
$$

Given $(\mathsf C_{r-1},h_{r-1})$, the next stage is $X_r=X_{r-1}\cup U_r$.
If $r>n$ there is nothing to add and $X_r=X_{r-1}$. If $r=1$ then
$X_1=U_1$ is affine and
[prop-nagata-affine-compactification] supplies $(\mathsf C_1,h_1)$.
Otherwise apply [thm-nagata-two-open] to the open cover
$X_r=X_{r-1}\cup U_r$, using $h_{r-1}$, the affine compactification witness
for $U_r$ from [prop-nagata-affine-compactification], and the dense
overlap from [lemma-nagata-partial-union-overlap-dense]. Choose the
resulting candidate and its compactification proof as
$(\mathsf C_r,h_r)$, and finally define

$$
\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)=\mathsf C_n,
\qquad h_{\mathrm{Noeth}}=h_n.
$$

The recursive datum is therefore a dependent finite sequence of pairs, not
an unproved sequence of candidates. At every stage also record that
$X_r\to S$ is separated and of finite type, as follows by restricting the
corresponding properties of $X\to S$ to the open $X_r\subseteq X$; these
are the hypotheses used at the next application of the two-open theorem.

A *Noetherian approximation* of a scheme $S$ consists of a cofiltered
index category $I_S$, a diagram $\lambda\mapsto S_\lambda$ of schemes of
finite type over $\mathbf Z$ whose transition morphisms
$t_{\mu\lambda}\colon S_\mu\to S_\lambda$ are affine, together with a limit
cone over that diagram with vertex $S$, so that

$$
S=\varprojlim_{\lambda\in I_S}S_\lambda .
$$

We write $\mathsf N(S)=(I_S,(S_\lambda)_\lambda, (t_{\mu\lambda})_{\lambda\leq\mu})$ for such a system. Each stage
$S_\lambda$ is then a Noetherian scheme, by the Hilbert basis theorem. The
construction of the following subsection produces such a system for every
quasi-compact quasi-separated $S$, by gluing the affine case
([lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine]) over a finite affine
cover.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Define $S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ to be the scheme obtained by gluing
$\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$. More generally, for every finite
refinement $\lambda$ of the coefficient system satisfying the same finite
equations, define $S_\lambda$ by gluing the corresponding datum.

For $0\leq r\leq n$, define

$$
X_r=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_r,
$$

so that $X_0=\emptyset$ and $X_n=X$.

attrs.title: Partial unions of the selected affine cover

objects.body:
Let $R$ be a ring, let $M$ be an $R$-module, and let $a\in R$. Define

$$
\Gamma_{(a)}(M)
=\{m\in M\mid \text{there is }n\geq0\text{ with }a^nm=0\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal I$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal on a qcqs scheme
$X$, let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n$, let
$X'=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A)$, and let
$Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ be of finite presentation. Select, by classical
choice from the nonempty witness type supplied by
[lemma-nagata-proj-closed-center-finite-degree-exists], a pair
$(d,\mathcal F)$. No property of the selected pair is built into this
definition. Denote it by
$\mathsf{FD}(Z')=(d(Z'),\mathcal F(Z'))$.

attrs.title: Finite-degree data attached to a closed center in Proj

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: only properness of the global
blow-up is needed, and it is proved directly as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isProper_blowupMap`; the
global blow-up is never exhibited as a projective morphism.

A morphism $f\colon Y\to X$ is projective if there exist $r\in\mathbb N$
and a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^r_X$ over $X$ whose
composite with the structural morphism is $f$.

Let $n$ be a finite index set and $S$ a scheme. Put

$$
\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}
=\operatorname{Proj}\bigl(\mathbf Z[T_i:i\in n]\bigr),
\qquad
\mathbf P(n;S)
=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},
$$

where the polynomial ring carries its total-degree grading, and take for the
structural morphism $\mathbf P(n;S)\to S$ the first projection. Here $n$
indexes the *homogeneous* coordinates, so the classical
$\mathbf P^r_S$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,r\};S)$.

This is the same scheme over $S$ as
[def-nagata-relative-projective-space], but obtained without any
gluing, so it does not come with the standard-chart interface required
there; only the properties of $\mathbf P(n;S)$ as a scheme over $S$ are
available from it. In particular it gives no way to construct morphisms
*into* $\mathbf P(n;S)$, which is what
[lemma-nagata-global-blowup-relative-projective-embedding] needs; the
comparison of the two nodes is left to whoever builds relative Proj.

attrs.title: Projective space over a base scheme, by base change

objects.body:
Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open in a qcqs scheme. Choose one
witness supplied by
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] and define
$\mathcal I_Y(W)$ to be its ideal component. Finiteness, quasi-coherence,
and the vanishing-set identity are specification fields, not additional
assertions in this definition.

attrs.title: Finite-type ideal attached to a quasi-compact open

objects.body:

and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so

Fix $\lambda_0$, assume $Y_{\lambda_0}$ is qcqs, and put
$Y=S\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}Y_{\lambda_0}$, and let $W\subseteq Y$ be a
quasi-compact open. Select finitely many affine opens of
$Y_{\lambda_0}$ meeting the image of $W$. On their inverse limits, write
$W$ as a finite union of basic opens $D(f_{ak})$. Choose finite-stage
lifts $f_{ak,\lambda_{ak}}$ and define

$$
\lambda_W=u(\{\lambda_0\}\cup\{\lambda_{ak}\}_{a,k}),
\qquad
W_{\lambda_W}=\bigcup_{a,k}D(f_{ak,\lambda_W})
\subseteq Y_{\lambda_W}.
$$

Quasi-compactness supplies a finite affine cover; on each chart the inverse
limit identifies the coordinate ring with the filtered colimit, so the open
has a finite basic-open presentation. Record those functions and lifts in
the witness before taking the common upper bound.

and its finitely many coefficients. Define

attrs.title: Affine-space immersion attached to a quasi-affine scheme

objects.body:
A morphism of schemes $p\colon Y\to X$ is *quasi-affine* if for every
affine open $X'\subseteq X$ the open subscheme $p^{-1}(X')\subseteq Y$ is a
quasi-affine scheme.

Let $A$ be a ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. The Rees algebra is

$$
\mathcal R_A(I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}I^nt^n\subseteq A[t].
$$

Its underlying ring is the subring of $A[t]$ consisting of polynomials whose
coefficient of $t^n$ belongs to $I^n$.

*Implementation note.* The current Mathlib object is the subalgebra
`reesAlgebra I` of the polynomial ring. The declarations
`mem_reesAlgebra_iff`, `reesAlgebra.monomial_mem`,
`adjoin_monomial_eq_reesAlgebra`, and
`reesAlgebra.fg` provide the membership and finite-generation facts
used below. The grading and the pieces in the next blocks are blueprint
data and must be defined explicitly.

Define

$$
\rho_s\colon A_s\otimes_A\mathcal R_A(I)
\longrightarrow\mathcal R_{A_s}(IA_s)
$$

degreewise by sending a coefficient $x\in I^n$ to $x/1\in(IA_s)^n$.

For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal R_A(I)_n$ be the $A$-submodule of Rees
elements whose underlying polynomial is supported in degree $n$.

attrs.title: Homogeneous piece of the Rees algebra

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and fix generators
$I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$. Define the $A$-algebra map

$$
\rho_I\colon A[T_0,\ldots,T_r]\longrightarrow\mathcal R_A(I)
$$

by $\rho_I(T_i)=f_it$, with each $T_i$ placed in degree one.

attrs.title: Homogeneous polynomial map to the Rees algebra

objects.body:
For a scheme $S$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, define

$$
\mathbb A^n_S=\operatorname{Spec}_S
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n})\bigr).
$$

Concretely, on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ of $S$ this is
$\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n])$; for a principal restriction
$D(a)\subseteq V$ the transition map is induced by
$R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to R_a[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$.

Let $S$ be qcqs and let $X\to S$ be of finite presentation. Select a
finite affine cover of
$S$, finite affine covers of its inverse images in $X$, finite
presentations of all chart algebras over the base chart algebras, finite
basic-open presentations of the overlaps, and the two directions of every
overlap isomorphism. Record these data and their finite identity, inverse,
and cocycle equations as $\mathsf R_X$.

overlaps quasi-compact. Finite presentation supplies finite generators and
relations; record both overlap directions and the finite identity and
cocycle equations as $\mathsf R_X$.

upper bound of their finitely many stages, and denote the resulting raw

$\mathsf R_{X,\lambda_{\mathrm{raw}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}$.

Let $X$ be a scheme and
$\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_X$-algebra. On every affine open $V\subseteq X$, form

$$
\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)).
$$

Quasi-coherence identifies the graded algebra on a basic affine restriction
with coefficientwise localization. The intended relative Proj is the scheme
obtained by gluing these affine Proj schemes along the induced standard-chart
equivalences, with structural map to $X$ glued from the degree-zero maps.
The construction includes the chosen affine cover, all overlap
isomorphisms, their cocycle equalities, and the resulting universal
restriction isomorphisms.

$$
\mathbf P^r_X
=\operatorname{Proj}_X
\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X^{r+1})\bigr),
$$

with the symmetric-algebra generators placed in degree one. Its standard
opens are required to be the relative affine schemes of the degree-zero
homogeneous localizations at those generators. The existence and
compatibility of this object are supplied by
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists].

This node is not formalized: it presupposes relative Proj, which is not
formalized either. Everything that needs only the scheme
$\mathbf P^r_X\to X$, and not its standard charts, uses
[def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] instead.

Let $X\to S$ be a morphism and choose the inverse systems
$\mathsf N(X)$ and $\mathsf N(S)$ together with their comparison maps to
$X$ and $S$. A finite-stage datum for this morphism consists of indices
$\lambda_X$ and $\lambda_S$, a morphism
$\varphi_{\lambda_X,\lambda_S}\colon X_{\lambda_X}\to S_{\lambda_S}$,
and an equality after composing with the two limit projections: the map
$X\to S\to S_{\lambda_S}$ equals
$X\to X_{\lambda_X}\to S_{\lambda_S}$. The datum also records the finite
affine charts and generator-and-relation lists used to construct
$\varphi_{\lambda_X,\lambda_S}$. Finally it records a finite affine cover
of $X$, compatible opens in
$X_{\lambda_X}\times_{S_{\lambda_S}}S$, and chartwise surjections of

$X\to X_{\lambda_X}\times_{S_{\lambda_S}}S$ is an immersion; all overlap
equalities are included in the datum.

Suppose $g$ is supplied with a factorization

c_{g,Z}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\longrightarrow Z

from the containment of the ideal defining $Z$ in the kernel ideal defining

g^{\mathrm{im}}\colon T\longrightarrow\operatorname{SIm}(g)

attrs.title: Canonical factor through a scheme-theoretic image

objects.body:
Let $a\colon T\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated immersion.
Define the scheme-theoretic closure of $T$ in $Y$ to be the closed
subscheme $\operatorname{SIm}(a)\hookrightarrow Y$.

Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a morphism. Define
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)$ to mean the Mathlib scheme-theoretic image
`Scheme.Hom.image g`, with inclusion $g_{\mathrm{im}}$ and factor map

[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. Whenever a later argument needs

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: scheme-theoretic density is
the predicate `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant`,
which [def-nagata-dense-compactification] uses directly.

$U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$ if the sheaf morphism

$$
\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_U
$$

is injective. This predicate is independent of whether the ambient scheme
is presented as part of a compactification.

Under the hypotheses of
[lemma-nagata-separate-closed-data-exists], choose its center

immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$, and define
$\mathsf{SepBl}_U(Z_1,Z_2)\to X$ to be the blow-up of $X$ along the
resulting center $C\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$.

$T_1,T_2\subseteq U$ be disjoint constructible subsets closed in $U$.
Define

$$
\mathcal J_i=\mathcal J_U(T_i),\qquad
\mathcal I_i=\operatorname{Ext}_{X,U}(\mathcal J_i),\qquad
Z_i=V(\mathcal I_i),

\mathsf{CSepBl}_U(T_1,T_2)
=\mathsf{SepBl}_U(Z_1,Z_2).

constructed finite-stage model
$X^{\mathrm{desc}}_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}\to S_{\lambda_{\mathrm{rel}}}$. Choose one witness from
[lemma-nagata-separated-descent-stage-exists] and define

objects.body:

Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Define
its sheaf Rees algebra by

$$
\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n,
$$

with multiplication induced by the canonical multiplication maps
$\mathcal I^m\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal I^n\to \mathcal I^{m+n}$ and unit the degree-zero copy of $\mathcal O_X$.
The direct sum is taken in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Define
multiplication on homogeneous summands by the displayed maps and extend it
by the universal property of the direct sum; the degree-zero inclusion is
the unit. Associativity and the unit laws are exactly
[lemma-nagata-sheaf-ideal-powers-assoc], so this is a graded
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra. The multiplication maps need not be
injective, and no such hypothesis is used.

attrs.title: Map to the blow-up chart of the extended ideal

objects.body:
Let $Z\to X$ be a morphism and let $X'\to X$ be the blow-up of a
finite-presentation center $C\subseteq X$. Put $U=X\setminus C$; then
$U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact. The *strict transform* of $Z$
is the scheme-theoretic closure of

$$
(Z\times_XU)\times_U(X'\times_XU)
$$

in $Z\times_XX'$, in the sense of
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. It is not enough to use only
the topological closure.

supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,

Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, let $I\subseteq A$, and let $a\in I$.
Define

$$
C_a(A,B,I)=B\otimes_A A[I/a].
$$

We regard $a$ as an element of $C_a(A,B,I)$ through the structural map
$A\to C_a(A,B,I)$.

Let $f\colon Y\to X$, let $\mathcal I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal on $X$,
and put $X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. The pullback of
$\mathcal I$ to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ is the
invertible exceptional ideal of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$, so the universal
property of the blow-up ([thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property],
Stacks Tag 0806) provides a unique lift
$\rho\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\to X'$ of the
composite to $X$. Define the *comparison morphism*

$$
\psi_{f,\mathcal I}\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\longrightarrow
Y\times_XX'
$$

with components the structure morphism of
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ and the lift $\rho$.
The morphism $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ is a closed immersion: this is
Zariski-local on $Y\times_XX'$, and over an affine open
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq Y$ lying over an affine open
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq X$ and a standard chart of $X'$ at
$a\in I$, it is the $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the canonical ring map
$B\otimes_AA[I/a]\to B[IB/\varphi(a)]$, which is surjective because a
fraction $y/\varphi(a)^n$ with $y\in I^nB$ is a $B$-linear combination of
fractions $\varphi(z)/\varphi(a)^n$ with $z\in I^n$.

attrs.title: Closed chart model of the global strict transform

objects.body:
For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
Z_i=(U\setminus U_j)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U_i,
\qquad
Z_{i,k}=V_i\times_U Z_k\hookrightarrow V_i
\quad(k=1,2).
$$

Thus $Z_i$ is the canonical reduced closed subscheme on the indicated
complement, and $Z_{i,k}$ carries the scheme-theoretic inverse-image
structure rather than only its underlying closed set.

Define $\mathsf C_{12}(U/S)$ to be the constructed factorization

$$
U\xrightarrow{j_W}W\longrightarrow S.
$$

Define

$$
V_{12}=V_1\times_UV_2.
$$

The separatedness of $U\to S$ gives a closed immersion
$V_{12}\to V_1\times_SV_2$, hence an immersion
$V_{12}\to X_1\times_SX_2$. Define

$$
X_{12}=\operatorname{SIm}
\bigl(V_{12}\longrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2\bigr)
$$

and let $p_i\colon X_{12}\to X_i$ be the restrictions of the two product
projections.

Let $C_i^0$ be the compactification selected by classical choice from the
nonempty type witnessing compactifiability of $U_i\to S$. Define

$$
C_i=\mathsf{Dense}(C_i^0)
=\bigl(U_i\hookrightarrow X_i\longrightarrow S\bigr).
$$

attrs.title: Chosen dense compactifications of the two opens

objects.body:
Apply the common-modification construction to the two open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow W_1$ and $U\hookrightarrow W_2$. Denote its output by

$$
W'_i\longrightarrow W_i,
\qquad
W=\mathsf{CM}(W_1,W_2;U),
$$

with the two constructed open immersions $W'_i\hookrightarrow W$ and their
common open subscheme $U$.

attrs.title: Final common modification for the two-open construction

objects.body:
Apply the graph-extension construction to
$U_i\subseteq U$ and $C_i$. Denote its output by

$$
X_i^{\mathrm{gr}}\longrightarrow X_i,\qquad
U_i\subseteq V_i\subseteq X_i^{\mathrm{gr}},\qquad
\psi_i\colon V_i\longrightarrow U.
$$

From now on replace $X_i$ by $X_i^{\mathrm{gr}}$ and retain the notation
$X_i$ for the resulting proper ambient scheme.

Let $N_2=\operatorname{IsoOpen}(\psi_2)\subseteq U$. Apply
$\mathsf{IsoBl}_{V_1,Z_{1,2}}(p_1)$ to the proper projection
$p_1\colon X_{12}\to X_1$. Define $X_1^{\mathrm{cmp}}$ to be this
constructed blow-up and define $X_{12}^{\mathrm{cmp}}$ to be the strict
transform of $X_{12}$. Transport $V_1$, all four boundary loci, and the
projection maps along the selected isomorphism over $V_1$, and thereafter
retain the notation $X_1,X_{12},p_i$ for the transported data.

For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
X_i^\circ=X_i\setminus\overline Z_{i,j}
$$

and glue the open subschemes $U_i\subseteq U$ and
$U_i\subseteq X_i^\circ$ by the identity. Denote the result by

$$
W_i=U\amalg_{U_i}X_i^\circ.
$$

The construction includes the two open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow W_i$ and $X_i^\circ\hookrightarrow W_i$ and the induced
structural map $W_i\to S$.

For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, define

$$
X_i^{\mathrm{prep}}
=\mathsf{CSepBl}_{V_i}(Z_{i,i},Z_{i,j})
$$

and transport $V_i$, $U_i$, and $\psi_i$ along the chosen isomorphism over
$V_i$. Replace $X_i$ by $X_i^{\mathrm{prep}}$ and let
$\overline Z_{i,k}$ denote the closure of the transported $Z_{i,k}$ in the
new $X_i$.

attrs.title: Prepared ambient schemes with separated boundary closures

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, and let
$K\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, with $n\geq1$ in the finite case. For a
Cartesian square with open vertical maps

$$
\begin{CD}
U' @>{g'}>> U\\
@V{j'}VV @VV{j}V\\
X' @>{g}>> X,
\end{CD}
$$

the Cartesian identity gives
$Lg'^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*Lg^*$. Define the mate

$$
\beta_{j,g}(K):j'_!Lg'^*K\longrightarrow Lg^*j_!K
$$

to be adjoint under $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ to

$$
Lg'^*K\xrightarrow{Lg'^*(\eta_j)}Lg'^*j^*j_!K
\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*Lg^*j_!K,
$$

where $\eta_j:\operatorname{id}\to j^*j_!$ is the inverse of the
restriction isomorphism for extension by zero.

In the coefficient situation and Cartesian square of
Definition [def-open-extension-base-change-mate], define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{j,g}(K):=\beta_{j,g}(K)^{-1}:
Lg^*j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*K.
$$

Thus the exchange is the inverse of the preceding adjunction mate, not an
independent stalkwise notation.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case. For the structure morphism
$a_Y:Y\to s=\Spec k$ and
$K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, define

$$
\smile_{K,L}:\RGamma(Y,K)\otimes^L\RGamma(Y,L)
\longrightarrow\RGamma(Y,K\otimes^LL)
$$

as the arrow corresponding under $La_Y^*\dashv Ra_{Y*}$ to

$$
La_Y^*(Ra_{Y*}K\otimes^LRa_{Y*}L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}La_Y^*Ra_{Y*}K\otimes^LLa_Y^*Ra_{Y*}L
\xrightarrow{\epsilon_K\otimes\epsilon_L}K\otimes^LL.
$$

Apply $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}$ to the resulting arrow on the point. This
is the lax-monoidal ordinary direct-image construction; it does not use
compact support.

Let $K$ be a field, fix an algebraic closure $\overline K$, and let
$P(T)\in K[T]$ have degree $r$ and satisfy $P(0)=1$. An
*ordinary root* of $P$ is an element
$\beta\in\overline K$ satisfying $P(\beta)=0$; it is nonzero because
$P(0)=1$. A *reciprocal root* of $P$ is an element
$\alpha\in\overline K^\times$ satisfying $P(\alpha^{-1})=0$. In
$\overline K[T]$ one has

$$
P(T)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-\alpha_jT),
$$

where the $\alpha_j$, counted with algebraic multiplicity, are the
reciprocal roots.

Let $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ be a smooth-proper datum and let
$\ell\neq p$ be prime. Choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\Ql$.
Applying Theorem
[thm-smooth-proper-structure-admissible] to
the datum $(\ell,\Qlb;\Ql,\Zl,\ell)$ makes
$Ra_X^!$ available at $\Ql$-coefficients. Let

$$
\eta_{X,\ell}:Ra_X^!\Ql\xrightarrow{\sim}\Ql(d)[2d]
$$

be the canonical smooth-purity isomorphism. Separately, geometric
Frobenius acts on $\Ql(-d)$ by $q^d$. Let
$c_{X,\ell}:Ra_{X!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}$ be the canonical proper
comparison. Define $\operatorname{tr}_{X,\ell}$ to be the composite

$$
H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))
\xrightarrow{\,H^0(Ra_{X!}(\eta_{X,\ell}^{-1}))\,}
H^0(Ra_{X!}Ra_X^!\Ql)
\xrightarrow{\,H^0(\epsilon_{a_X})\,}\Ql,
$$

where $\epsilon_{a_X}$ is the exceptional adjunction counit. Define

$$
\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_{X,\ell}:
H^{2d}(X,\Ql)
\xrightarrow{\ H^{2d}(c_{X,\ell})^{-1}\ }
H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
H_c^{2d}(X,\Ql(d))\otimes_{\Ql}\Ql(-d)
\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{tr}_{X,\ell}\otimes1\ }
\Ql(-d).
$$

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$, a prime $\ell\neq p$,
and every integer $0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
\langle x,y\rangle_i=
\operatorname{tr}^{(-d)}_{X,\ell}(x\smile y):
H^i(X,\Ql)\times H^{2d-i}(X,\Ql)
\longrightarrow\Ql(-d).
$$

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and put $s=\Spec k$.
For every $n\geq1$, let
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)$ be the category of
bounded complexes with finite cohomology modules, let
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ be the category of bounded
derived-complete complexes with finitely generated cohomology, and let
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ be the bounded derived category of
finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. For every
$E'\in\mathcal E_\ell$, the canonical equivalence
$D^b_c(s,E')\simeq D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E')$ identifies the constructible
transition functor for $E'\subset L$ with
$K\mapsto K\otimes^L_{E'}L$; derived-tensor associativity supplies its
unit, tower, and shift coherence. Define

$$
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)=
D^b_c(s,\Qlb).
$$

Equivalently, this is the common-stage pair category
$\operatorname{2-colim}^{\mathrm{pair}}_{E'\in\mathcal E_\ell} D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E')$ for the displayed transition datum.

For every finite-type $\Fq$-scheme $Y_0$ and $n\geq1$, put

$$
N_n(Y_0)=\#Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n}).
$$

For a closed point $x\in|Y_0|$, set
$\deg(x)=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$. Define the Hasse–Weil zeta series by

$$
Z(Y_0,T)=
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}N_n(Y_0)\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
\in1+T\mathbf Q[[T]].
$$

The exponential is the formal power-series exponential.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], put
$s=\Spec k$, and let $\bar s\to s$ be its geometric point. For
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case, define the derived-stalk functor

$$
\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}:D^b_c(s,\Lambda)\longrightarrow
\begin{cases}
D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n),
&\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\\
D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E),&\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,\\
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E),&\Lambda=E,\\
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb),&\Lambda=\Qlb,
\end{cases}
\qquad K\longmapsto K_{\bar s}.
$$

The $\Qlb$-valued component is the common-stage form of the finite-stage
stalk equivalences and, under the defining identification
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)=D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$, is the corresponding point
identification.

attrs.title: Derived fiber over the geometric point

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For composable morphisms $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$, define

$$
c^*_{f,h}:L(h\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*Lh^*.
$$

At finite level this is the identity comparison for inverse image; at the
integral level it is induced termwise on finite reductions and then by
$R\varprojlim$; at the rational level it is derived-tensor associativity;
over $\Qlb$ it is represented at one common finite stage.

For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$ and an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$. Apply Definitions [def-filtered-two-colimit] and
[def-qbar-pair-triangulation] to the ambient diagram of
Definition [def-qbar-ambient-finext-diagram], and define

$$
D(Y,\Qlb)=
\underset{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}{\operatorname{2-colim}^{\mathrm{pair}}}
D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y).
$$

Thus an object, morphism, shift, or distinguished triangle in
$D(Y,\Qlb)$ is represented at one finite coefficient field, modulo the
explicit common-stage relation.

For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, and the index category $\mathcal E_\ell$ of
Definition [def-qbar-finext-diagram]. For every
$E\in\mathcal E_\ell$, put

$$
\mathcal A_E(Y)=D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y),
$$

and for $E\subset L$ let
$T^{\mathrm{amb}}_{L/E}=-\otimes^L_{E_Y}L_Y$. Derived-tensor
associativity supplies the unit, tower, and shift isomorphisms and their
coherence equations.

For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, and the
common-stage data of Definitions [def-qbar-finext-diagram]–
[def-qbar-pair-triangulation].
Define the algebraically closed coefficient category directly by the
filtered common-stage construction

$$
D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)=
\underset{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}{\operatorname{2-colim}^{\mathrm{pair}}}
D^b_c(Y,E).
$$

Its shifts, distinguished triangles, and $\Qlb$-scalar multiplication are
those of Definition [def-qbar-pair-triangulation].

For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$ and an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, as in
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
Let $\mathcal E_\ell$ be the poset category whose objects are the finite
extensions $\Ql\subset E\subset\Qlb$, with one arrow $E\to L$ exactly
when $E\subset L$. The compositum of finitely many objects is a common
upper bound, so $\mathcal E_\ell$ is filtered. We use a small skeleton of
this poset in a Grothendieck universe containing the coefficient fields and
the categories below. Put

$$
\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,E),
\qquad
T_{L/E}(K)=K\otimes_E L.
$$

The transition datum includes exact natural isomorphisms

$$
\eta_E:T_{E/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id},
\qquad
a_{M,L,E}:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{M/E}
$$

for $E\subset L\subset M$. The unit equations, the tower pentagon, and
the shift comparisons are part of this datum.

attrs.title: Finite coefficient index and transition diagram

objects.body:
For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, choose
$\mathcal B_E(Y)\in\{\mathcal A_E(Y),\mathcal C_E(Y)\}$, and take the
corresponding common-stage category of
Definition [def-filtered-two-colimit].
Define $(E,K)[1]=(E,K[1])$, with the transition shift isomorphisms used
on morphisms. A triangle in the pair category is distinguished exactly
when it is isomorphic to the image of a distinguished triangle in
$\mathcal B_M(Y)$ for one finite common stage $M$. For a representative
$(M,u)$, a cone triangle means the image of a chosen cone triangle for
$u$ in $\mathcal B_M(Y)$; no functorial choice of cones in a bare
triangulated category is asserted. For $\alpha\in\Qlb$, scalar
multiplication on a morphism is defined after enlarging to a common stage
containing $\alpha$.

For a smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$, every prime
$\ell\neq p$, and
$0\leq i\leq2d$, define

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}}.
$$

Proposition [prop-cohomological-finiteness] supplies the
finite-dimensionality, invertibility, and vanishing outside
$0\leq i\leq2d$; those conclusions are not part of this definition.

A smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X$ consists of a smooth, proper,
geometrically connected $\Fq$-scheme $X_0$, an integer $d\geq0$, an
identification of $d$ with the pure dimension of $X_0$, and the
geometric fiber $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$.

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
A strict reduction tower on $Y$ is a sequence of complexes

$$
C_n\in
C\bigl(\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y)\bigr)
\qquad(n\geq1)
$$

together with actual transition chain maps
$\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n+1}C_{n+1}\to \operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n$ of
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-module complexes. Their composites are
required to agree literally, and the induced derived comparison

$$
(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y
\otimes^L_{(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_Y} C_{n+1}
\xrightarrow{\sim} C_n
$$

is required to be an isomorphism. To derive inverse limit, regard this
system as an object of the abelian category of *all* inverse systems of
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-module complexes and take a K-injective
replacement there. Strict reduction compatibility is a property of the
chosen system; no assertion that strict compatible systems themselves form
an abelian subcategory is being made. This defines
$R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n$ in
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$, characterized
by the functorial Milnor triangle

$$
R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n\longrightarrow
\prod_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n
\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}
\prod_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n
\longrightarrow
\bigl(R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}C_n\bigr)[1].
$$

attrs.title: Strict reduction tower and derived inverse limit

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum], and let
$\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with
$n\geq1$ in the finite case. For an exceptional-adjoint admissible
structure morphism
$a_Y:Y\to\Spec k$, define

$$
\omega_Y:=Ra_Y^!\Lambda\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda),
\qquad
D_YK:=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_Y}(K,\omega_Y)
\qquad\bigl(K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)\bigr).
$$

At finite level $\Lambda_Y=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y$; at integral and
rational level it is $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $E_Y$; the
$\Qlb$-object is represented over a common finite field.

Let $p$ be a prime, let $a\geq1$, and put $q=p^a$. Set

$$
k_0=\Fq,
\qquad
k=\Fbar,
$$

For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$,
write

$$
Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k,
\qquad
a_Y:Y\longrightarrow\Spec k
$$

for its geometric fiber and structure morphism.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type morphism between finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric
fiber $f:X\to Y$.
For a derived Weil object $(K,\theta_K)$ with
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, specialize the compact-support exchange of
Definition [def-compact-support-exchange] to the Cartesian Frobenius
square. Choose a compactification

$$
X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0
$$

of $f_0$, let
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ be its geometric fiber,
and denote the geometric Frobenius of $\overline X$ by
$g_{\overline X}$. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{Rf_!K}:Lg_Y^*Rf_!K
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K)}Rf_!Lg_X^*K\\
&\xrightarrow{Rf_!(\theta_K)}Rf_!K.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}$ is literally the compactification
composite

$$
Lg_Y^*Rp_*j_!K
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p,g_Y}(j_!K)}
Rp_*Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!K
\xrightarrow{Rp_*(\operatorname{Ex}_{j,g_{\overline X}})}
Rp_*j_!Lg_X^*K;
$$

its first arrow is proper base change and its second arrow is
open-extension exchange.

attrs.title: Compact-support image of a derived Weil object

objects.body:
For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
Define $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ to be the full
triangulated subcategory of derived-complete
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$ such that

$$
\operatorname{red}_{Y,n}(K)
\in D^b_c\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
$$

for every $n$, and one interval $[r,s]\subset\mathbf Z$, independent of
$n$, contains the cohomological support of every reduction.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type morphism between finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be its geometric fiber.
The Frobenius square for $f_0$ is Cartesian and the direct-image exchange
of Definition [def-direct-image-exchange] has the specialized form

$$
\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}:Lg_Y^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*Lg_X^*.
$$

For a derived Weil object $(K,\theta_K)$ with
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, define

$$
\theta_{Rf_*K}:Lg_Y^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K)}Rf_*Lg_X^*K
\xrightarrow{Rf_*(\theta_K)}Rf_*K.
$$

attrs.title: Direct image of a derived Weil object

objects.body:
Define $\mathscr A^{\mathrm{intr}}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(X)$ to be the full
subcategory of $\mathcal D(X,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ on those $K$ for which the
intrinsic Koszul completion unit is an isomorphism and the canonical finite
reduction tower is uniformly bounded constructible. This definition has no
K-flat or K-injective package parameter.

Unresolved dependencies: def:weil-a2-derived-category

For $b\geq a$, let

$$
\nu_{b,a,K}:
K_b\otimes^L_{P_b}P_a\longrightarrow K_a
$$

be the derived-tensor associator followed by the multiplication isomorphism
$P_b\otimes^L_{P_b}P_a\simeq P_a$.

attrs.title: Normalization comparison for the canonical reduction tower

objects.body:
*Constructed by:* lemma:weil-pbc-zl-reduction-perfect

Specialize the adic coefficient construction to
$\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $I=(\ell)$, and
$P_a=\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^a$. For $K\in\mathcal D(X,\Lambda)$ set

$$
K_a:=K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_a,
\qquad q_{b,a}:K_b\longrightarrow K_a\quad(b\geq a)
$$

using the quotient map $P_b\to P_a$.

Unresolved dependencies: def:weil-a2-derived-category

attrs.title: Canonical finite reduction tower over $\mathbf Z_\ell$

objects.body:
Let $\Psi(\beta):\epsilon_X^{-1}F\to G$ be the sheaf map induced from the
representative formula by the universal property of sheafification.

attrs.title: Reverse Hom map for the comparison

objects.body:
For $\beta:F\to\epsilon_{X,*}G$, assign to a left-Kan-extension
representative $(W\xrightarrow a\iota_XU,s)$ the section

$$
G(a)(\beta_U(s))\in G(W).
$$

attrs.title: Representative formula for the reverse Hom map

objects.body:
For $A$-module sheaves $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $G$ on
$X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, send
$\alpha:\epsilon_X^{-1}F\to G$ to the map $\Phi(\alpha):F\to\epsilon_{X,*}G$
whose component at $U$ is

$$
s\longmapsto
\alpha_{\iota_XU}\bigl[(1_{\iota_XU},s)\bigr].
$$

attrs.title: Forward Hom map for the comparison

objects.body:
Let $\mathsf{Continuous}(\iota_X)$ mean that the image-sieve operation sends a
covering sieve to a covering sieve and satisfies the displayed pullback
equation.

attrs.title: Continuity predicate for the site inclusion

objects.body:
For an etale object $U\to X$ and a sieve $R\subset h_U$, let
$\iota_{X,!}^{\mathrm{sieve}}R$ be the sieve on $\iota_XU$ generated by the
arrows $\iota_XV\to\iota_XU$ with $V\to U$ in $R$.

attrs.title: Image of an etale sieve in the pro-etale site

objects.body:
For a commutative ring $A$ and $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let

$$
u^R_{X,L}:L\longrightarrow
R\epsilon_{X,*}\mathbf L\epsilon_X^{-1}L
$$

be the derived adjunction unit. Define

$$
c_{X,L}:R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},L)
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathbf L\epsilon_X^{-1}L)
$$

as $R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},u^R_{X,L})$ followed by the canonical identity
$R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},R\epsilon_{X,*}(-)) =R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},-)$. Write $c^n_{X,L}$ for its map on
$n$th cohomology.

Let $\mathsf{GeometricMorphismCert}(\epsilon_X^{-1},\epsilon_{X,*})$ mean
that the Hom correspondence satisfies the adjunction-certificate predicate
and that $\epsilon_X^{-1}$ preserves finite limits.

Let $\mathsf{FunctorLaw}(\iota_X)$ be the conjunction of the identity equation
for every etale object and the composition equation for every composable pair
of etale-site arrows.

attrs.title: Functor-law certificate for the site assignment

objects.body:
Let $\mathsf{AdjunctionCert}(\Phi,\Psi)$ be the conjunction of the left
inverse equation, the right inverse equation, source naturality, and target
naturality for the displayed Hom-map pair.

attrs.title: Adjunction-certificate predicate for the comparison functors

objects.body:
Let $\mathsf{TriangleCert}(\eta^X,\varepsilon^X)$ be the conjunction of the
left-triangle equation and the right-triangle equation.

attrs.title: Triangle-certificate predicate for the comparison adjunction

objects.body:
Let $\mathsf{NaturalUnitCounit}(\eta^X,\varepsilon^X)$ be the conjunction of
unit naturality, counit naturality, the unit restriction equation, and the
counit restriction equation.

attrs.title: Naturality predicate for the comparison unit and counit

objects.body:
Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type morphism between finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric
fiber $f:X\to Y$, and assume
$f$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at $\Lambda$. The Frobenius specialization
of Definition [def-exceptional-pullback-exchange] is

$$
\operatorname{FrEx}_{f}^{!}:Lg_X^*Rf^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Lg_Y^*.
$$

For a derived Weil object $(L,\theta_L)$ with
$L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, define

$$
\theta_{Rf^!L}:Lg_X^*Rf^!L
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{FrEx}_{f}^{!}(L)}Rf^!Lg_Y^*L
\xrightarrow{Rf^!(\theta_L)}Rf^!L.
$$

attrs.title: Exceptional pullback of a derived Weil object

objects.body:
An auxiliary finite coefficient datum is a tuple

$$
(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)
$$

in which $\ell\neq p$ is prime, $\Qlb$ is an algebraic closure of
$\Ql$, $E/\Ql$ is a finite extension inside $\Qlb$,
$\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring, and $\varpi_E$ is a uniformizer.
For every $n\geq1$,
the finite coefficient ring is written in full as
$\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and the transition homomorphism is the quotient
map

$$
\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow
\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n.
$$

For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ as in
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
For every $n\geq1$, a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf
$(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is
*constructible* if $Y$ has a finite partition by constructible locally
closed subschemes on each of which the sheaf is locally constant with finite
$\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$-module stalks. The category

$$
D^b_c\bigl(Y,\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\bigr)
\subset
D\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_Y\bigr)
$$

is the full triangulated subcategory of complexes with finitely many nonzero
cohomology sheaves, all constructible.

The arithmetic Frobenius of $k$ is

$$
\varphi_q:k\longrightarrow k,
\qquad z\longmapsto z^q.
$$

The geometric Frobenius element is
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}$. If
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, the associated semilinear automorphism is

$$
g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\longrightarrow Y.
$$

It is distinct from the absolute $q$-power morphism of the scheme $Y$.
Every Frobenius operator below is induced by $g_Y$ and is geometric.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, let $Y_0$ be of finite type
over $k_0$ with geometric fiber $Y$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For derived Weil objects
$(K,\theta_K)$, $(L,\theta_L)$ with
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, pullback gives

$$
\beta_{\mathcal H om}:Lg_Y^*R\mathcal Hom(K,L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom(Lg_Y^*K,Lg_Y^*L).
$$

Contravariance in the first variable forces the inverse of $\theta_K$.
Define

$$
\theta_{R\mathcal Hom(K,L)}:=
R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_L)\circ\beta_{\mathcal H om}:
Lg_Y^*R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom(K,L).
$$

attrs.title: Internal Hom of derived Weil objects

objects.body:
Fix the prime power $q=p^a$ of Definition
[def-weil-base-field] and let $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ be an algebraic
closure of $\mathbf Q$. For $w\in\mathbf Z$, a nonzero
$\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is a $q$-Weil number of weight
$w$ if

$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{w/2}
$$

for every field embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$.

Specialize A2 to $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $I=(\ell)$, and
$P_n=\Lambda/\ell^n$. For a scheme $Z$ write

$$
\mathsf C(Z):=D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathbf Z_\ell),
\qquad
\mathsf C_n(Z):=D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathbf Z/\ell^n)
$$

for the full subcategories defined, respectively, by
`def:weil-a2-dbc-zl` and `def:weil-a2-dbc-torsion`.

Fix a proper Cartesian square $\square$ as in S10. An A2 constructible
rebinding certificate for $K\in\mathsf C(X)$ consists of the following
displayed data.

1. An A2 proper complete-base-change datum, hence compatible etale-origin
objects
$$
L_n\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf Z/\ell^n),\qquad
\alpha_n:\epsilon_X^{-1}L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n,
$$
including their transition equations. The superscript $b$ is part of
the certificate: one interval $[d_0,d_1]$ works for every $L_n$ and
every $K_n$.
1. On each of $X,X',Y,Y'$, one finite stratification, each stratum having
finitely many connected components, and A2 finite-torsion
constructibility witnesses, uniform in $n$, for every finite object
occurring in S7–S10. On $Y'$ these are, in particular, the four
objects $A_n,B_n,C_n,D_n$ of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-level-map-corners]; their witnesses use one common
interval and one common refinement.
1. The finite exceptional-direct-image values for the identity
compactifications of the proper maps,
$$
Rf_!^{(1,f)}K_n\in\mathsf C_n(Y),\qquad
Rf'_!{}^{(1,f')}E_n\in\mathsf C_n(Y'),
$$
with the A2 torsion witnesses retained by the typed A1 input and with
their transition squares. The certificate records their displayed
identifications with $Rf_*K_n$ and $Rf'_*E_n$.
1. A2 constructible-stratification witnesses for
$$
S(K):=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K,
\qquad
T(K):=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$
in $\mathsf C(Y')$. Their finite reductions are required to be the
objects identified by the maps $\alpha_n$ and $\delta_n$ of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square].

Let $\mathsf C_\square(X)$ be the full subcategory of $\mathsf C(X)$ on
objects for which the type of such certificates is nonempty. Certificates
are membership witnesses only; morphisms in $\mathsf C_\square(X)$ are the
ambient A2 morphisms, so no selected witness enters their equality.

Unresolved dependencies: def:weil-a1-rfshriek-selected, def:weil-a1-torsion-derived-category, def:weil-a2-constructible-stratification-witness, def:weil-a2-dbc-torsion, def:weil-a2-dbc-zl, def:weil-a2-finite-level-etale-origin-realization, def:weil-a2-proper-complete-base-change-datum, def:weil-a2-torsion-constructibility-witness

For a tower $M_\bullet=(M_n,t_{n+1,n})$, put

$$
s((x_n)_n)=(t_{n+1,n}(x_{n+1}))_n,
\qquad
R\varprojlim_nM_n:=\operatorname{Cone}
\left(1-s:\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow\prod_nM_n\right)[-1].
$$

Thus there is a functorial distinguished triangle

$$
R\varprojlim_nM_n\longrightarrow\prod_nM_n
\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow .
$$

Maps of towers act componentwise on the two products and hence on the cone.

Let $g:Y'\to Y$, let $K$ be on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and let $L$ be on
$Y'_{\mathrm{proet}}$. An adic operator and base-change datum consists of
compatible tower endomorphisms

$$
\phi_n:K_n\to K_n,\qquad \psi_n:L_n\to L_n,
$$

and compatible maps $b_n:Lg^*K_n\to L_n$ such that

$$
b_n\,Lg^*(\phi_n)=\psi_n b_n
$$

for every $n$. Compatibility includes the transition squares, the
normalization squares, and their cocycles. This is a datum of ordinary
endomorphisms. A genuine Frobenius or Weil structure has the different type
$\operatorname{Fr}^*K_n\to K_n$ and is not identified with this datum.

Say that the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ attached to $K$ is uniformly
bounded constructible if there are integers $d_0\leq d_1$ and one finite
stratification of $X$, each of whose strata has finitely many connected
components, such that, for every $n$, $H^i(K_n)=0$ outside
$[d_0,d_1]$ and each $H^i(K_n)$ is finite lisse on every stratum. The
normalization isomorphisms and their cocycle are part of this datum.

For schemes and morphisms

$$
\begin{CD}
X' @>{g'}>> X\\
@V{f'}VV       @VV{f}V\\
Y' @>{g}>> Y,
\end{CD}
$$

we write $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ when
$\alpha:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_Y Y'$ is a specified isomorphism and
$f\circ g'=g\circ f'$ as maps to $Y$. The notation
$g'^{-1}F$ always means inverse image using this specified identification.

attrs.title: Cartesian square and chosen pullback identification

objects.body:
For a coefficient ring $A$ and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, a witness
that $K$ comes from the etale site is a pair

$$
(L,\theta),\qquad L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A),\quad
\theta:\epsilon_X^{-1}L\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

including the two inverse equations for $\theta$.

attrs.title: Witness for coming from the etale site

objects.body:
Let $\Lambda$ be Noetherian, let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq\Lambda$ have
$\Lambda/I$ torsion, and suppose every $P_n:=\Lambda/I^n$ is perfect over
$\Lambda$. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ put

$$
K_n:=K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n.
$$

For $b\geq a$, let $q_{b,a}:K_b\to K_a$ be induced by
$P_b\to P_a$. The quotient identities give
$q_{a,a}=1$ and $q_{c,a}=q_{b,a}q_{c,b}$. Associativity also gives the
normalization isomorphisms

$$
K_b\otimes^L_{P_b}P_a\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a,
$$

and these obey the same cocycle.

attrs.title: Adic coefficient datum and reduction tower

objects.body:
Let $K$ be derived complete and let every $K_n$ have a displayed witness
$\epsilon_X^{-1}L_n\simeq K_n$ with
$L_n\in D_c^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda/I^n)$. Define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}:
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

to be the ordered composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K
&\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n Lg^*Rf_*K_n\\
&\xrightarrow{R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}}
R\varprojlim_nRf'_*L(g')^*K_n\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*R\varprojlim_nL(g')^*K_n
=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
\end{aligned}
$$

In the notation above, the first two arrows are $H$ followed by $V'$.
The first isomorphism uses reconstruction and the perfect projection formula;
the second displayed isomorphism is the inverse of direct-image/limit
commutation. This definition fills the map-construction omission in Tag
`09C9`.

Write

$$
S=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K,
\qquad T=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
$$

Let $s:S\xrightarrow{\sim}A_\infty$ be the pullback/tensor comparison in the
first part of the completed construction, and let
$t:D_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be the inverse of direct-image/limit
commutation. Define genuine completed Weil structures by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Theta_S&:=s^{-1}\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(s):
\Phi_{Y'}S\xrightarrow{\sim}S,\\
\Theta_T&:=t\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi_{Y'}(t^{-1}):
\Phi_{Y'}T\xrightarrow{\sim}T.
\end{aligned}
$$

Under these identifications the completed base-change map is the ordered
composite

$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}=tWs,
\qquad W=V'H=H'V.
$$

attrs.title: Weil structures on the completed source and target

objects.body:
For $g:Y'\to Y$ define

$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K:=
R\varprojlim_n\bigl(Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n\bigr).
$$

The comparison from ordinary pullback is the completion map of $Lg^*K$.

Put

$$
S=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*K,
\qquad T=Rf'_*L(g')^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.
$$

Let

$$
\sigma_n:S\otimes^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}A_n
$$

be finite reduction of completed pullback. For $E=L(g')^*K$, let

$$
\tau_n:T\otimes^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n
$$

be the inverse of
$\widehat{Rf'_*E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*\widehat E=T$, tensored with
$P_n$, followed by finite reduction of $\widehat{Rf'_*E}$. Define

$$
\alpha_n=h_n\sigma_n:S\otimes^LP_n\to B_n,
\qquad
\delta_n=h'_n\tau_n:T\otimes^LP_n\to D_n,
$$

and let

$$
\overline\xi_n=
\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}\otimes^L1_{P_n}:
S\otimes^LP_n\longrightarrow T\otimes^LP_n.
$$

Thus every arrow in the completed reduction square is named, typed, and
expressed as an ordered composite of reduction, direct-image, projection-
formula, or base-change maps.

attrs.title: The four edges of the completed reduction square

objects.body:
For $A,B$ on the same ringed pro-etale topos, define

$$
A\widehat\otimes^L_\Lambda B:=
R\varprojlim_n(A\otimes^L_\Lambda B\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n).
$$

Thus $A\widehat\otimes^L\Lambda$ is the derived $I$-completion of $A$.

Define

$$
\operatorname{comp}_K:K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_nK_n
$$

as the map induced by the compatible quotient arrows $K\to K_n$.

For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ choose an injective resolution
$K\xrightarrow{\simeq}I^\bullet$. Apply
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,I^r}$ in every degree and use the naturality
lemma to obtain a morphism of complexes

$$
g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet.
$$

Choose a K-injective replacement
$g'^{-1}I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\simeq}J^\bullet$ in the Grothendieck
category of etale abelian sheaves on $X'$. Compose the displayed map with
$f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet\to f'_*J^\bullet$ and define

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K}:g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\longrightarrow f'_*J^\bullet
$$

to be its class in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}})$. The target complex is a model
for $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$, since $J^\bullet$ is K-injective; the source is a model
for $g^{-1}Rf_*K$ because $g^{-1}$ is exact.
Its class in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}})$ is

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*g'^{-1}K.
$$

For complexes $A,B$, let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^r(A,B)$ be the
degree-$r$ graded maps, with differential $d(h)=d_Bh-(-1)^rh d_A$.
A complex $B$ is K-injective when this Hom complex is acyclic for every
acyclic $A$.

For an identity or a horizontally or vertically pasted Cartesian square, use
one injective resolution and form the degreewise exchange maps by their
unit–pullback-identification–counit formula before selecting targets.

For a bounded-below complex $K$, a presentation consists of an injective
resolution $u:K\to I$, a K-injective complex $J$, a quasi-isomorphism
$q:g'^{-1}I\to J$, and the complex map

$$
E_I:g^{-1}f_*I\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}I
$$

obtained degreewise from the underived exchange. Write
$E_{I,J}:=f'_*q\,E_I$.

For injective resolutions $u:K\to I$ and $u':K\to I'$, a comparison is a
chain map $a:I\to I'$ with $au\simeq u'$.

For two target replacements $q:A\to J$ and $q':A\to J'$ with $J,J'$
K-injective, a comparison is a chain map $c:J\to J'$ together with a
homotopy $cq\simeq q'$.

The continuous left-exact functor $\iota_X$ induces the geometric morphism

$$
\epsilon_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm{et}}.
$$

For every commutative coefficient ring $A$, its inverse- and direct-image
functors have the typed source and target

$$
\epsilon_X^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{et}})
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{proet}}),
\qquad
\epsilon_{X,*}:\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{proet}})
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}).
$$

For $G\in\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$ one has
$(\epsilon_{X,*}G)(U)=G(\iota_XU)$. For
$F\in\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{et}})$, the inverse image is the
pro-etale sheafification of the left Kan extension along $\iota_X^{\mathrm{op}}$;
before sheafification its value at $W\to X$ is

$$
\underset{(W\to\iota_XU)}{\operatorname{colim}}F(U).
$$

Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For an $A$-module
sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, define

$$
\delta_{f,F}:\epsilon_Y^{-1}f_{\mathrm{et},*}F
\longrightarrow f_{\mathrm{proet},*}\epsilon_X^{-1}F
$$

to be adjoint to

$$
f_{\mathrm{et},*}F\xrightarrow{f_{\mathrm{et},*}\eta^X_F}
f_{\mathrm{et},*}\epsilon_{X,*}\epsilon_X^{-1}F
=\epsilon_{Y,*}f_{\mathrm{proet},*}\epsilon_X^{-1}F.
$$

The equality follows by evaluating both restrictions on an etale object of
$Y$. Right deriving this natural transformation and using exactness of
$\epsilon_Y^{-1}$ defines

$$
D_f(L):\epsilon_Y^{-1}Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L
\longrightarrow Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}\epsilon_X^{-1}L
$$

for $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

For a pro-etale object $W\to X$, let $I_W$ be the category whose objects are
factorizations $W\xrightarrow{a}\iota_XU\to X$ with $U\to X$ etale. A
morphism from $(a,U)$ to $(a',U')$ is an etale-site arrow $h:U'\to U$ such
that $a=\iota_X(h)a'$. The transition map on a sheaf $F$ is restriction
$F(U)\to F(U')$.

attrs.title: Etale factorization index for a pro-etale object

objects.body:
Write the unit and counit of the preceding adjunction as

$$
\eta^X:\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{et}})}
\longrightarrow\epsilon_{X,*}\epsilon_X^{-1},
\qquad
\varepsilon^X:\epsilon_X^{-1}\epsilon_{X,*}
\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{proet}})}.
$$

For $F\in\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{et}})$, the component
$\eta^X_{F,U}$ sends $s\in F(U)$ to the class represented by
$(1_{\iota_XU}:\iota_XU\to\iota_XU,s)$. For
$G\in\operatorname{Sh}_A(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$, the component
$\varepsilon^X_{G,W}$ sends a representative
$(W\xrightarrow{a}\iota_XU,s)$ to the restriction $G(a)(s)\in G(W)$.
This map on the Kan-extension presheaf factors uniquely through pro-etale
sheafification.

attrs.title: Unit and counit of the comparison

objects.body:
For a scheme $X$, define the assignment

$$
\iota_X:X_{\mathrm{et}}\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm{proet}}
$$

as follows. An object $p:U\to X$, etale in the A2 small etale category, is
sent to the same structural morphism $p$. It is an object of the A2 small
pro-etale category because an etale morphism is weakly etale. An
$X$-morphism $h:U\to V$ is sent to the same scheme morphism $h$. Thus both
forgetful functors to $\operatorname{Over}(X)$ agree on this assignment.

attrs.title: Etale objects inside the pro-etale site

objects.body:
Consider a Cartesian square

$$
\begin{CD}
U @>{j_X}>> X\\
@V{v}VV @VV{\bar v}V\\
V @>{j_Y}>> Y
\end{CD}
$$

with $j_X,j_Y$ open immersions and $\bar v$ finite. For an abelian sheaf
$G$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, define

$$
\beta_{\bar v,j_Y,G}:(j_Y)_!v_*G\longrightarrow
\bar v_*(j_X)_!G
$$

as the morphism adjoint to

$$
v_*G\xrightarrow{\sim}
j_Y^{-1}\bar v_*(j_X)_!G.
$$

The displayed isomorphism is finite base change
$j_Y^{-1}\bar v_*\cong v_*j_X^{-1}$ followed by
$j_X^{-1}(j_X)_!G\cong G$.

Let $u:T'\to T$ be finite and $F$ an etale sheaf on $T$. For an etale
$V\to T$ and $s\in F(V)$, define

$$
u_V^\sharp(s)\in(u^{-1}F)(V\times_TT')
$$

to be the image of $s$ under the unit from the presheaf inverse image to its
sheafification.

attrs.title: Pullback of a section along a finite morphism

objects.body:
For $E_n=L(g')^*K_n$, define

$$
\vartheta_{E,n}:=
L(g')^*(\vartheta_n)\,\kappa_{g',K_n}:
\Phi_{X'}E_n\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n.
$$

The Weil structures on $B_n$ and $D_n$ are the typed composites

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Theta_{B,n}:\Phi_{Y'}B_n
&\xrightarrow{\kappa_g}Lg^*\Phi_YRf_*K_n
\xrightarrow{Lg^*\beta_{f,n}}Lg^*Rf_*\Phi_XK_n
\xrightarrow{Lg^*Rf_*\vartheta_n}B_n,\\
\Theta_{D,n}:\Phi_{Y'}D_n
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{f',E_n}}Rf'_*\Phi_{X'}E_n
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*\vartheta_{E,n}}D_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

Transport these structures across the two projection-formula isomorphisms:

$$
\Theta_{A,n}:=h_n^{-1}\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(h_n),
\qquad
\Theta_{C,n}:=(h'_n)^{-1}\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(h'_n).
$$

Thus every $\Theta_{Z,n}$ has the genuine Weil type
$\Phi_{Y'}Z_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_n$ for
$Z=A,B,C,D$.

attrs.title: Weil structures on the four finite corners

objects.body:
A Frobenius-equivariant datum for the proper Cartesian square $\square$ and
the tower $K_\bullet$ includes displayed witnesses

$$
\epsilon_X^{-1}L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n,
\qquad L_n\in D_c^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},P_n),
$$

compatible with the tower transitions. Pullback supplies the corresponding
etale-origin witnesses for $E_n=L(g')^*K_n$. The datum then consists of
automorphisms

$$
\operatorname{Fr}_X,\quad \operatorname{Fr}_Y,\quad
\operatorname{Fr}_{X'},\quad \operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}
$$

such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f\operatorname{Fr}_X&=\operatorname{Fr}_Yf,&
g\operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_Yg,\\
g'\operatorname{Fr}_{X'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_Xg',&
f'\operatorname{Fr}_{X'}&=\operatorname{Fr}_{Y'}f'.
\end{aligned}
$$

The four resulting Frobenius faces are equipped with their Cartesian
identifications, and these identifications make the resulting cube commute
with the chosen Cartesian identification for $\square$. Put
$\Phi_Z=L\operatorname{Fr}_Z^*$. Since every $\operatorname{Fr}_Z$ is an
automorphism, every $\Phi_Z$ is an exact equivalence and preserves products
and fibres.

The pullback faces give canonical isomorphisms

$$
\kappa_g:\Phi_{Y'}Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*\Phi_Y,
\qquad
\kappa_{g'}:\Phi_{X'}L(g')^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g')^*\Phi_X.
$$

The proper Frobenius faces give finite-level exchange isomorphisms

$$
\beta_{f,n}:\Phi_YRf_*K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\Phi_XK_n,
\qquad
\beta_{f',M}:\Phi_{Y'}Rf'_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*\Phi_{X'}M.
$$

Finally the datum contains isomorphisms

$$
\vartheta_n:\Phi_XK_n\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n
$$

such that, for $r_{n+1,n}:K_{n+1}\to K_n$,

$$
r_{n+1,n}\vartheta_{n+1}
=\vartheta_n\Phi_X(r_{n+1,n}).
$$

The constant coefficient quotients carry their identity Frobenius
structures, and all displayed comparisons are required to respect their
normalizations and cocycles.

Let $h:W\to V$ be a morphism and let $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ be a
geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. The *geometric fibre* of $h$
over $\bar v$ is the set of morphisms $\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ with
$h\circ\bar w=\bar v$; equivalently, the set of $\Omega$-points of the scheme-theoretic
fibre $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It is finite when $h$ is finite.

attrs.title: Geometric fibre of a finite morphism

objects.body:
Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ have torsion cohomology sheaves and choose
$a$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The canonical truncation tower
$\tau_{\leq q}K$ defines spectral sequences

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K),
$$

and

$$
{E'}_2^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).
$$

Their filtration in total degree $n$ is the image filtration induced by
$\mathcal H^n(Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$; the second
filtration is induced by
$\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K)\to \mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$.

For a proper $f:X\to Y$, define $\mathsf{IA}(f)$ to mean: for every prime
$\ell$, every $g:Y'\to Y$, every square $\square$, and every injective sheaf
$I$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the sheaf
$g'^{-1}I$ is $f'_*$-acyclic, i.e.
$R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for all $q>0$.

Let

$$
Q_m:=K(\Lambda;f_1^m,\ldots,f_r^m)
$$

be the Koszul complex in degrees $[-r,0]$. Its map $Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$ is
the tensor product, over $j$, of the two-term chain maps whose degree-zero
component is the identity and whose degree-minus-one component is
multiplication by $f_j$. Define

$$
K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}:=
R\varprojlim_m(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Q_m).
$$

The augmentations $\Lambda\to Q_m$ give
$\kappa_K:K\to K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}$. Call $K$ intrinsically derived
$I$-complete when $\kappa_K$ is an isomorphism; below, ``derived
$I$-complete'' always means this intrinsic condition.

Let $\xi_K:Lg^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*E$ be the unit–counit exchange map

$$
Lg^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow
Rf'_*L(f')^*Lg^*Rf_*K
\simeq Rf'_*L(g')^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*L(g')^*\epsilon_K}Rf'_*E.
$$

Define the four edges

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_n&:=Lg^*(\pi_{f,K,n}):A_n\longrightarrow B_n,\\
v_n&:=\xi_K\otimes^L1_{P_n}:A_n\longrightarrow C_n,\\
h'_n&:=\pi_{f',E,n}:C_n\longrightarrow D_n,\\
v'_n&:=\xi_{K_n}:B_n\longrightarrow D_n.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $v_n$ use
$Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes P_n)\simeq(Lg^*Rf_*K)\otimes P_n$.
The transported S8 map is $v'_n$, because its construction was identified
there with this unit–counit exchange map.

For the proper Cartesian square $\square$, put $E=L(g')^*K$ and, for every
$n\geq1$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_n&:=Lg^*((Rf_*K)\otimes^LP_n),&
B_n&:=Lg^*Rf_*K_n,\\
C_n&:=(Rf'_*E)\otimes^LP_n,&
D_n&:=Rf'_*E_n,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $E_n=L(g')^*K_n=E\otimes^LP_n$. The chosen Cartesian
identification supplies
$L(g')^*Lf^*=L(f')^*Lg^*$ throughout.

Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point. Define
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ to have objects pairs $(V,\bar v)$ with $V\to S$
etale and $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ above $\bar s$.
A morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is an $S$-map $V\to W$ carrying
$\bar v$ to $\bar w$. We index stalk colimits by
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ so that restriction maps point forward.

Let $f:X\to Y$ admit a chosen compactification

$$
X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y,
\qquad f=pj,
$$

with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper. For this datum set

$$
Rf_!^{(j,p)}E:=Rp_*j_!E.
$$

For proper $f$, its identity compactification is $(j,p)=(1_X,f)$.

For a morphism of ringed topoi $h:\mathcal T\to\mathcal S$, an object
$E\in D(\mathcal T,\Lambda)$, and a strict-perfect package $F^\bullet$ on
$\mathcal S$, define

$$
\pi_{h,E,F}:Rh_*E\otimes^L_\Lambda F^\bullet
\longrightarrow Rh_*(E\otimes^L_\Lambda Lh^*F^\bullet)
$$

to be adjoint to

$$
Lh^*(Rh_*E\otimes^LF^\bullet)
\simeq Lh^*Rh_*E\otimes^LLh^*F^\bullet
\xrightarrow{\epsilon_E\otimes1}
E\otimes^LLh^*F^\bullet.
$$

For $F^r=\Lambda^{N_r}$, let $\rho_r$ be the inverse of the finite-sum
identification

$$
(Rh_*E)^{N_r}\xrightarrow{\pi_r}Rh_*(E^{N_r}).
$$

For a projective term with the displayed splitting, define

$$
\rho_{F^r}:=
(Rh_*E\otimes p_r)\,\rho_r\,
Rh_*(1_E\otimes h^*i_r).
$$

The bounded totalization of the $\rho_{F^r}$ is denoted
$\rho_{h,E,F}$.

For a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$, define $\mathsf{PBC}(f)$ to mean that for
every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every associated Cartesian square $\square$, and
every torsion sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, the map
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism in the derived category.
The assertion includes the specified map of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], not an unnamed isomorphism.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be strictly henselian local, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$,
$s=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S$, and
$X_0=\mathbf P^1_s$. For a sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ write
$F_0$ for its inverse image on $(X_0)_{\mathrm{et}}$.

Let

$$
\mathcal I_{\bar s}:=
(\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s})^{\mathrm{op}}.
$$

For $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, define
$D_{\bar s}:\mathcal I_{\bar s}\to\mathbf{CRing}$ by
$D_{\bar s}(V,\bar v)=A_V$. An arrow
$(W,\bar w)\to(V,\bar v)$ in $\mathcal I_{\bar s}$ represented by a pointed
map $a:(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is sent to
$a^\#:A_W\to A_V$. Put

$$
A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}:=\varinjlim_{\mathcal I_{\bar s}}D_{\bar s},
\qquad
S_{(\bar s)}:=\operatorname{Spec}A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}.
$$

The affine scheme–ring anti-equivalence carries the colimit cocone to the
canonical limit cone

$$
S_{(\bar s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}
\varprojlim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}_{\bar s}}V.
$$

On a localization of a ringed topos, let $Q$ be represented by a bounded
complex $F^\bullet$ of finite projective $\Lambda$-modules. A strict-perfect
package for this representation consists, for every $r$, of an integer
$N_r$ and maps

$$
F^r\xrightarrow{i_r}\Lambda^{N_r}
\xrightarrow{p_r}F^r,\qquad p_ri_r=1.
$$

Write $e_r=i_rp_r$; then $e_r^2=e_r$, $p_re_r=p_r$, and $e_ri_r=i_r$.
Perfectness means that such packages exist after a covering. When
$Q\in D(\Lambda)$ is a perfect coefficient complex, one global package and
its associated constant sheaf may be used.

For every $q\geq a$, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_q&=g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K,&
G_q&=g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal H^q(K)[-q],\\
B_q&=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K,&
H_q&=Rf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q].
\end{aligned}
$$

The canonical truncation triangle and its exchanged image are

$$
\begin{CD}
A_{q-1}@>{i_q}>>A_q@>{j_q}>>G_q@>{k_q}>>A_{q-1}[1]\\
@V{e_{q-1}}VV@V{e_q}VV@V{\bar e_q}VV@VV{e_{q-1}[1]}V\\
B_{q-1}@>{i'_q}>>B_q@>{j'_q}>>H_q@>{k'_q}>>B_{q-1}[1].
\end{CD}
$$

For total degree $n$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_A^{q,n}&=\mathcal H^n(A_q),&
\mathcal E_A^{p,q}&=\mathcal H^{p+q}(G_q)
=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K),\\
D_B^{q,n}&=\mathcal H^n(B_q),&
\mathcal E_B^{p,q}&=\mathcal H^{p+q}(H_q)
=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
\end{aligned}
$$

The exact-couple differential is

$$
d_1=(j_{q-1})_*\circ(k_q)_*:
\mathcal E_A^{p,q}\longrightarrow\mathcal E_A^{p+2,q-1},
$$

and likewise $d'_1=(j'_{q-1})_*(k'_q)_*$. This first
exact-couple page is the page conventionally denoted $E_2$ in the
hypercohomology indexing.

Let $F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. The chosen
Cartesian identification gives a canonical isomorphism of inverse-image
functors

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;g'^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$

Define $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ to be the adjoint of the composite

$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}f_*F
\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}f_*F
\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f}g'^{-1}F.
$$

Thus

$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\longrightarrow
f'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is a globally constructed morphism of sheaves. Naturality, identity, and
pasting are properties of this fixed mate; no family of stalk maps is used to
construct it.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type morphism between finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be its geometric fiber. The identity
$f\circ g_X=g_Y\circ f$ gives

$$
\beta_{f}^{*}:Lg_X^*Lf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*Lg_Y^*.
$$

For a derived Weil object $(K,\theta_K)$ with
$K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, the specified structure on $Lf^*K$ is

$$
\theta_{Lf^*K}:Lg_X^*Lf^*K
\xrightarrow{\beta_f^*}Lf^*Lg_Y^*K
\xrightarrow{Lf^*(\theta_K)}Lf^*K.
$$

objects.body:
For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$ of
Definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-datum].
The rational coefficient ring sheaf and bounded constructible category are
defined intrinsically by

$$
E_Y:=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}[1/\varpi_E],
\qquad
D^b_c(Y,E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y).
$$

The right-hand side is the full subcategory of complexes with bounded
cohomology whose cohomology sheaves are constructible $E_Y$-modules:
after a finite constructible stratification they are locally constant with
finite-dimensional $E$-vector-space stalks. For $E=\Ql$, the integral
ring and uniformizer are $\Zl$ and $\ell$.

If $E\subset L$ is a finite extension, scalar extension is the exact
triangulated functor

$$
-\otimes^L_{E_Y}L_Y:D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,L),
\qquad L_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}[1/\varpi_L].
$$

For a scheme $Y$, choose a small skeleton of the category of weakly etale
morphisms $U\to Y$ in a Grothendieck universe containing $Y$ and all
coefficient rings used below. A morphism is
weakly etale when it is flat and its diagonal is flat. A family
$\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering if every $U_i\to U$ is weakly
etale and, for every affine open $V\subset U$, finitely many affine opens
$V_j\subset U_{i_j}$ have images covering $V$.

For a ring $A$, let $A_Y$ denote the constant sheaf of rings on
$Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and let $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the abelian
category of sheaves of $A_Y$-modules. Its derived category
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is the localization of the category of complexes
at quasi-isomorphisms; it is used only through its ordinary triangulated
structure.

Fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, let $Y_0$ be of finite type
over $k_0$ with geometric fiber $Y$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. For derived Weil objects
$(K,\theta_K)$ and $(L,\theta_L)$ with
$K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$,
monoidality of pullback gives

$$
\beta_{\otimes}:Lg_Y^*(K\otimes^L L)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_Y^*K\otimes^LLg_Y^*L.
$$

Define

$$
\theta_{K\otimes L}:=
(\theta_K\otimes^L\theta_L)\circ\beta_{\otimes}:
Lg_Y^*(K\otimes^LL)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes^LL.
$$
