objects.body:
Continue with the hypotheses above and assume $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$. For
$0\leq i\leq r$ put

$$
R_i(T)=
\begin{cases}
A(T),&i\text{ odd},\\
B(T),&i\text{ even},
\end{cases}
$$

and define the *complete weight-$i$ factor* $P_i^{\mathrm{rec}}(T)$ of
the reduced fraction $A/B$ to be the weight-$i$ stratum of $R_i$ in the sense
of [def-zla-weight-stratum]. By
[prop-zla-weight-stratum-rational] it lies in $\mathbf Q[T]$, satisfies
$P_i^{\mathrm{rec}}(0)=1$, and its reciprocal roots are exactly the
reciprocal roots of $R_i$ that are universally pure of weight $i$, with the
multiplicities they have in $R_i$.

An *eventual recurrence of order $d$* for a sequence
$a\in K^{\mathbf N}$ is a tuple $(c_1,\ldots,c_d;N)$ in
$K^d\times\mathbf N$ satisfying

$$
a_n+c_1a_{n-1}+\cdots+c_da_{n-d}=0
\qquad(n\geq\max\{N,d\}).
$$

Let $a\in\mathbf Z^{\mathbf N}$ have finite-dimensional rational shift span
$W=\operatorname{Sh}_{\mathbf Q}(a)$. Define

$$
M(a)=\sum_{m\geq0}\mathbf Z\,S^ma\subseteq W.
$$

This is a shift-stable torsion-free abelian group with
$M(a)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q=W$.

A polynomial $P(T)\in\Omega[T]$ with $P(0)=1$ is *pure of weight $w$* if
all of its reciprocal roots, counted with multiplicity, are nonzero, algebraic
over $\mathbf Q$, and universally pure of weight $w$ in the sense of
[def-zla-universal-purity].

Let $K$ be a field. A *normalized polynomial fraction* is a pair
$(A,B)\in K[T]^2$ with $B(0)=1$. Two pairs are equivalent when

$$
(A,B)\sim(A',B')
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
AB'=A'B.
$$

The resulting equivalence class is a *normalized rational germ at zero*.
Its rational-function value is $A/B\in K(T)$ and its Taylor series is

$$
\tau_K[A,B]=A(T)B(T)^{-1}\in K[[T]],
$$

the inverse being taken in $K[[T]]$. Write $K(T)_0\subseteq K(T)$ for the
subring of rational functions regular at $T=0$.

For a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space $V$ and
$u\in\operatorname{End}_E(V)$, define

$$
P_{V,u}(T)=\det(1-Tu\mid V)\in E[T].
$$

After scalar extension to an algebraic closure $\Omega/E$, write

$$
P_{V,u}(T)=\prod_{j=1}^{\dim_EV}(1-\alpha_jT).
$$

The multiset $\{\alpha_j\}$, with algebraic multiplicities, is the multiset of
*reciprocal roots* of $P_{V,u}$; it is the eigenvalue multiset of $u$.
If $u$ is invertible then every $\alpha_j\neq0$, $\deg P_{V,u}=\dim_EV$, and
the leading coefficient is
$[T^{\dim V}]P_{V,u}=(-1)^{\dim V}\det(u)$.

Let $P(T)=1+c_1T+\cdots+c_bT^b\in\mathbf Z[T]$ have degree $b$. Its
*reversal* is

$$
P^{\mathrm{rev}}(U)=U^bP(U^{-1})=U^b+c_1U^{b-1}+\cdots+c_b\in\mathbf Z[U].
$$

For a field $\Omega$ containing $\mathbf Q$, a scalar
$\alpha\in\Omega^\times$ is a *reciprocal root* of $P$ if
$P(\alpha^{-1})=0$. The same definitions apply verbatim to a polynomial with
constant coefficient $1$ over any field containing $\mathbf Q$.

For a sequence $a=(a_n)_{n\geq0}\in K^{\mathbf N}$, define the left shift $Sa$
by $(Sa)_n=a_{n+1}$, and put

$$
\operatorname{Sh}_K(a)=\Span_K\{S^ma:m\geq0\}\subseteq K^{\mathbf N}.
$$

The associated Hankel matrix is $H(a)=(a_{r+s})_{r,s\geq0}$; its columns are
the shifts of $a$. It has rank at most $h$ if every $(h+1)\times(h+1)$ minor
$\det(a_{r_x+s_y})_{0\leq x,y\leq h}$ vanishes, for all choices of nonnegative
indices $r_x,s_y$.

Let $E$ be a field and let $V,W$ be finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. A
bilinear pairing $B:V\times W\to E$ is *perfect* if the adjoint map

$$
\phi_B:W\longrightarrow V^\vee,
\qquad
\phi_B(w)(v)=B(v,w),
$$

is an isomorphism. Given automorphisms $F_V\in\operatorname{Aut}_E(V)$,
$F_W\in\operatorname{Aut}_E(W)$ and a scalar $\mu\in E^\times$, the pairing is
a *similitude pairing of multiplier $\mu$* if

$$
B(F_Vv,F_Ww)=\mu B(v,w)
\qquad(v\in V,\ w\in W).
$$

Let $E$ be a field of characteristic zero. A *finite cohomological trace
datum* over $E$ consists of:

1. an integer $r\geq0$ and, for each $0\leq i\leq r$, a finite-dimensional
$E$-vector space $V_i$ together with an endomorphism
$F_i\in\operatorname{End}_E(V_i)$;
1. integers $N_n\in\mathbf Z$ for every $n\geq1$;
1. the equalities
$$
N_n=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)
\qquad\text{in }E,\qquad(n\geq1),
$$
the left-hand side being the image of $N_n$ under
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q\to E$.

Put $P_i(T)=\det(1-TF_i\mid V_i)$. In the intended application $V_i$ is the
$i$-th cohomology group of a perfect complex and $F_i$ is induced by a
Frobenius automorphism, but nothing below uses a complex: only the finite
family $(V_i,F_i)_{0\leq i\leq r}$ and the trace equalities enter.

A nonzero algebraic number $\alpha\in\Qbar\subseteq\mathbf C$ is
*universally pure of weight $w\in\mathbf R$* if every complex root of the
minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbf Q$ has absolute value $q^{w/2}$;
equivalently, $|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{w/2}$ for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, these embeddings being the
complex roots of that minimal polynomial. The condition is read off the
minimal polynomial alone, so it applies verbatim to a nonzero element of any
field of characteristic zero that is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$.

Let $R\in\mathbf Q[T]$ satisfy $R(0)=1$. Since $R(0)\neq0$, no irreducible
factor of $R$ is a scalar multiple of $T$, so $R$ has a factorization

$$
R=\prod_{j}F_j^{m_j},
\qquad
F_j\in\mathbf Q[T]\text{ irreducible},\quad F_j(0)=1,
$$

with the $F_j$ pairwise distinct and $m_j\geq1$, and this normalized
irreducible factorization is unique. For a real number $w$, the
*weight-$w$ stratum* of $R$ is

$$
R_w(T)=\prod_{j\in J_w}F_j(T)^{m_j},
\qquad
J_w=\{j:|z|=q^{-w/2}\text{ for every complex root }z\text{ of }F_j\},
$$

the product of those normalized irreducible rational factors of $R$ all of
whose complex roots have absolute value $q^{-w/2}$, taken with the
multiplicities they have in $R$.

objects.body:
This chapter is the formalized route to
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] (Stacks Tag 081S), the single
primitive obligation of the modification layer. It follows Deligne's notes as
written up by Conrad
[ConradNagata]: two blow-up lemmas of Deligne
(*Lemme* 0.2 and *Lemme* 0.3, which are Lemmas 1.4 and 1.5 of
*loc. cit.*), and then Conrad's Theorem 2.4 (Deligne's
*Théorème* 1.2, Nagata's Theorem 3.2): a rational map to a separated
finite-type target becomes defined, in the precise sense of a quasi-domination,
after a single admissible blow-up of the source. The proof is a chain of four
special cases, the last of which uses Zariski's Main Theorem to replace an
arbitrary target by a quasi-affine one.

The route written in the previous chapter — Raynaud–Gruson flattening by
blow-up (Stacks Tags 0815, 081R, 081P, 081L) — is not the formalized one;
see the remark after [lemma-nagata-module-strict-transform-exact] and the
route remark closing this chapter. This chapter is formalized: most statements
below carry a non-empty `\lean` field naming the declaration that realizes
them, up to Conrad's Theorem 2.4 itself
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_extend_partialSection`) and its
$U=V$ corollary.

Throughout, $S$ is a quasi-compact and quasi-separated base scheme and all
fibre products of $S$-schemes are taken over $S$ unless another base is
displayed. We freely use the affine blow-up charts of
[def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]: for an ideal $I\subseteq A$ and $s\in I$
we write

$$
U(s)=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[I/s]\bigr)
\subseteq\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A),
$$

the open locus on which the extended ideal $I\cdot\mathcal O$ is invertible
with global basis $s$; by
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] these charts, taken over a
generating set of $I$, cover the blow-up.

the output of a previously defined construction; no new existential choice is
made inside the final theorem.

(`nagataCompactification_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`) asserts the

morphism of finite presentation over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base,
rather than for the finite-presentation envelope $X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\to S$

([def-nagata-final-descended-model],

[def-nagata-final-basechanged-compactification] and their spec lemmas)
are collapsed into its proof and are not separately formalized.

Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with finitely many
irreducible components $Z_1,\dots,Z_r$, with generic points $\eta_j$. Then
there is a finite affine open covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ such that
$\eta_j\in U_i$ for all $i$ and $j$. For any such covering the open

$$
U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m
$$

is dense in $X$.

## Proof

By [lem-chow-affine-through-generic-points] every $x\in X$ has an affine
open neighbourhood containing all the $\eta_j$; since $X$ is quasi-compact,
finitely many of them cover $X$. For the density statement note that
$U\cap Z_j$ is an open subset of $Z_j$ containing $\eta_j$, hence is dense in
the irreducible space $Z_j$; as $X=Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_r$, the closure of $U$
contains every $Z_j$ and therefore equals $X$.

attrs.title: Affine cover through the generic points

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $V$ be an affine scheme equipped with a morphism
$g\colon V\to S$ that is locally of finite type. Then there are a finite index
set $n$ and an immersion $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with
$j$ followed by $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ equal to $g$. Here the homogeneous
coordinates $T_i$ of $\mathbf P^n_S$ are indexed by the finite set $n$.

## Proof

Write $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, so that $V=\Spec B$. We give an elementary
construction; it does not use ample invertible sheaves.

*Step 1: a cover adapted to $g$.* Every point of $V$ has a basic open
neighbourhood $D(b)$ with $g(D(b))$ contained in an affine open of $S$: pick an
affine open $W\subseteq S$ around the image point and then a basic open of $V$
inside $g^{-1}(W)$. Since $V$ is quasi-compact, finitely many of these cover
$V$: there are a finite set $\Lambda$, sections $b_\lambda\in B$ and affine
opens $W_\lambda\subseteq S$ with $D(b_\lambda)\subseteq g^{-1}(W_\lambda)$ and
$V=\bigcup_{\lambda}D(b_\lambda)$.

*Step 2: generators with a common denominator.* Fix $\lambda$ and put
$A_\lambda=\Gamma(W_\lambda,\mathcal O_S)$. The induced morphism
$D(b_\lambda)\to W_\lambda$ is a morphism of affine schemes that is locally of
finite type, so $B_{b_\lambda}=\Gamma(D(b_\lambda),\mathcal O_V)$ is a finitely
generated $A_\lambda$-algebra. Clearing denominators, we may choose the
generators of the shape $c_\mu/b_\lambda^{N}$ with $c_\mu\in B$ and a single
exponent $N$, indexed by a finite set $M_\lambda$. Put

$$
t_{\lambda,\ast}=1,\qquad t_{\lambda,\mu}=c_\mu b_\lambda
\quad(\mu\in M_\lambda),
$$

a family indexed by the finite set $M_\lambda^{+}=M_\lambda\sqcup\{\ast\}$.
In $B_{b_\lambda}$ we have $t_{\lambda,\ast}/b_\lambda=1/b_\lambda$ and
$t_{\lambda,\mu}/b_\lambda=c_\mu$, hence
$c_\mu/b_\lambda^{N}=(1/b_\lambda)^{N}\cdot c_\mu$ lies in the subring
generated by $A_\lambda$ and the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$.
Therefore $B_{b_\lambda}$ is generated as a ring by the image of $A_\lambda$
together with the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$.

*Step 3: the morphism.* Let
$n=\Lambda\sqcup\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}M_\lambda^{+}$, a finite set, and
let $s\colon n\to B$ be the family given by $s_\lambda=b_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $s_{(\lambda,\mu)}=t_{\lambda,\mu}$. The
$D(b_\lambda)$ cover $V$, so the $s_i$ generate the unit ideal of $B$, and
therefore they define a morphism $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ over $S$ with
$j^{-1}\bigl(D_+(T_i)\bigr)=D(s_i)$.

*Step 4: $j$ is an immersion.* The opens $D_+(T_{\lambda})$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ have preimages $D(b_\lambda)$, which cover $V$; hence the
image of $j$ is contained in $U=\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}D_+(T_\lambda)$.
Being an immersion is local on the target, so it suffices to show that the
restriction of $j$ over each $D_+(T_\lambda)$ is an immersion. On the standard
chart $D_+(T_\lambda)\cong\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S$ this
restriction is the morphism

$$
D(b_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S,
\qquad Y_i\longmapsto s_i/b_\lambda .
$$

Since $D(b_\lambda)\subseteq g^{-1}(W_\lambda)$, it factors through the open
subscheme $\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}$, and the resulting
morphism
$D(b_\lambda)\to\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda} =\Spec A_\lambda[Y_i]$ is $\Spec$ of the $A_\lambda$-algebra map
$Y_i\mapsto s_i/b_\lambda$. That map is surjective by Step 2, because its
image already contains the quotients $t_{\lambda,\bullet}/b_\lambda$. Hence
$D(b_\lambda)\to\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}$ is a closed
immersion, and composing with the open immersion
$\mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_{W_\lambda}\to \mathbf A^{\,n\setminus\{\lambda\}}_S$ shows that the restriction of $j$ over
$D_+(T_\lambda)$ is an immersion.

attrs.title: An affine scheme of finite type immerses into projective space

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$ with generic points $\eta_i$, and let $x\in X$.
Then there is an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and all the
$\eta_i$.

## Proof

After renumbering we may assume $x\in Z_i$ for $i\leq r$ and $x\notin Z_k$ for
$k>r$. Then $\bigcap_{k>r}(X\setminus Z_k)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$,
so there is an affine open $W$ with
$x\in W\subseteq\bigcap_{k>r}(X\setminus Z_k)$; thus $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$ for
$k>r$. For $i\leq r$ the set $W\cap Z_i$ is a nonempty open subset of the
irreducible space $Z_i$, hence contains its generic point, so $\eta_i\in W$.

By [lem-chow-disjoint-affines] applied to $Z_{r+1},\dots,Z_n$ there are
pairwise disjoint affine opens $U_k\ni\eta_k$ for $k>r$. Fix $k>r$. Since $X$
is quasi-separated, $W\cap U_k$ is a quasi-compact open of $U_k$, and it does
not contain $\eta_k$ because $\eta_k\in Z_k$ while $W\cap Z_k=\emptyset$. As
in the proof of [lem-chow-disjoint-affines], $\eta_k$ is a minimal prime
of the affine scheme $U_k$, so 00EV provides a standard affine
open $U_k'\subseteq U_k$ with $\eta_k\in U_k'$ and $U_k'\cap W=\emptyset$.

The opens $W$ and $U_k'$ for $k>r$ are pairwise disjoint and affine, so

$$
U:=W\cup\bigcup_{k>r}U_k'
$$

is affine by 01I5, and it contains $x$ and all the $\eta_i$.

attrs.title: An affine open containing a point and all generic points

objects.body:
Let $T$ and $Y$ be schemes over $S$ with $Y\to S$ separated, let
$a,b\colon T\to Y$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes and let $V\subseteq T$ be a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme with $a|_V=b|_V$. Then $a=b$.

## Proof

This is 01RH. Concretely, the equaliser of $a$ and $b$ is the
base change of the diagonal $Y\to Y\times_S Y$ along
$(a,b)\colon T\to Y\times_S Y$, hence a closed subscheme of $T$ because
$Y\to S$ is separated; it contains $V$, which is scheme-theoretically dense, so
it is all of $T$.

attrs.title: Two morphisms agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dense open

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $j\colon V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ be a quasi-compact
immersion. Let $Z\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $j$.
Then $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_S$, the induced morphism
$V\to Z$ is an open immersion identifying $V$ with a scheme-theoretically dense
open subscheme of $Z$, and $Z\to S$ is proper.

The formalisation packages this data as a structure
`ProperClosedModel`, in the case in which it is used below: $S$ is
noetherian and $g\colon V\to S$ is locally of finite type with $V$ affine, so
that $j$ is supplied by [lem-chow-affine-immersion] and is automatically
quasi-compact because $V$ is then noetherian.

## Proof

The first two assertions are 01RG applied to the quasi-compact
immersion $j$. For the last one, $\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is proper by
01WC, a closed immersion is proper by 01W5, and
a composition of proper morphisms is proper; hence $Z\to S$ is proper.

attrs.title: Closed model of a quasi-compact immersion

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme, let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be pairwise distinct
irreducible components of $X$ and let $\eta_i\in Z_i$ be their generic points.
Then there are affine opens $U_i\subseteq X$ with $\eta_i\in U_i$ and
$U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset$ for $i\neq j$. Consequently
$U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ is an affine open containing all the $\eta_i$.

## Proof

For $k\neq i$ we have $\eta_i\notin Z_k$: otherwise
$Z_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}\subseteq Z_k$, contradicting that $Z_i$ and $Z_k$
are distinct irreducible components. Hence
$\bigcap_{k\neq i}(X\setminus Z_k)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta_i$, and
since the affine opens form a basis of the topology we may choose an affine
open $V_i$ with

$$
\eta_i\in V_i\subseteq\bigcap_{k\neq i}(X\setminus Z_k).
$$

In particular $V_i\cap Z_k=\emptyset$, and a fortiori $\eta_k\notin V_i$, for
all $k\neq i$.

Fix $i$ and put $W_i:=\bigcup_{j\neq i}(V_i\cap V_j)$. Each $V_i\cap V_j$ is
quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-separated, so $W_i$ is a quasi-compact open
subset of $V_i$, and $\eta_i\notin W_i$ because $\eta_i\notin V_j$ for
$j\neq i$. Write $V_i=\Spec R_i$. The irreducible components of the open
subscheme $V_i$ are the nonempty intersections $C\cap V_i$ with $C$ an
irreducible component of $X$, so $Z_i\cap V_i$ is an irreducible component of
$V_i$ with generic point $\eta_i$; equivalently $\eta_i$ corresponds to a
minimal prime $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq R_i$. By 00EV applied to
$R_i$, the minimal prime $\mathfrak p_i$ and the quasi-compact open
$W_i\subseteq\Spec R_i$, there is $f_i\in R_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ with
$D(f_i)\cap W_i=\emptyset$. Put $U_i:=D(f_i)$. Then $U_i$ is an affine open
containing $\eta_i$, and for $j\neq i$ we have
$U_i\cap V_j\subseteq V_i\cap V_j\subseteq W_i$, whence
$U_i\cap V_j=\emptyset$ and in particular $U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset$.

Finally, a scheme that is the disjoint union of two affine opens is affine by
01I5; iterating, $U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ is affine.

attrs.title: Disjoint affine neighbourhoods of generic points

objects.body:
In the situation of [lem-chow-graph] put $V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and
$X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$, an open subscheme of $Z$. Then the morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i}\colon V_i\to U_i\subseteq X$ glue to a morphism of $S$-schemes

$$
\pi\colon X'\longrightarrow X
$$

with $\pi|_{V_i}=p_i|_{V_i}$, and $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$.

In the formalisation $V_i$ is the preimage under $p_i$ of the image of $U_i$ in
$Z_i$, and $V_i$, $U$ and $X'$ are all opens of $Z$; the last assertion reads
that the composition of the open immersion $U\to X'$ with $\pi$ is the inclusion
$U\to X$.

## Proof

By [lem-chow-graph](3) we have $U\subseteq V_i$ for every $i$, and
$p_i|_U\colon U\to U_i\subseteq X$ is the inclusion. Since $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $Z$ and $V_i\cap V_j\subseteq Z$ is open, $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $V_i\cap V_j$. The two morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ and $p_j|_{V_i\cap V_j}$ into $X$ agree on $U$, and
$X\to S$ is separated, so they are equal by
[lem-chow-agree-on-dense-open]. Hence the $p_i|_{V_i}$ glue to
$\pi\colon X'\to X$, and $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$.

Let $S$ be noetherian, let $X\to S$ be separated of finite type and let
$X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ be a finite affine open covering such that
$U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$. Choose, by
[lem-chow-affine-immersion], immersions
$j_i\colon U_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ and, by [lem-chow-closed-model],
closed subschemes $Z_i\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ with $U_i\to Z_i$ a
scheme-theoretically dense open immersion and $Z_i\to S$ proper. Let
$Z\subseteq\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ be the
scheme-theoretic image of

$$
j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U)\colon U
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S .
$$

Then:

1. $Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ is a
closed immersion, $j$ induces an open immersion $U\to Z$ identifying $U$ with
a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme of $Z$, and $Z\to S$ is proper;
1. for every $i$ the projection $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z\colon Z\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ factors through $Z_i$, and the induced morphism
$p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$ is proper;
1. $p_i|_U$ is the open immersion $U\to U_i\to Z_i$; in particular
$U\subseteq p_i^{-1}(U_i)$.

The formalisation takes the $m$-fold fibre product
$\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ to be the categorical
product in the category of $S$-schemes, so that (1) is a closed immersion into
that product rather than into a single projective space; the composition with
the Segre embedding of [lem-chow-segre], giving a closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$ as used in Step 7 of the proof of
[thm-chow-lemma], is the separate statement
`ChowGraph.exists_isClosedImmersion_over` listed above. It also
weakens the hypotheses to what the proof uses:
the members of the cover need not be affine and need not cover $X$, only $X$
needs to be a noetherian space, and $U$ need not be dense in $X$.

## Proof

Each $j_i|_U$ is an immersion, being the composition of the open immersion
$U\to U_i$ with the immersion $j_i$. Hence $j$ is an immersion by
[lem-chow-tuple-immersion], and it is quasi-compact because $U$ is
noetherian. Part (1) now follows from 01RG for the first two
assertions; for the third, $\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S \mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to S$ is proper, being a finite fibre product of proper
$S$-schemes, and $Z$ is a closed subscheme of it, so $Z\to S$ is proper by
01W5.

For (2), the open immersion $U\to Z$ is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically
dominant, so $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z\colon Z\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ and its restriction
$\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j=j_i|_U$ to $U$ have the same kernel. That kernel
contains the ideal sheaf of $Z_i$, because $j_i|_U$ factors through $Z_i$ by
construction; so the universal property of the closed immersion
$Z_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ produces the morphism $p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$ with
$p_i$ followed by $Z_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$ equal to $\mathrm{pr}_i|_Z$. (This
is 01R9 in the case in which $Z_i$ is presented as the
scheme-theoretic image of $j_i|_U$, which it is: formation of the
scheme-theoretic image commutes with restriction to the open $U_i\subseteq X$.)
It is proper: $Z\to S$ is proper by (1) and $Z_i\to S$ is separated, so $p_i$
is proper by 01W6.

Part (3) is immediate from $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ j=j_i|_U$ and the fact that
$j_i$ identifies $U_i$ with an open subscheme of $Z_i$.

In the situation of [lem-chow-glue] one has $\pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i$ for every
$i$. Consequently $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is the proper morphism
$p_i|_{V_i}$.

## Proof

The inclusion $V_i\subseteq\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ holds because $\pi|_{V_i}=p_i|_{V_i}$
takes values in $U_i$. The morphism $p_i|_{V_i}\colon V_i\to U_i$ is proper,
being the base change of the proper morphism $p_i$ along the open immersion
$U_i\to Z_i$. The open subscheme $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq Z$ is separated over
$S$, hence $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is separated. Applying 01W6
to the commutative triangle formed by $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ and the two
morphisms to $U_i$, we conclude that $V_i\to\pi^{-1}(U_i)$ is universally
closed; in particular $V_i$ is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. On the other hand
$U\subseteq V_i$ and $U$ is dense in the open subscheme
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq Z$, so $V_i$ is dense in $\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. Being closed
and dense, $V_i=\pi^{-1}(U_i)$.

attrs.title: The preimages of the members of the cover

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme such that
the inclusion $u\colon U\to X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let
$X^{*}\subseteq X$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $u$. Then:

1. $X^{*}\to X$ is a surjective closed immersion which is an isomorphism
over $U$;
1. $U\subseteq X^{*}$ is a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme;
1. if $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ is a finite affine open covering, then the
opens $U_i^{*}:=X^{*}\cap U_i$ are affine, cover $X^{*}$, and satisfy
$U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=U$.

## Proof

By construction $X^{*}\to X$ is a closed immersion, and $U$ factors through it.
Its image is a closed subset containing the dense subset $U$, hence is all of
$X$, so $X^{*}\to X$ is surjective. The quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of $X^{*}$
is $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to u_*\mathcal O_U)$, whose restriction to $U$ is
$\ker(\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U)=0$; hence $X^{*}\cap U=U$ and $X^{*}\to X$
is an isomorphism over $U$. This proves (1). Since formation of the
scheme-theoretic image commutes with restriction to opens, the
scheme-theoretic image of $U\to X^{*}$ is $X^{*}$, which is (2). For (3), each
$U_i^{*}$ is a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $U_i$, hence affine, and
$U_1^{*}\cap\dots\cap U_m^{*}=X^{*}\cap U=U$.

In Lean, $X^{*}$ is `U.ι.image`, the scheme-theoretic image of the
inclusion `U.ι`, and $U_i^{*}$ is the open
`U.ι.imageι ⁻¹ᵁ Uᵢ` of $X^{*}$; the copy of $U$ in $X^{*}$ is
`U.ι.imageι ⁻¹ᵁ U`. Surjectivity comes from the identification of the
underlying set of a scheme-theoretic image with the closure of the set-theoretic image
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.range_imageι`), and being an isomorphism
over $U$ is expressed as `IsIso (U.ι.imageι ∣_ U)`. Only
quasi-compactness of $u$ is used: quasi-separatedness is automatic for an open immersion, and
Mathlib's kernel ideal sheaf theory needs only quasi-compactness.

attrs.title: Scheme-theoretic closure of a dense open

objects.body:
The morphism $s$ of [def-chow-segre] is a closed immersion. Consequently,
for index sets $n_1,\dots,n_m$ there are an index set $N$ and a closed
immersion of $S$-schemes

$$
\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{N}_S ;
$$

one may take $N=n_1\times\dots\times n_m$. Moreover, if all the $n_i$ are
finite, then $\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to S$ is
proper.

## Proof

Being a closed immersion is local on the target and on $S$, so we may assume
$S=\Spec A$ is affine and check the assertion on the standard affine charts
$D_+(X_e)\subseteq\mathbf P^N_S$, which cover $\mathbf P^N_S$. For a
multi-index $e$ one has

$$
s^{-1}\bigl(D_+(X_e)\bigr)=\prod_{i=1}^m D_+(x_{i,e_i}),
$$

which is affine, being a finite fibre product of affine schemes over the affine
base. On these charts $s$ is induced by the $A$-algebra homomorphism

$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_S}\bigl(D_+(X_e)\bigr)
\longrightarrow
\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n_1}_S}\bigl(D_+(x_{1,e_1})\bigr)\otimes_A\dots
\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{n_m}_S}\bigl(D_+(x_{m,e_m})\bigr),
\qquad
\frac{X_f}{X_e}\longmapsto\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{x_{i,f_i}}{x_{i,e_i}}.
$$

This homomorphism is surjective: for each $i$ and each $0\leq f_i\leq n_i$ the
multi-index $f=(e_1,\dots,e_{i-1},f_i,e_{i+1},\dots,e_m)$ satisfies
$X_f/X_e\mapsto x_{i,f_i}/x_{i,e_i}$, and these ratios generate the target as
an $A$-algebra. Hence $s$ is, locally on the target, the morphism of affine
schemes attached to a surjective ring homomorphism, i.e. a closed immersion.
Compare 01WD. (The argument above is written for a general
$m$; the formalisation carries it out for the binary case $m=2$ over
$\Spec\mathbf Z$, obtains a general base $S$ by base change, and reduces the
general $m$ to the binary case by the induction below.)

The $m$-fold statement follows by induction on the index set of the product.
For the empty product the fibre product is $S$ itself, which is
$\mathbf P^{N}_S$ for a one-element index set $N$; and if
$\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\to\mathbf P^{N}_S$ is
a closed immersion, then so is

$$
\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\bigl(\mathbf P^{n_2}_S\times_S\dots\times_S
\mathbf P^{n_m}_S\bigr)
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\mathbf P^{N}_S
\longrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_1\times N}_S,
$$

the first morphism because closed immersions are stable under base change and
the second by the binary case.

The last assertion does not use the Segre embedding: a finite fibre product of
proper $S$-schemes is proper over $S$, because properness is stable under base
change and under composition, and $\mathbf P^{n_i}_S\to S$ is proper by
01WC.

attrs.title: The Segre embedding is a closed immersion

objects.body:
Let $S$ be a scheme, let $Y_1,\dots,Y_m$ be schemes over $S$ and let
$f_i\colon T\to Y_i$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes. If some $f_k$ is an
immersion, then

$$
(f_1,\dots,f_m)\colon T\longrightarrow Y_1\times_S\dots\times_S Y_m
$$

is an immersion.

## Proof

Composing $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ with the projection $\mathrm{pr}_k$ gives back
$f_k$, which is an immersion; hence $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ is an immersion, because
if a composition $h\circ g$ is an immersion then so is $g$.

(The blueprint originally deduced this from 01KR by factoring
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ through $T\times_S Y_2\times_S\dots\times_S Y_m$, which also
requires the $Y_i$ to be separated over $S$. The argument above needs neither.)

attrs.title: Tuples of morphisms with one immersion

objects.body:
Let $B:V\times W\to E$ be a perfect similitude pairing of multiplier $\mu$ for
the automorphisms $F_V,F_W$. Then

$$
\phi_BF_W=\mu\,(F_V^{-1})^\vee\phi_B,
$$

so $F_W$ is conjugate to $\mu\,(F_V^{-1})^\vee$.

## Proof

Evaluate both sides at $w\in W$ and then at $v\in V$: the left side gives
$B(v,F_Ww)$ and the right side gives $\mu B(F_V^{-1}v,w)$, and these agree by
the similitude identity applied to the pair $(F_V^{-1}v,w)$. Since $\phi_B$
is an isomorphism, the displayed identity exhibits the conjugacy.

For a finite cohomological trace datum,

$$
\sum_{n\geq1}N_n\frac{T^n}{n}
=\sum_{n\geq1}\left(\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i\Tr(F_i^n\mid V_i)\right)\frac{T^n}{n}
\qquad\text{in }TE[[T]].
$$

## Proof

The two series are compared coefficientwise; in degree $n$ the assertion is
the image in $E$ of the equality (iii) of [def-zla-trace-datum] divided by
the invertible integer $n$. The left-hand side is the coefficientwise scalar
extension along $\mathbf Q\to E$ of a series with rational coefficients.

Let $K\hookrightarrow L$ be an injective field homomorphism. For every finite
square matrix $M$ over $K$,

$$
\det(M)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det(M\otimes_KL)=0.
$$

Consequently a finite family of sequences in $K^{\mathbf N}$ that is linearly
independent over $K$ remains linearly independent over $L$, and every finite
bound on the dimension of the shift span over $L$ descends to a bound over
$K$.

## Proof

The determinant is a finite polynomial expression in the matrix entries and is
compatible with the ring homomorphism $K\to L$, which is injective, so it
reflects the vanishing of that expression. The consequence follows from
[lem-zla-finite-coordinates]: a $K$-independent family has a nonvanishing
finite coordinate determinant, which stays nonzero over $L$.

Assume $P_i$ is pure of weight $i$ for every $i$. If $i\neq j$, then $P_i$
and $P_j$ have no common reciprocal root in $\Omega$.

## Proof

A common reciprocal root would be universally pure of weight $i$ and of weight
$j$, so $i=j$ by [lem-zla-scalar-weight-unique].

attrs.title: Different weights have disjoint reciprocal roots

objects.body:
With the notation of [def-zla-integral-shift-lattice], there is a finite
set $J\subset\mathbf N$ such that coordinate evaluation

$$
\operatorname{ev}_J:W\longrightarrow\mathbf Q^J
$$

is injective. Its restriction maps $M(a)$ injectively into $\mathbf Z^J$.
Hence $M(a)$ is a finite free abelian group.

## Proof

Choose a basis of $W$ consisting of shifts of $a$ and let $J$ be a set of
coordinates on which the corresponding determinant does not vanish
([lem-zla-finite-coordinates]); then $\operatorname{ev}_J$ is injective on
$W$ for dimension reasons. Every element of $M(a)$ is an integral linear
combination of integral sequences, hence integral, so
$\operatorname{ev}_J(M(a))\subseteq\mathbf Z^J$, and a subgroup of a finite
free abelian group is finite free.

Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K^{\mathbf N}$ be linearly independent. There exist
indices $n_1,\ldots,n_r\in\mathbf N$ such that

$$
\det\left(v_j(n_i)\right)_{1\leq i,j\leq r}\neq0.
$$

## Proof

Induct on $r$ by finite Gaussian elimination: given indices that work for
$v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1}$, subtract from $v_r$ the unique combination of
$v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1}$ agreeing with it at those indices; the residual sequence
is nonzero by independence, so it does not vanish at some further coordinate
$n_r$, and expanding the determinant along the last row gives a nonzero
value.

Let $f(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}a_nT^n$ be the Taylor series of the normalized rational
germ $A(T)/B(T)$, where $B(T)=1+c_1T+\cdots+c_dT^d$. Then

$$
a_n+c_1a_{n-1}+\cdots+c_da_{n-d}=0
$$

whenever $n>\deg A$ and $n\geq d$. In particular $(c_1,\ldots,c_d;\deg A+1)$
is an eventual recurrence of order $d$ for $a$.

## Proof

Read off the coefficient of $T^n$ in the identity $B(T)f(T)=A(T)$: the
left-hand side contributes $\sum_{k=0}^{d}c_ka_{n-k}$ with $c_0=1$, and the
right-hand side contributes $0$ once $n>\deg A$.

attrs.title: A rational germ supplies a recurrence

objects.body:
With the notation of [def-zla-integral-shift-lattice], the shift
endomorphism $S:M(a)\to M(a)$ has a monic characteristic polynomial

$$
C(U)=U^r+c_{r-1}U^{r-1}+\cdots+c_0\in\mathbf Z[U],
$$

where $r$ is the rank of $M(a)$, and for every $n\geq0$,

$$
a_{n+r}+c_{r-1}a_{n+r-1}+\cdots+c_0a_n=0.
$$

## Proof

By [lem-zla-finite-coordinate-lattice] the group $M(a)$ is finite free, and
it is stable under the shift, so $S$ has an integral matrix in any basis; its
characteristic polynomial is monic with integer coefficients.
Cayley–Hamilton over $\mathbf Z$ gives
$S^ra+c_{r-1}S^{r-1}a+\cdots+c_0a=0$ in $M(a)$, and reading this equality of
sequences in coordinate $n$ is the displayed recurrence.

Let $K$ be a field. Suppose $A,B,O,E\in K[T]$ have constant coefficient $1$,
both pairs $(A,B)$ and $(O,E)$ are coprime, and $OB=EA$. Then

$$
O=A,\qquad E=B.
$$

## Proof

From $OB=EA$ and coprimality of $(A,B)$, Euclid's lemma gives $A\mid O$ and
$B\mid E$; symmetrically coprimality of $(O,E)$ gives $O\mid A$ and
$E\mid B$. So $O$ and $A$ agree up to a unit of $K[T]$, that is a nonzero
scalar, and likewise for $E$ and $B$; the normalization by constant
coefficient $1$ makes both scalars equal to $1$.

Let $A\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy $A(0)=1$. If

$$
A(T)=P(T)Q(T),\qquad P,Q\in\mathbf Q[T],\qquad P(0)=Q(0)=1,
$$

then $P,Q\in\mathbf Z[T]$.

## Proof

Reversal turns a polynomial with constant coefficient $1$ and degree $b$ into
the monic polynomial $U^bA(U^{-1})$, and it is multiplicative for the
degrees involved here, so the factorization becomes a factorization of the
monic integral polynomial $U^{\deg A}A(U^{-1})$ into the monic rational
polynomials $U^{\deg P}P(U^{-1})$ and $U^{\deg Q}Q(U^{-1})$. Gauss's lemma –
primitive integral normalization together with multiplicativity of the content
– forces both monic rational factors to be integral, and reversing back gives
$P,Q\in\mathbf Z[T]$.

If $a\in K^{\mathbf N}$ satisfies an eventual recurrence, then
$\operatorname{Sh}_K(a)$ is finite-dimensional.

## Proof

Let $(c_1,\ldots,c_d;N)$ be the recurrence and put
$M=\max\{N,d\}$. Beyond the threshold the recurrence expresses $S^ma$, for
$m\geq M$, as a $K$-linear combination of $S^{m-1}a,\ldots,S^{m-d}a$ up to a
sequence supported in the finitely many coordinates below the threshold; hence
$\operatorname{Sh}_K(a)$ is contained in the span of
$a,Sa,\ldots,S^{M-1}a$ together with the finitely many coordinate vectors
supported before the recurrence threshold, and by induction on $m$ every shift
lies in that finite-dimensional space.

attrs.title: A recurrence gives finite shift span

objects.body:
For $P$ as in [def-zla-reversal], the polynomial $P^{\mathrm{rev}}$ is
monic, and for every field $\Omega$ containing $\mathbf Q$ and every
$\alpha\in\Omega^\times$,

$$
P(\alpha^{-1})=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P^{\mathrm{rev}}(\alpha)=0.
$$

## Proof

Monicity is the coefficient $c_0=1$ of $P$ read in top degree after reversal.
The equivalence is the defining identity
$P^{\mathrm{rev}}(\alpha)=\alpha^bP(\alpha^{-1})$ together with
$\alpha\neq0$.

If a nonzero algebraic number is universally pure of weight $w$ and of weight
$w'$, then $w=w'$.

## Proof

The scalar is itself a complex root of its own minimal polynomial, so its
absolute value is both $q^{w/2}$ and $q^{w'/2}$; the real exponential with
base $q>1$ is injective, so $w=w'$.

If two normalized rational germs have the same Taylor series, then they are
equal. Equivalently, Taylor expansion gives an injective map

$$
K(T)_0\hookrightarrow K[[T]].
$$

## Proof

A denominator with constant coefficient $1$ is invertible in $K[[T]]$, so the
equality $AB^{-1}=A'B'^{-1}$ of power series may be cross-multiplied to
$AB'=A'B$ in $K[[T]]$; both sides are polynomials, and $K[T]\to K[[T]]$ is
injective, so the equality holds in $K[T]$, which is the defining relation of
the equivalence.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space and let
$u\in\operatorname{End}_E(V)$. Then

$$
P_{V,u}(T)^{-1}
=\operatorname{Exp}\left(\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(u^n\mid V)\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
\qquad\text{in }E[[T]],
$$

the inverse on the left being taken in $E[[T]]$, which is legitimate because
$P_{V,u}(0)=1$. Equivalently,

$$
T\frac{d}{dT}\operatorname{Log}P_{V,u}(T)^{-1}
=\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(u^n\mid V)T^n.
$$

No semisimplicity assumption is imposed on $u$.

## Proof

Differentiating a determinant gives the matrix identity
$\frac{d}{dT}\det(1-Tu)=-\det(1-Tu)\Tr\!\left((1-Tu)^{-1}u\right)$ in
$E[[T]]$, where the formal resolvent is
$(1-Tu)^{-1}=\sum_{n\geq0}T^nu^n$; taking the trace coefficientwise turns the
right-hand side into $-\det(1-Tu)\sum_{n\geq1}\Tr(u^n)T^{n-1}$. Both sides of
the asserted identity therefore have constant coefficient $1$ and the same
logarithmic derivative, and over a $\mathbf Q$-algebra a power series is
determined by its constant coefficient and its derivative.

Two stratifications $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$ and
$(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to X)_{l<m}$ of a scheme $X$ have a common refinement.

## Proof

Index the pairs $(k,l)$ by $k+nl<nm$. The intersections $X_k\cap X'_l$ are
locally closed (an intersection of two locally closed sets is locally
closed), pairwise disjoint, and cover $X$. Take as scheme on the stratum
$X_k\cap X'_l$ the fibre product $Z_k\times_XW_l$ with the immersion
$Z_k\times_XW_l\to X$; it is an immersion, as a composite of the base
change of $\kappa_l$ with $\iota_k$, and its image is
$\iota_k(\iota_k^{-1}(X'_l))=X_k\cap X'_l$. This stratification refines
both given ones.

A constant sheaf is locally constant.

## Proof

The identity cover $(X\to X)$ is a trivialising datum: the restriction of
$M_X$ to $\et X$ localised at $X$ is $M_X$ again, which is constant.

Finite direct sums of finite locally constant sheaves are finite locally
constant; the same holds for locally constant sheaves and for finite
sheaves.

## Proof

For two sheaves with trivialising data $(U_i\to X)_i$ and $(V_j\to X)_j$,
the family $(U_i\times_XV_j\to X)_{i,j}$ is an étale cover trivialising
both. Restriction to a localised site is exact and preserves finite direct
sums, and a finite direct sum $M_X\oplus N_X$ of constant sheaves is the
constant sheaf $(M\oplus N)_X$, because sheafification and the constant
presheaf functor are additive. Stalks commute with finite direct sums,
and a finite direct sum of finite sets is finite.

Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between finite locally constant
sheaves, and the middle term of a short exact sequence whose outer terms
are finite locally constant, are finite locally constant. (The kernel and
cokernel statements are formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$; the extension
statement is not.)

## Proof

Restricting to an étale cover trivialising both sheaves
([lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct]), we may assume the morphism is
$\varphi\colon M_X\to N_X$ with $M$, $N$ finite (the stalks of the constant
sheaf $M_X$ are $M$). By [lemma-constructible-hom-constant-locally]
kernel and cokernel are locally constant with finite stalks.

For an extension $0\to M_X\to\mathcal E\to N_X\to0$, again on a
trivialising cover, consider the sheaf $P$ of sections of
$\mathcal E\to N_X$: over $U\to X$ its sections are the morphisms
$s\colon N_U\to\mathcal E|_U$ with $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}$. It is a torsor
under the sheaf $\mathcal{H}om(N_X,M_X)=\Hom_\Lambda(N,M)_X$ (two sections
differ by a morphism $N_U\to M_U$, and locally sections exist since the
sequence is locally split in the étale topology: the stalks are finite
modules and a surjection of sheaves is locally surjective on sections).
The group $\Hom_\Lambda(N,M)$ is finite, so by
[lemma-constructible-torsor-trivialises] $P$ has a section over an
étale cover $(U_i\to X)$, and over $U_i$ the sequence splits:
$\mathcal E|_{U_i}\cong M_{U_i}\oplus N_{U_i}=(M\oplus N)_{U_i}$. Hence
$\mathcal E$ is locally constant, with finite stalks $M\oplus N$.

attrs.title: Kernels, cokernels and extensions of finite locally constant sheaves

objects.body:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a ring, let $M$ be a finite
$\Lambda$-module, let $N$ be a $\Lambda$-module and let $\varphi\colon M_X\to N_X$ be a
morphism of constant sheaves on $\et X$. Then there is an étale cover
$(U_i\to X)_i$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}$ is induced by a $\Lambda$-linear
map $f_i\colon M\to N$, i.e. equals $(f_i)_{U_i}\colon M_{U_i}\to N_{U_i}$.
Consequently the kernel and the cokernel of $\varphi$ are locally constant,
with restrictions $(\ker f_i)_{U_i}$ and $(\operatorname{coker}f_i)_{U_i}$.

## Proof

By the adjunction between constant sheaves and global sections,
$\Hom(M_X,N_X)=\Hom_\Lambda(M,\Gamma(X,N_X))$. A global section of $N_X$
over $X$ is, on an étale cover, a section of the constant presheaf, that
is, an element of $N$; hence, on an étale cover $(U_i\to X)_i$ obtained by
intersecting the covering sieves for the finitely many sections $\varphi(m)$,
$m\in M$, every $\varphi(m)$ is the constant section $n_{i,m}$ over $U_i$.
Over a nonempty $U_i$ the map $N\to\Gamma(U_i,N_X)$ is injective (a
section of the constant presheaf which becomes zero in the sheafification
vanishes on a covering sieve, whose members are nonempty), so
$m\mapsto n_{i,m}$ is $\Lambda$-linear, giving $f_i\colon M\to N$ with
$\varphi|_{U_i}$ the morphism of constant sheaves induced by $f_i$ (both
morphisms out of the constant sheaf $M_{U_i}$ have the same adjoint
$M\to\Gamma(U_i,N_X)$; here one uses that the restriction of a constant
sheaf to $\et{U_i}$ is the constant sheaf, compatibly with the unit maps).
Empty $U_i$ are discarded from the cover.
Since restriction to $\et{U_i}$ is exact and the constant sheaf functor is
exact (a composite of the exact constant presheaf functor and
sheafification), the kernel and cokernel of $\varphi|_{U_i}$ are the
constant sheaves on $\ker f_i$ and $\operatorname{coker}f_i$.

Let $a\colon Z\to X$ and $b\colon Z'\to X$ be immersions with the same
image. Then $a^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant if and only if
$b^*\mathcal F$ is.

## Proof

Let $W=Z\times_XZ'$ with projections $p\colon W\to Z$ and $q\colon W\to Z'$.
The projection $p$ is an immersion, as a base change of $b$, and it is
surjective, its image being $a^{-1}(b(Z'))=a^{-1}(a(Z))=Z$. A surjective
immersion is a surjective closed immersion (an immersion is a closed
immersion into an open subscheme, and surjectivity forces that open to be
everything), hence a universal homeomorphism. The same holds for $q$. Now
$p^*a^*\mathcal F\cong q^*b^*\mathcal F$, both being the pullback along
$a\circ p=b\circ q$, so by
[lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] applied to
$p$ and to $q$, $a^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant if and only if
$p^*a^*\mathcal F$ is, if and only if $q^*b^*\mathcal F$ is, if and only if
$b^*\mathcal F$ is.

If $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F'$ in $\shv{\et X}$, then $\mathcal F$ is
locally constant (finite, finite locally constant, constructible) if and
only if $\mathcal F'$ is.

## Proof

An isomorphism of sheaves induces isomorphisms of the restrictions to every
localised site, of all stalks, and of all pullbacks, and each of the four
notions is a condition on these. A trivialising datum, respectively a
stratification, for $\mathcal F$ is therefore one for $\mathcal F'$.

If $\mathcal G\in\shv{\et U}$ is constructible, then so is
$j_!\mathcal G$.

## Proof

As before: $i^*j_!\mathcal G=0$ by
[lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowershriek], and $j^*j_!\mathcal G\cong \mathcal G$ by the unit isomorphism of the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$
([sec-openclosed-setting]).

attrs.title: Extension by zero along an open immersion

objects.body:
If $\mathcal G\in\shv{\et Z}$ is constructible, then so is
$i_*\mathcal G$.

## Proof

By [prop-constructible-open-closed] it suffices to see that
$j^*i_*\mathcal G$ and $i^*i_*\mathcal G$ are constructible. The first is
zero by [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar], and the zero sheaf is
constructible (the trivial stratification with one stratum; the zero sheaf
is constant with finite stalks). The second is isomorphic to $\mathcal G$
by the counit isomorphism of
[prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful], hence constructible by
[lemma-constructible-iso-invariance].

Let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ be a stratification with all
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ finite locally constant, and let
$(\kappa_l\colon W_l\to X)_l$ refine it. Then all $\kappa_l^*\mathcal F$
are finite locally constant.

## Proof

Fix $l$ and choose $k$ with $X'_l\subseteq X_k$. The base change
$\kappa'_l\colon W_l\times_XZ_k\to Z_k$ of $\kappa_l$ is an immersion, and
the composite $\iota_k\circ\kappa'_l\colon W_l\times_XZ_k\to X$ is an
immersion with image $\iota_k(\iota_k^{-1}(X'_l))=X'_l$, the same image as
$\kappa_l$. Its pullback of $\mathcal F$ is
$\kappa_l'^*\iota_k^*\mathcal F$, finite locally constant by
[prop-constructible-pullback] (its lemmas for locally constant and
finite sheaves). By [lemma-constructible-immersion-independence],
$\kappa_l^*\mathcal F$ is finite locally constant.

For $g\colon Y\to X$ and $M\in\mathcal A$ there is a natural isomorphism
$g^*(M_X)\cong M_Y$. In particular $g^*$ sends constant sheaves to constant
sheaves.

## Proof

Both $M\mapsto g^*(M_X)$ and $M\mapsto M_Y$ are left adjoint to
$\mathcal G\mapsto\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)=\Gamma(X,g_*\mathcal G)$, because
base change along $g$ preserves the terminal object of the site
($Y\times_XX\cong Y$); left adjoints are unique up to unique isomorphism.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be
finite. Then $g^*\mathcal F$ is finite.

## Proof

For a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$, the stalk $(g^*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$
is the stalk $\mathcal F_{g\circ\bar y}$ by
[lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], which is finite by hypothesis.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$ be
locally constant. Then $g^*\mathcal F$ is locally constant.

## Proof

Let $(U_i\to X)_i$ be a trivialising datum for $\mathcal F$. The base
change $(U_i\times_XY\to Y)_i$ is an étale cover of $Y$, since étale
morphisms and jointly surjective families are stable under base change.
The restriction of $g^*\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i\times_XY}$ is the pullback,
along the projection $g_i\colon U_i\times_XY\to U_i$, of the restriction
of $\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i}$: pullback along $g$ followed by restriction to
the localised site equals restriction followed by pullback along $g_i$,
because both are the sheaf pullback along the composite of the base change
functors, which agree. The restriction of $\mathcal F$ to $\et{U_i}$ is
constant, and pullbacks of constant sheaves are constant by
[lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Hence
$(U_i\times_XY\to Y)_i$ is a trivialising datum for $g^*\mathcal F$.

Let $g\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_{k<n}$
be a stratification of $X$. Then the base changes
$(\iota'_k\colon Z_k\times_XY\to Y)_{k<n}$ form a stratification of $Y$,
with strata $g^{-1}(X_k)$.

## Proof

Immersions are stable under base change, and the image of the base change
$Z_k\times_XY\to Y$ of $\iota_k$ is the preimage $g^{-1}(\iota_k(Z_k))$:
the underlying set of a fibre product of schemes surjects onto the
set-theoretic fibre product, so the image of the projection to $Y$ is
exactly the set of points of $Y$ whose image in $X$ lies in the image of
$\iota_k$. The sets $g^{-1}(X_k)$ are locally closed, pairwise disjoint and
cover $Y$, as preimages of the locally closed, pairwise disjoint sets $X_k$
covering $X$.

Let $\mathcal G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of groups on $\et X$
and let $P$ be a $\mathcal G$-torsor. Then $P$ is trivial on an étale
cover of $X$.

## Proof

Working on the members of a trivialising cover of $\mathcal G$ we may
assume $\mathcal G=G_X$ for a finite group $G$. A $G_X$-torsor is
representable by a scheme $P\to X$ finite étale (locally on $X$ it is
$\bigsqcup_{g\in G}X$, and the transition functions are locally constant
permutations; see [SGA4]); since $P\to X$ is étale and
surjective it is an étale cover, and $P$ restricted to $P$ has the
tautological section, so it is trivial there.

attrs.title: Torsors under finite locally constant sheaves

objects.body:
Let $u\colon Z'\to Z$ be a universal homeomorphism. Then
$\mathcal G\in\shv{\et Z}$ is constant (locally constant) if and only if
$u^*\mathcal G$ is. If moreover $u$ is a surjective closed immersion, then
$\mathcal G$ is finite (finite locally constant) if and only if
$u^*\mathcal G$ is.

## Proof

The direction ``only if'' is
[lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant], [lemma-constructible-pullback-finite].
For the converse, base change along $u$ is an equivalence of sites
$\et Z\simeq\et{Z'}$ by
[lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence]
(Tag `04DZ`), hence $u^*$ is an equivalence of categories of sheaves
([prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos]). Constancy: $u^*$ is
fully faithful and carries constant sheaves to constant sheaves, so from
$u^*\mathcal G\cong u^*M_{Z}$ we get $\mathcal G\cong M_Z$. Local
constancy: let $(V'_i\to Z')_i$ be a trivialising étale cover of
$u^*\mathcal G$. Each $V'_i$ is isomorphic over $Z'$ to $V_i\times_ZZ'$
for an étale $V_i\to Z$, and the $V_i$ cover $Z$ since $u$ is
surjective. The projection $u_i\colon V_i\times_ZZ'\to V_i$ is a
universal homeomorphism, and $u_i^*(\mathcal G|_{V_i})\cong (u^*\mathcal G)|_{V'_i}$ is constant, so $\mathcal G|_{V_i}$ is constant
by the first part applied to $u_i$. Finiteness, for $u$ a surjective closed
immersion: the residue field maps of a closed immersion are surjective,
hence isomorphisms, so every geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ lifts to a
geometric point $\bar z'$ of $Z'$ with $u\circ\bar z'=\bar z$, and the
stalk of $\mathcal G$ at $\bar z$ is the stalk of $u^*\mathcal G$ at
$\bar z'$.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $U\subseteq X$ be
quasi-compact. A composition of two $U$-admissible blow-ups is a
$U$-admissible blow-up. The chosen isomorphism over $U$ is the composite of
the chosen pullback isomorphisms.

## Proof

Apply [thm-nagata-composition-of-blowups]. It writes the composite as
the blow-up of a finite-presentation center $Y\hookrightarrow X$ whose
support is the union of the first center and the image of the second center.
Both sets are disjoint from $U$, because the first blow-up is the identity
over $U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], and the second
center is disjoint from its inverse image. Thus $Y\cap U=\varnothing$,
equivalently its defining ideal restricts to the unit ideal on $U$, so the
resulting blow-up is $U$-admissible. The isomorphism supplied by the
composition theorem is over $X$. Pulling it back to $U$ identifies the
composite with the composite of the two specified pullback isomorphisms;
the equality follows after composing with the structure maps, where it is
the associativity equality for fibre products.

If $\pi\colon X'\to X$ is $U$-admissible, then its center ideal restricts to
the unit ideal on $U$, and the induced morphism
$X'\times_XU\to U$ is an isomorphism. The inverse and the equality over
$U$ are part of the resulting specified isomorphism.

## Proof

Choose the ideal and blow-up identification from
[def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. The unit-ideal restriction is the
disjointness condition on the center. Apply
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] to identify the blow-up over $U$
with $U$, then transport that isomorphism across the chosen identification
with $X'$.

attrs.title: An admissible blow-up is unchanged over the preserved open

objects.body:
Let $U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open
immersion, and let $\mathcal I$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal with
$\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Then the inverse image of $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$.
Consequently the same assertion holds after any finite composite of
$U$-admissible blow-ups.

## Proof

First, the complement of the support of an invertible ideal is
scheme-theoretically dense: on an affine open where the ideal is generated
by a single non-zero-divisor $a$, the restriction map to the complement of
the support is the localization away from $a$, which is injective.
Applying this on $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ to the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$, which is
invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], shows that the
inverse image of the complement $W$ of the center is scheme-theoretically
dense in the blow-up. Density now descends along the partial isomorphism:
the blow-up map $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $W$ by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], hence also over the smaller
open $U\subseteq W$; since $U$ is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically
dense in $X$, the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow W$ is scheme-theoretically
dominant, and transporting it across the isomorphism over $W$ and composing
with the dense open immersion $\pi^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ shows that $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is
scheme-theoretically dense. For a finite composite, the inverse image of
$U$ at each stage is again a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open,
so induction on the length of the composite applies the one-step lemma at
each stage.

attrs.title: Density is preserved by an admissible blow-up

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

The blow-up in the zero ideal is empty: the positive-degree part of its Rees
algebra vanishes, so the irrelevant ideal is zero and Proj has no points.

## Proof

If $I=0$, then $I^n=0$ for every $n>0$. Hence the irrelevant ideal of
$\mathcal R_A(0)$ is zero. A point of Proj would be a homogeneous prime not
containing the irrelevant ideal, which is impossible because every prime
contains zero.

For $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the affine blow-up morphism
restricts to an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\setminus Z$.

## Proof

The complement is covered by the basic opens $D(a)$, $a\in I$. On $D(a)$
the localized ideal is the unit ideal, so
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict] and
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-top] identify the blow-up with $D(a)$.
The identifications agree on overlaps by
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict-cocycle], and hence glue.

The constructed morphism $e_I$ is a closed immersion over
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

## Proof

A surjective graded algebra map induces a closed immersion in the opposite
direction on Proj. The source of $\rho_I$ has Proj $\mathbf P^r_A$, and
its degree-zero map is the identity of $A$, so the closed immersion is over
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

attrs.title: Closed immersion into relative projective space

objects.body:
If $I$ is finitely generated, the affine blow-up morphism is proper.

## Proof

It is projective by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-projective], and is
therefore proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-is-proper].

The restriction isomorphism is the identity for $s=1$, and its two possible
composites on an iterated basic open $D(st)$ agree literally after the
chosen canonical associativity isomorphisms.

## Proof

On each standard chart, the map for $s=1$ is induced by the identity of the
Rees algebra, hence is the identity. For $s,t$, both composites send a
homogeneous fraction to its image in the localization at $st$; the two
coefficient maps are equal by [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-one]
and [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-mul].
The chart maps therefore agree on a cover, proving the asserted identity
and cocycle equalities globally.

attrs.title: Identity and cocycle laws for affine restriction

objects.body:
The blow-up of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ in the unit ideal is canonically
isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

## Proof

The Rees algebra of the unit ideal is $A[t]$. The single standard open
$D_+(t)$ covers Proj, and its chart algebra $A[A/1]$ is $A$.

If $U$ is affine, then $U$ is quasi-affine in the sense used in
[lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists]; in
particular that lemma applies to any $U\to S$ of finite type with $U$
affine.

## Proof

The identity of $U$ realizes the canonical map
$U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ as an open immersion, and
$U$ is quasi-compact. This is the defining quasi-affine property, and a
finite-type structure morphism is in particular locally of finite type.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

The algebra $B_{\lambda_B}$ is finitely presented over
$A_{\lambda_B}$, and the constructed map $\beta_B$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

The displayed quotient is a finite presentation by construction. Tensoring
it with $A$ sends every lifted relation to the original $r_j$ and preserves
the finite polynomial presentation. Thus the base-changed presentation is
the chosen presentation of $B$, with $\beta_B$ and its generatorwise inverse
mutually inverse.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the Raynaud–Gruson flattening
chain is not formalized. Elimination of indeterminacy is obtained instead
by the route of the chapter *Elimination of indeterminacy after Deligne
and Conrad*, whose output is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`.

Let $p\colon X'\to X$ be faithfully flat and quasi-compact. If
$f\colon Y\to X$ is quasi-compact and $Y\times_XX'\to X'$ is affine, then
$f$ is affine.

## Proof

Work over an affine $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and choose a finite affine
cover $X'_0=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$. Write the affine pullbacks
as $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$. On overlaps the $B_i$ carry the canonical
descent identifications. Set
$B=\ker(\prod_iB_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}B_i\otimes_AA_{ij})$.
Faithful flatness makes tensoring this equalizer with each $A_i$ exact and
identifies $B\otimes_AA_i$ with $B_i$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$
pulls back to the given affine cover and glues to $Y\times_XX'_0$; the
comparison with $Y$ is an isomorphism after the faithfully flat cover and
therefore an isomorphism. Thus $Y$ is affine over $X_0$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Every selected finite coefficient subalgebra, basic-open element, restricted
overlap map, and proposed inverse is defined at
$\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}$. Under base change to the original chart rings,
these objects are the corresponding restrictions of the data in
$\mathsf G_S$.

## Proof

Each finite coefficient list lies in one finitely generated
$\mathbf Z$-subalgebra by
[lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras]. The selected upper bound
dominates every such stage by
[lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. Hence all selected
coefficients and restricted maps are simultaneously defined at the named
common stage, and base change returns the original finite lists. The full
chart rings are recovered only after taking the filtered colimit over all
finite refinements; no single stage is asserted to contain every coefficient
of an arbitrary chart ring.

The overlap maps in $\mathsf G_{S,\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}}$ preserve the
selected opens, are mutually inverse, and satisfy all identity and
triple-overlap cocycle equations.

## Proof

Every required equality is determined by finitely many generators after
localization. Equality in the colimit is witnessed at a finite stage.
The definition includes all those witness stages in one finite set, and the
selected upper-bound lemma makes every equation hold simultaneously at
$\lambda_{\mathrm{glue}}(S)$.

attrs.title: The selected finite-stage datum satisfies the gluing axioms

objects.body:
Let $A\to B$ be flat, let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and put

$$
I=\ker\bigl(A\longrightarrow\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\bigr).
$$

For $T_B=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ one has

$$
\ker\bigl(B\longrightarrow\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B})\bigr)=IB.
$$

The equality is natural in the flat algebra $B$ and commutes with
localization on $B$.

## Proof

Use the finite affine cover and finite affine refinements from
[lemma-nagata-affine-image-kernel-localization]. Tensor its finite
sheaf equalizer with $B$. Flatness makes tensoring exact, and tensoring
commutes with the finite products in this diagram. The resulting affine
coordinate rings are precisely those of the base-changed cover of $T_B$,
so the resulting equalizer computes $\Gamma(T_B,\mathcal O_{T_B})$.
Exactness identifies the kernel of the base-changed structural map with
$I\otimes_A B$, whose image in $B$ is $IB$. Naturality follows from the
naturality of tensor product, and compatibility with localization is
[lemma-nagata-affine-image-kernel-localization] applied over $B$.

attrs.title: Flat base change of the affine image kernel

objects.body:
Let $A$ be a ring, let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and let $s\in A$. Put

$$
I=\ker\bigl(A\longrightarrow\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\bigr).
$$

If $T_s=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A_s)$, then

$$
\ker\bigl(A_s\longrightarrow\Gamma(T_s,\mathcal O_{T_s})\bigr)=IA_s.
$$

This equality is functorial under further localization.

## Proof

Choose a finite affine cover $(T_i)$ of $T$. Quasi-separatedness makes
each $T_i\cap T_j$ quasi-compact, so choose a finite affine refinement of
every such intersection. The sheaf equalizer for this finite covering
computes $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ from finite products of the coordinate
rings of the selected affine opens and their finite affine refinements.
Localizing this equalizer at $s$ is exact, commutes with its finite
products, and replaces every selected affine by its inverse image in
$T_s$. It therefore computes $\Gamma(T_s,\mathcal O_{T_s})$. Taking the
kernel of the structural map gives $IA_s$. Repeating the same construction
after a second localization gives the stated functoriality.

The constructed open $A(x;\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)$ is affine and contains
$x$ and every $\eta_i$.

## Proof

The selected witness exists by
[lemma-nagata-affine-neighbourhood-generic-points-exists]; its
specification says that the open is affine and contains $x$ and every
selected generic point.
