Let $X$ be quasi-separated, let $x\in X$, and let
$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$ be generic points of finitely many distinct
irreducible components. There is an affine open of $X$ containing $x$ and
every $\eta_i$.

## Proof

Reorder the components so that
$x\in Z_1\cap\cdots\cap Z_m$ and
$x\notin Z_{m+1},\ldots,Z_r$, where $Z_i$ is the component with generic
point $\eta_i$. Choose an affine open $W$ containing $x$ and disjoint from
$Z_{m+1},\ldots,Z_r$. Then $W$ contains
$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_m$. By Stacks Project, Tag 01ZV, choose pairwise
disjoint affine opens $A_i$ containing $\eta_i$ for $i>m$. Since $X$ is
quasi-separated, each $W\cap A_i$ is quasi-compact; it does not contain
$\eta_i$. Write $A_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ and let
$\mathfrak p_i$ be the minimal prime corresponding to $\eta_i$. Stacks
Project, Tag 00EV, applied to $W\cap A_i$ gives
$f_i\in R_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ such that
$D(f_i)\cap W=\varnothing$. Replace $A_i$ by $D(f_i)$. It still contains
$\eta_i$, remains disjoint from the other $A_j$, and is disjoint from $W$.
Thus

$$
W\amalg A_{m+1}\amalg\cdots\amalg A_r
$$

is a finite disjoint union of affine schemes, hence is affine, and it
contains $x$ and every selected generic point. This is the construction in
Stacks Project, Tag 01ZX.

attrs.title: Existence of an affine neighbourhood through finitely many generic points, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible ideal on $X$, and
let $\mathcal J$ be a quasi-coherent ideal (finite-typeness is not needed).
Then the blow-ups of $\mathcal L\mathcal J$ and of $\mathcal J$ are
canonically isomorphic over $X$.

## Proof

Tensor the tautological quotient for $\mathcal J$ with the pullback of the
invertible ideal $\mathcal L$ to obtain an invertible quotient of
$\mathcal L\mathcal J$; this gives a lift from
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(X)$ to
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L\mathcal J}(X)$. Conversely, tensor the
tautological quotient of $\mathcal L\mathcal J$ with the dual of the
pulled-back invertible module $\mathcal L$. The evaluation isomorphism
gives an invertible quotient of $\mathcal J$ and hence a reverse lift.
Locally this is division by a basis of $\mathcal L$, so the quotient maps
are compatible with the specified ideal inclusions and glue independently
of the chosen bases. Both composites induce the original tautological
quotient, so uniqueness in
[thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] makes them identities.

attrs.title: Blow-up is unchanged after multiplying by an invertible factor

objects.body:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal I$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent
ideal on $X$. Its blow-up is proper over $X$. In particular,
every admissible blow-up used in this chapter is proper.

## Proof

A finite type quasi-coherent ideal defines the global blow-up of
[def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its structure map is proper by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper]. An admissible blow-up is a blow-up
of precisely this form.

Under the data of [def-nagata-blowup-universal-lift], the constructed
map $\widetilde f$ is an $X$-morphism: its composite with
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is $f$.

## Proof

On each standard chart, the degree-zero component of
[lemma-nagata-blowup-universal-graded-map] is the canonical map to
$\mathcal O_Y$, hence the composite with the blow-up structure map is $f$.
The chart maps agree on overlaps by functoriality of localization, and the
glued equality is therefore the specified equality over $X$.

The degreewise map $\alpha_f$ respects the unit and multiplication and is a
graded algebra morphism.

## Proof

In degree $n$, tensor $q$ $n$ times. Let
$\mu_{\mathcal I}\colon(f^*\mathcal I)^{\otimes n}\to f^*(\mathcal I^n)$ be multiplication. The composite of $q^{\otimes n}$
with
multiplication isomorphism
$\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal L^n$ from
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-tensor-power] and the injection
$\mathcal L^n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ is ordinary $n$-fold
multiplication. It therefore kills $\ker(\mu_{\mathcal I})$; injectivity
of $\mathcal L^n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_Y$ shows that $q^{\otimes n}$
itself kills this kernel. Hence it factors uniquely through
$f^*(\mathcal I^n)$. These factorizations commute with multiplication by
associativity and with the degree-zero unit, giving the graded algebra map.
Associativity of tensor products and the multiplication maps for ideal
powers show that these degreewise maps preserve the unit and multiplication.

attrs.title: The quotient construction is a graded algebra map

objects.body:
Under the data of [def-nagata-blowup-universal-lift], every $X$-morphism
$h\colon Y\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ inducing the chosen
invertible quotient equals the constructed map $\widetilde f$.

## Proof

On each affine open of $X$, let $D_+(f)$ range over the standard opens
indexed by the degree-one elements $f\in\mathcal I$; these opens cover the
blow-up Proj. The inverse image of each chart
under $h$ is determined by the degree-zero map obtained from the given
quotient $f^*\mathcal I\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$: on a representative
$x/f_i^n$ it is the coefficient of the corresponding quotient fraction in
$\mathcal O_Y$. The constructed lift uses exactly the same degreewise maps,
by definition of $\alpha_f$ and the tensor-power identification, so $h$ and
$\widetilde f$ agree on each inverse-image chart. These equalities are
compatible on chart overlaps because both maps send a localized fraction to
its further localization; the localization cocycle gives literal equality.
The standard charts cover the target, hence their inverse images cover $Y$,
and equality of morphisms on this cover implies $h=\widetilde f$.

If $\overline Z_{i,i}$ and $\overline Z_{i,j}$ are disjoint, then their
strict transforms remain disjoint after every further $V_i$-admissible
blow-up.

## Proof

Let $b\colon X'_i\to X_i$ be a further $V_i$-admissible blow-up. By
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-restrict], the strict transform of
$\overline Z_{i,k}$ is the closure of its restriction over the open on
which $b$ is an isomorphism. It is therefore contained in
$b^{-1}(\overline Z_{i,k})$. The inverse images of the disjoint closed
subschemes $\overline Z_{i,i}$ and $\overline Z_{i,j}$ are disjoint, so
their contained strict transforms are disjoint as well.

The subschemes $Z_i$ are closed in $U$. Each $Z_{i,k}$ is closed in
$V_i$, their underlying closed sets are disjoint, and $\psi_i$ is an
isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of $Z_i$.

## Proof

Since the support of $Z_i$ is $U\setminus U_j$, it is closed in $U$ and
contained in $U_i$. Base change of this closed immersion along $\psi_i$
gives each closed immersion $Z_{i,k}\hookrightarrow V_i$. The supports of
$Z_i$ and $Z_j$ are disjoint because
$(U\setminus U_j)\cap(U\setminus U_i)=U\setminus(U_i\cup U_j)=\varnothing$;
their inverse images in $V_i$ are consequently disjoint. Finally,
$Z_i\subseteq U_i$, and [lemma-nagata-graph-extension] identifies
$\psi_i^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ with an isomorphism. This gives the required
isomorphism on the open neighbourhood $U_i$ of $Z_i$.

attrs.title: Closedness and disjointness of the four boundary loci

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs and let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open. There is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $X_1\to X$ for which the complement of the inverse
image of $U$ is the support of an effective Cartier ideal.

## Proof

Choose the finite type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ with
$V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$ supplied by
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists]. Its restriction to
$U$ is the unit ideal, so its blow-up is $U$-admissible. Moreover,
[thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes the extended ideal an
effective Cartier ideal. Its vanishing locus is the inverse image of
$V(\mathcal I)$, which is the complement of the inverse image of $U$;
the latter inverse image is the preserved open by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. Hence this Cartier ideal has
precisely the required boundary support.

Let $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be an effective Cartier ideal and let
$T'\to T$ be a blow-up. Then the extended ideal
$\mathcal L\mathcal O_{T'}$ is again effective Cartier, and in particular
is invertible.

## Proof

Work over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq T$ on which
$\mathcal L=(x)$ with $x$ a non-zero-divisor. A standard chart of the
blow-up has ring $A[I/a]\subseteq A_a$. If
$x(y/a^n)=0$ in this chart, then $a^mxy=0$ in $A$ for some $m$; regularity
of $x$ gives $a^my=0$, hence $y/a^n=0$. Thus the image of $x$ is regular
on every blow-up chart. It generates the extended ideal there, so these
local equations make $\mathcal L\mathcal O_{T'}$ an effective Cartier
ideal, hence an invertible one.

attrs.title: Total transform of a Cartier ideal under a blow-up

objects.body:
In $A[I/a]$, the extended ideal satisfies

$$
I\,A[I/a]=(a).
$$

## Proof

For $x\in I$, the identity $x=a(x/a)$ gives
$IA[I/a]\subseteq(a)$. Since $a\in I$ and $1\in A[I/a]$, the element
$a=a\cdot1$ belongs to $IA[I/a]$, so every multiple of $a$ belongs to that
ideal and $(a)\subseteq IA[I/a]$.

Multiplication by $a$ on $A[I/a]$ is injective.

## Proof

The chart algebra is a subring of $A_a$. The image of $a$ is a unit in
$A_a$, hence multiplication by it is injective on the subring.

On the overlap of the $a$-chart and the $b$-chart, the two generators $a$
and $b$ of the extended ideal differ by a unit.

## Proof

On the overlap, both $(a)$ and $(b)$ equal the same extended ideal. More
explicitly, $b=a(b/a)$ and $a=b(a/b)$, and $(a/b)(b/a)=1$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

Two representatives $x/a^m$ and $y/a^n$ define the same element of
$A[I/a]$ exactly when they are equal in the localization $A_a$; equivalently,
some power of $a$ annihilates $a^nx-a^my$ after aligning denominators.

## Proof

This is the equality relation in localization away from the powers of $a$.
The statement must use localization equivalence, not cancellation by $a$,
because $a$ may be a zero divisor in $A$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

Every element of $A[I/a]$ is represented in $A_a$ by $x/a^n$ for some
$n\geq 0$ and $x\in I^n$.

## Proof

The generators have the required form with $n=1$. The set of such
fractions contains the image of $A$, and is closed under addition and
multiplication after replacing two denominators by a common power of $a$.
It therefore contains the generated subalgebra. Conversely,
$x\in I^n$ is a sum of products of $n$ elements of $I$, so $x/a^n$ belongs
to the generated algebra.

attrs.title: Normal form in a chart algebra

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: centres are carried as
finite-type ideal sheaves (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`)
throughout, so the translation between finite-presentation closed immersions
and finite-type ideals is never made.

A closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is of finite presentation if and
only if its defining quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is of finite type.

## Proof

The assertion is local on $X$. On $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ the closed
immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. The
quotient $A/I$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra exactly when $I$ is
finitely generated as an ideal. Translate this equivalence back to the
associated quasi-coherent ideal sheaf.

attrs.title: Finite-presentation closed immersions and finite type ideals

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

For every $\mu\geq\mu_{\mathrm{cl}}(g)$, the base change $g_\mu$ is a
closed immersion.

## Proof

Project the eventual closed-immersion field of the witness in
[lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists] along the index selected in
[def-nagata-closed-immersion-stage].

attrs.title: A finite-presentation closed immersion descends at the selected stage

objects.body:
Let $g_\lambda\colon Z_\lambda\to Y_\lambda$ be of finite presentation
between finite-presentation $S_\lambda$-schemes. If its base change to the
inverse limit $S$ is a closed immersion, then there is
$\mu\geq\lambda$ such that every later base change $g_\nu$ is a closed
immersion.

## Proof

Cover $Y_\lambda$ by finitely many affine opens and cover the inverse images
in $Z_\lambda$ by finitely many affine opens; this is finite because the
morphism is finitely presented. On one such chart write the map as
$B_\lambda\to C_\lambda$ with $C_\lambda$ finitely presented over
$B_\lambda$. After tensoring with the colimit ring, the map
$B\to C$ is surjective. Choose finitely many algebra generators of
$C_\lambda$ over $B_\lambda$. Their images in $C$ have preimages in $B$;
choose representatives of those preimages at a common later stage. The
finitely many equations expressing each generator as such a preimage hold
at one further common stage by
[lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data]. Consequently the chart
map is surjective at that stage and at every later stage, hence a closed
immersion on the chart. Repeat for the finite affine chart list and take a
common upper bound. The chartwise closed immersions agree on overlaps (they
are base changes of the same map), so their images glue to a global closed
immersion. Base change of a finite-presentation morphism to a later stage
preserves finite presentation, and the same finite upper-bound argument
proves the assertion for every $\nu\geq\mu$.

attrs.title: Existence of a stage where a finite-presentation map is closed

objects.body:
Every $X_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y$ is of finite presentation, all
transitions are closed immersions, and the canonical map
$X\to\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

## Proof

Finite type of $\mathcal I_\alpha$ is equivalent to finite presentation of
$X_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y$, and each transition $X_\beta\to X_\alpha$ is a
closed immersion because its composite with the closed immersion
$X_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y$ is the closed immersion
$X_\beta\hookrightarrow Y$.

For the limit, the content is that $\mathcal I$ is the union of its finite
type subideals. We prove this by absolute Noetherian approximation of $Y$
rather than by the quasi-coherent extension theorem
([Tag 01PF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PF)): write
$Y=\varprojlim_j Y_j$ with $Y_j$ Noetherian and affine transition maps. An
affine open of $Y$ is the preimage of an affine open $V$ of some stage $Y_j$,
and a section of $\mathcal I$ over it comes from a section over $V$ at a
later stage; so we may assume it comes from $Y_j$. The ideal
$\mathcal K_j\subseteq\mathcal O_{Y_j}$ cutting out the scheme-theoretic
image of $X$ in $Y_j$ is of finite type, because a closed immersion into a
Noetherian scheme is of finite presentation, and its inverse image
$\mathcal K_j\cdot\mathcal O_Y$ is a finite type subideal of $\mathcal I$
containing the given section.

Finally, if $T$ is any scheme with compatible maps $T\to X_\alpha$, then the
induced map $T\to Y$ has $\mathcal I_\alpha$ in its kernel ideal for every
$\alpha$, hence has $\mathcal I$ in its kernel ideal by the exhaustion just
proved; so it factors uniquely through $X=V(\mathcal I)$ by the universal
property of closed immersions. This is exactly the limit property.

Each constructed map $X'_i\to X_i$ is a $U$-admissible blow-up. Each
$X'_i\to\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$ is an open immersion, their two copies of
$U$ agree, and $\mathsf{CM}(X_1,X_2;U)$ is separated and of finite type
over $S$.

## Proof

Apply Stacks Project, Tag 0F3X (Lemma 38.33.4), with the qcqs base $S$,
the common quasi-compact open $U$, and the separated finite-type
morphisms $X_i\to S$. The two input maps are open immersions and are
identified over $U$, so the hypotheses of that theorem are exactly the
hypotheses of the present construction. Its scheme-theoretic image
$X_{12}\subseteq X_1\times_SX_2$ is the object named in
[def-nagata-common-modification]; the two projections are the partial
sections used by
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section]. The theorem first
principalizes the two projection ideals and then takes their product
center, which is the map $X'_{12}\to X_{12}$ supplied by
[lemma-nagata-product-ideal-common-blowup]. Its strict-transform
comparison gives $X'_{12}\subseteq X'_i$ as an open subscheme, with both
restrictions identified with $U$; this is the extension step recorded by
[lemma-nagata-extend-admissible-blowup]. Consequently the two open
immersions glue along exactly $X'_{12}$, not merely along their underlying
topological intersection. The graph of this overlap is a closed immersion
because $X'_2\to S$ is separated. The composite
$X'_{12}\to X_1\times_SX_2$ is proper, and the product map from
$X'_1\times_SX'_2$ to $X_1\times_SX_2$ is separated; hence the graph map
is proper by
[lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target]. It is therefore closed,
so the two-open diagonal criterion
[lemma-nagata-separated-two-open-cover] proves that the glued scheme
is separated. The same theorem gives finite type, and the composition
statement
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp] shows that each projection is a
$U$-admissible blow-up.

The constructed factorization $C_{S'}$ is a compactification of
$X\times_SS'\to S'$.

## Proof

Open immersions, quasi-compact morphisms, and proper morphisms are stable
under arbitrary base change. The factorization equality follows from the
universal property of the two fibre products.

The subset $Z_{12,2}$ is dense in
$p_1^{-1}(\overline Z_{1,2})$.

## Proof

Choose an open neighbourhood $N\subseteq X_1$ of
$\overline Z_{1,2}$ over which $p_1$ is an isomorphism, as supplied by
[lemma-nagata-comparison-isiso-near-boundary]. Then
$p_1^{-1}(\overline Z_{1,2})$ lies in $p_1^{-1}(N)$, and the restriction

$$
p_1^{-1}(\overline Z_{1,2})\longrightarrow\overline Z_{1,2}
$$

is an isomorphism. By the definition of $Z_{12,2}$, its inverse image under
this isomorphism is $Z_{1,2}$. Since $Z_{1,2}$ is dense in its closure
$\overline Z_{1,2}$, the inverse image $Z_{12,2}$ is dense in
$p_1^{-1}(\overline Z_{1,2})$.

The constructed map $X_1^{\mathrm{cmp}}\to X_1^{\mathrm{old}}$ is
$V_1$-admissible, the transported $p_1$ is an isomorphism over an open
neighbourhood of $\overline Z_{1,2}$, and all previously established
boundary-disjointness relations still hold.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-comparison-restrict-proper-open], the restriction of
$p_1$ over $V_1$ is the base change
$V_1\times_UV_2\to V_1$ of $\psi_2$. The maximal isomorphism open $N_2$
contains $Z_2$ by [lemma-nagata-boundary-loci] and
[lemma-nagata-maximal-isomorphism-open]; hence $p_1$ is an
isomorphism over $\psi_1^{-1}(N_2)$, an open containing $Z_{1,2}$.

The subset $Z_{1,2}$ is closed in $V_1$, and $p_1$ is proper by
[lemma-nagata-comparison-projections-proper]. Therefore the property
of $\mathsf{IsoBl}_{V_1,Z_{1,2}}(p_1)$ gives the asserted isomorphism near
the closure. The new comparison scheme is the strict transform by
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-strict-transform]. Finally
[lemma-nagata-boundary-disjoint-persists] preserves every earlier
disjointness relation under this further $V_1$-admissible blow-up.

attrs.title: Properties of the improved first comparison projection

objects.body:
Both projections $p_i\colon X_{12}\to X_i$ are proper.

## Proof

Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] to
$V_{12}\to X_1\times_SX_2$. It gives the canonical closed immersion
$\iota_{12}\colon X_{12}\hookrightarrow X_1\times_SX_2$ occurring in
[def-nagata-two-open-comparison-space]. For
$\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, the morphism $X_j\to S$ is proper by
[lemma-nagata-prepared-boundaries]; hence the projection
$\pi_i\colon X_1\times_SX_2\to X_i$ is its proper base change. The
equality $p_i=\pi_i\circ\iota_{12}$ expresses $p_i$ as a composite of
proper morphisms, so $p_i$ is proper.

For $\{i,j\}=\{1,2\}$, the canonical morphism

$$
V_{12}=V_1\times_UV_2\longrightarrow p_i^{-1}(V_i)
$$

is an isomorphism. Under this identification,
$p_i^{-1}(V_i)\to V_i$ is the base change of
$\psi_j\colon V_j\to U$ along $\psi_i\colon V_i\to U$.

## Proof

Restrict the scheme-theoretic image defining $X_{12}$ to the open target
$V_i\times_SX_j\subseteq X_i\times_SX_j$. The inverse image of this
open in $V_{12}$ is all of $V_{12}$, so
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] identifies
$p_i^{-1}(V_i)$ with the scheme-theoretic image of

$$
V_{12}\longrightarrow V_i\times_SX_j.
$$

The map $V_{12}\to V_i\times_SV_j$ is the pullback of the diagonal
$U\to U\times_SU$; it is therefore a closed immersion because
$U\to S$ is separated. Composing with the open immersion
$V_i\times_SV_j\to V_i\times_SX_j$ shows that the displayed map is an
immersion. It is also proper: its composite to $V_i$ is the base change
of the proper morphism $\psi_j$, while
$V_i\times_SX_j\to V_i$ is separated; apply
[lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target]. A proper immersion is a
closed immersion, so
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion] identifies its
scheme-theoretic image with $V_{12}$ itself.
The first projection of the fibre square is the displayed map to $V_i$,
and its second component is the map to $V_j$. The universal property of
the fibre product gives the inverse identification with the base change of
$\psi_j$ along $\psi_i$, so the description of the projection is exactly
the one asserted.

attrs.title: Restriction of the comparison image over the proper-extension open

objects.body:
Let $A'$ be a valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$, and let
$A''$ be a valuation subring of the residue field
$k'=A'/\mathfrak m'$. The inverse image

$$
C=\{a\in A'\mid a\bmod\mathfrak m'\in A''\}
$$

is a valuation ring. Its fraction field is the fraction field of $A'$,
$\mathfrak m'\subseteq C$, and $C/\mathfrak m'\cong A''$.

## Proof

Let $x$ be a nonzero element of $\operatorname{Frac}(A')$. Since
$A'$ is a valuation ring, either $x\in A'$ or $x^{-1}\in A'$. If
exactly one lies in $A'$, that element lies in $C$ whenever its residue
is zero. If both are units of $A'$, compare their nonzero residue classes
in $k'$; the valuation-ring property of $A''$ puts one of the two
residues in $A''$, and hence puts $x$ or $x^{-1}$ in $C$. Thus
$C$ is a valuation ring. If $\mathfrak m'=0$, then $A'=k'$ is a field,
$C=A''$, and $\operatorname{Frac}(C)=k'=A'$. If
$\mathfrak m'\ne0$, choose $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m'$. For every $a\in A'$,
both $at$ and $t$ lie in $\mathfrak m'\subseteq C$, so
$a=(at)/t\in\operatorname{Frac}(C)$. Hence in this case also
$\operatorname{Frac}(C)=\operatorname{Frac}(A')$. The restricted residue
map $C\to A''$ is surjective by the inverse-image definition, and its
kernel is $\mathfrak m'$, giving $C/\mathfrak m'\cong A''$.

Under the hypotheses of
[def-nagata-composition-center-ideal], the ideal $\mathcal K(Z')$ is
finite type and

$$
|Y(Z')|=|V(\mathcal I)|\cup b(|Z'|).
$$

## Proof

Write $S=b(|Z'|)$ and $\mathcal J=\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^d$ as in
the definition. The module $\mathcal F$ is finite type, and the product of
the finite-type ideals $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$ is finite type. If
$x\notin V(\mathcal I)\cup S$, then $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and
the first blow-up is an isomorphism near $x$ by
[thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]; the defining equation
$\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A/\mathcal F\mathcal A)=Z'$ is empty there.
On the degree-one chart this says $\mathcal F_x=\mathcal I_x^d=\mathcal O_{X,x}$,
hence $\mathcal K_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Thus
$V(\mathcal K)\subseteq V(\mathcal I)\cup S$.

Conversely, $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal I$ gives
$V(\mathcal I)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$. If $x\in S\setminus V(\mathcal I)$,
then $b$ is an isomorphism near $x$, and the standard chart calculation for
$\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A/\mathcal F\mathcal A)$ identifies
$x\in S$ with $\mathcal F_x\ne\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Since
$\mathcal I_x^d=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, this gives
$\mathcal K_x=\mathcal F_x\ne\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so
$x\in V(\mathcal K)$. Both inclusions follow, and therefore
$|Y(Z')|=|V(\mathcal I)|\cup b(|Z'|)$.

attrs.title: Support of the constructed composition center

objects.body:
Under the hypotheses of
[def-nagata-composition-center-ideal], let $E$ be the exceptional
divisor of the first blow-up, write $\mathcal I_E$ for its invertible ideal,
and let $\mathcal I_{Z'}$ define the second center. On $X'$ one has

$$
b^{-1}\mathcal J\,\mathcal O_{X'}
=\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}.
$$

## Proof

Let $D_+(at)=\operatorname{Spec}(R_a)$ be a standard chart of the first
blow-up, where $R_a=A[\mathcal I/a]$ and $a\in\mathcal I$. The extended
ideal of $\mathcal J$ is, by definition, the image of $\mathcal J$ in
$R_a$. The equation
$Z'=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A/\mathcal F\mathcal A)$ says that its
ideal on this chart is generated by all fractions $f/a^d$ with
$f\in\mathcal F$ (and their $R_a$-multiples). The chart calculation for
the exceptional ideal gives $\mathcal I_E R_a=(a)$. Therefore, for every
generator $f\in\mathcal F$,

$$
f=a^d\,(f/a^d)\quad\text{in }R_a,
$$

and hence
$(\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X'})R_a=(a)^d\,\mathcal I_{Z'}R_a$.
This proves the asserted equality on every standard chart. On the overlap
of the $a$- and $c$-charts one has
$f/a^d=(c/a)^d(f/c^d)$ and $(a)^d=(a/c)^d(c)^d$; the two products are
literally the same ideal after localization. The standard charts cover
$X'$, so equality of the quasi-coherent ideals glues to
$b^{-1}\mathcal J\,\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}$.

attrs.title: Comparison of the two second-center ideals

objects.body:
Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be affine, let $U\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open and let $f\colon U\to\mathbb A^n_X$ be an $X$-morphism.
There is a finite type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $X$ with
$V(\mathcal I)\subseteq X\setminus U$, so that
$\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ is a $U$-admissible
blow-up, together with an open subscheme $W\subseteq\widetilde X$ containing
the inverse image of $U$ and an $X$-morphism
$\widetilde f\colon W\to\mathbb A^n_X$ extending $f$, whose graph

$$
\Gamma_{\widetilde f}\hookrightarrow
\widetilde X\times_X\mathbb A^n_X
$$

is closed. That is, $(W,\widetilde f)$ is a quasi-domination of
$\widetilde X$ over $\mathbb A^n_X$ extending $f$.

No density hypothesis on $U$ is needed here; when $U$ is dense in $X$, the
open $W$ is automatically dense in $\widetilde X$ by
[lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup].

## Proof

Since $U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact we may cover $U$ by finitely
many basic opens $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{u_i})$, $1\le i\le m$; then the
finitely generated ideal $(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ cuts out $X\setminus U$. The
$X$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{u_i})\to\mathbb A^n_X$ corresponds to
an $A$-algebra map

$$
A[t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1}]\to A_{u_i},\qquad t_j\mapsto g_{ij}/u_i^N
$$

with $g_{ij}\in A$ and $N$ large (one $N$ for all $i,j$). Agreement on the
overlaps $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{u_iu_{i'}})$ says that for some large $M$,
$(u_iu_{i'})^M(u_i^Ng_{i'j}-u_{i'}^Ng_{ij})=0$ in $A$. Replacing $g_{ij}$ by
$u_i^Mg_{ij}$ and $N$ by $N+M$ we may assume

$$
u_i^Ng_{i'j}=u_{i'}^Ng_{ij}\quad\text{for all }i,i',j,
$$

and we call this common element $g_{i,i',j}=g_{i',i,j}\in A$; note
$g_{i,i,j}=u_i^Ng_{ij}$.

Let $I\subseteq A$ be the ideal generated by all $u_i^N$ and all
$g_{i,i',j}$, and let $\mathcal I$ be the associated quasi-coherent ideal
sheaf; it is of finite type. Since $I\subseteq(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ we get
$V(\mathcal I)\subseteq X\setminus U$, and $\mathcal I$ restricts to the unit
ideal on $U$ because $u_i^N$ is invertible on
$\operatorname{Spec}(A_{u_i})$; so $\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ is a $U$-admissible blow-up.

Write $\mathbb P^n_X=\operatorname{Proj}(A[T_0,\ldots,T_n])$. The affine
charts $\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/u_i^N])$ and
$\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/g_{i,i',j}])$ cover $\widetilde X$ by
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. Define $X$-morphisms on them
by

$$
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[I/u_i^N]\bigr)\to
\mathbb A^n_X=D_+(T_n),\qquad
T_j/T_n\mapsto g_{i,i,j}/(u_i^N)^2,
$$

$$
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[I/g_{i,i',j}]\bigr)\to D_+(T_j),\qquad
T_r/T_j\mapsto g_{i,i',r}/g_{i,i',j}\ (r\le n-1),\quad
T_n/T_j\mapsto u_i^Nu_{i'}^N/g_{i,i',j}.
$$

All displayed fractions lie in the relevant chart algebra because their
numerators lie in $I$. Repeated use of the relation
$u_i^Ng_{i'j}=u_{i'}^Ng_{ij}$ checks that these maps agree on overlaps, so
they glue to an $X$-morphism $\widetilde f\colon\widetilde X\to \mathbb P^n_X$. On $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{u_i})\subseteq U$ the first
formula reads $T_j/T_n\mapsto g_{ij}/u_i^N$, so $\widetilde f$ extends $f$.

For the last sentence: $\mathbb P^n_X\to X$ is separated, so the graph
$\Gamma_{\widetilde f}\subseteq\widetilde X\times_X\mathbb P^n_X$ is closed.
Taking $W=\widetilde f^{-1}(\mathbb A^n_X)$, which is an open subscheme of
$\widetilde X$ containing the inverse image of $U$, the intersection
$\Gamma_{\widetilde f|_W}=\Gamma_{\widetilde f}\cap(\widetilde X\times_X \mathbb A^n_X)$ is closed in $\widetilde X\times_X\mathbb A^n_X$, which is
the quasi-domination condition of
[def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination].

attrs.title: Extension to $\mathbb A^n$ after one admissible blow-up, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U,V\subseteq X$ be open, let $p\colon Y\to X$ be a
morphism and let $f\colon U\to Y$ be a section of $p$ over $U$. Let
$q\colon X'\to X$ be a $V$-admissible blow-up, write $p'\colon Y\times_XX'\to X'$ for the base change of $p$ and $f'\colon q^{-1}(U)\to Y\times_XX'$ for the
base change of $f$. If the conclusion of
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] holds for the data
$(X',q^{-1}(U),q^{-1}(V),p',f')$, then it holds for $(X,U,V,p,f)$.

## Proof

Let $X''\to X'$ be a $q^{-1}(V)$-admissible blow-up solving the problem
upstairs. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp] the composite
$X''\to X'\to X$ is again a $V$-admissible blow-up of $X$: there is a
$V$-admissible centre $K$ on $X$ and an isomorphism
$X''\cong\operatorname{Bl}_K(X)$ over $X$. The conclusion of the theorem
depends on the blow-up only through its total space over $X$, so it suffices
to produce it for $X''\to X$. The extension of $f$ is the extension of $f'$
followed by the projection $Y\times_XX'\to Y$; that it is a section of $p$ and
extends $f$ follows from the two projection formulas defining $f'$. For the
closedness of the graph, the square exhibiting $Y\times_XX''$ as
$(Y\times_XX')\times_{X'}X''$ is cartesian, and the two graphs correspond
under the resulting isomorphism.

attrs.title: Reduction by base change along an admissible blow-up

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open
subschemes, let $p\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism with $Y$ qcqs, and let
$f\colon U\to Y$ be a section of $p$ over $U$ whose image is closed in
$p^{-1}(V)$. There is a $V$-admissible blow-up
$q\colon\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ such that, after
base change along $q$, the closure of the image of $f$ is disjoint from the
part lying over $\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)}$.

## Proof

We produce the two centres required by
[lemma-nagata-conrad-disjointness-blowup], applied with $Z=Y$, with the
open immersions $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$, and with $f(U)=\Gamma_f$ in the
role of the scheme lying over $U$.

Let $\mathcal H$ be the ideal of the reduced structure on the closed subset
$\overline{V\setminus U}$, so $V(\mathcal H)=\overline{V\setminus U}$; since
$V\setminus U$ is closed in $V$, its closure misses $U$. Give $X\setminus V$
a finite type closed subscheme structure $V(\mathcal K)$ using
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists].

We first check $p\bigl(p^{-1}(V(\mathcal H^2))\cap\overline{f(U)}\bigr) \subseteq X\setminus V$ as sets. Indeed a point of the left-hand side lies
in $\overline{V\setminus U}$, and if it lay in $V$ then, $f(U)$ being closed
in $p^{-1}(V)$, the point of $\overline{f(U)}$ above it would lie in $f(U)$
and so map into $U$, which is disjoint from $\overline{V\setminus U}$. As
$\mathcal K$ is of finite type,
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-power-in-ideal] gives an $n$ with

$$
\mathcal K^n\cdot\mathcal O_Y\subseteq
\mathcal H^2\cdot\mathcal O_Y+\mathcal I_{\overline{f(U)}} .
$$

The ideal $\mathcal H$ need not be of finite type. By
[lemma-nagata-ideal-directed-union-finite-type] it is the directed
supremum of its finite type quasi-coherent subideals $\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}$;
products and inverse images of ideals commute with directed suprema, so
$\mathcal H^2\cdot\mathcal O_Y+\mathcal I_{\overline{f(U)}}$ is the directed
supremum of the $\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}^2\cdot\mathcal O_Y+ \mathcal I_{\overline{f(U)}}$, and
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-compact] applied to the finite type
ideal $(\mathcal K\cdot\mathcal O_Y)^n$ produces an $\alpha$ with

$$
\mathcal K^n\cdot\mathcal O_Y\subseteq
\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}^2\cdot\mathcal O_Y+\mathcal I_{\overline{f(U)}} .
$$

Now take $\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}$ and
$\mathcal I_2=\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}^2+\mathcal K^n$, so that
$T_2=V(\mathcal I_2)=T_1\cap V(\mathcal K^n)$ is disjoint from $V$, and
$\mathcal I=\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2$. The centre $\mathcal I$ is of finite
type and $V(\mathcal I)\subseteq V(\mathcal I_2)\subseteq X\setminus V$, so
the blow-up is $V$-admissible; the containment
$\overline{V\setminus U}=V(\mathcal H)\subseteq V(\mathcal I_{1,\alpha})$
holds because $\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal H$, the scheme $f(U)$
lies over $U$ because $f$ is a section of $p$, and the displayed containment
is hypothesis (3) of [def-nagata-conrad-disjointness-setup]. So
[lemma-nagata-conrad-disjointness-blowup] applies and gives the
assertion.

(Conrad additionally arranges $\mathcal I_{1,\alpha}|_U=\mathcal O_U$; this
is not needed here, because $V(\mathcal I)\subseteq V(\mathcal K^n)$ is
already disjoint from $V$, hence from $U$.)

Let $U\subseteq V$ be open subschemes of a scheme $X$ with $U$ quasi-compact,
and let $S\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact subset disjoint from
$\overline{V\setminus U}$. There is a quasi-compact open subscheme
$X^{\circ}\subseteq X$ with $S\subseteq X^{\circ}$, $U\subseteq X^{\circ}$
and $X^{\circ}\cap V=U$.

## Proof

Since $V\setminus U$ is closed in $V$ we have
$\overline{V\setminus U}\cap V=V\setminus U$; in particular the open set
$W=X\setminus\overline{V\setminus U}$ contains $U$ and satisfies
$W\cap V=U$. It contains $S$ by hypothesis, so $S\cup U$ is a quasi-compact
subset of $W$. The underlying space of a scheme has a basis of quasi-compact
opens, so $S\cup U$ is contained in a quasi-compact open
$X^{\circ}\subseteq W$. Then $X^{\circ}\cap V\subseteq W\cap V=U$ and
$U\subseteq X^{\circ}\cap V$, so $X^{\circ}\cap V=U$.

Let $i\colon Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion of $X$-schemes and
suppose the section $f\colon U\to Y$ factors as $f=i\circ f'$ through $Y'$.
If the conclusion of [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] holds for the data
$(X,U,V,Y'\to X,f')$, then it holds for $(X,U,V,p,f)$, with the same
admissible blow-up and the same open subscheme of it.

## Proof

The extension of $f$ is the extension $g\colon W\to Y'$ of $f'$ followed by
$i$; it is a section of $p$ over $W$ and extends $f$ because $i$ is a
morphism over $X$. The comparison morphism
$Y'\times_XX'\to Y\times_XX'$ is a base change of $i$, hence again a closed
immersion, and the graph of $i\circ g$ is the image of the graph of $g$ under
it. A closed immersion is a closed map, so that image is closed.

attrs.title: Reduction to a closed subscheme of the target

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense quasi-compact open and let
$\pi\colon\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ be a
$U$-admissible blow-up. Then $U$, viewed as an open subscheme of
$\widetilde X$ via [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], is
topologically dense in $\widetilde X$. If moreover
$V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$, then $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in
$\widetilde X$.

## Proof

Write $\mathcal I'=\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$, a finite type
invertible ideal by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Its
complement $\widetilde X\setminus V(\mathcal I')$ is a quasi-compact open
subscheme, and $\pi$ restricts over it to an isomorphism onto
$X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement].
An invertible ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, so
$\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}\to j_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X\setminus V(\mathcal I')}$ is injective for the inclusion $j$ of that complement:
the complement is scheme-theoretically dense, hence topologically dense.
Since $\mathcal I$ is the unit ideal on $U$ we have
$U\subseteq X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, and $U$ is dense there because it is
dense in $X$. Density is transitive along the two displayed inclusions, so
$U$ is dense in $\widetilde X$.

If $V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$ then $X\setminus V(\mathcal I)=U$, so the
displayed scheme-theoretically dense complement *is* $U$.

In the situation of [def-nagata-conrad-disjointness-setup], the two
closed subsets

$$
\overline{Y'},\qquad
p'^{-1}\bigl(\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)}\bigr)
$$

of $Z'$ are disjoint. In words: after the base change by $q$, the closure
of the image of $Y$ in $Z$ no longer meets the part of $Z$ lying over the
closure of $V\setminus U$.

## Proof

Formation of topological closures commutes with restriction to an open
subspace, and by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] the same
holds for scheme-theoretic images of quasi-compact immersions. The
assertion is therefore local on $X$ and on $Z$, so we may assume
$X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. Put
$I_j=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I_j)$. We construct, locally on $X'$, a function on
$Z'$ which vanishes on $p'^{-1}(\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)})$ and equals
$1$ on $\overline{Y'}$.

*Step 1: the charts $U(s_2)$, $s_2\in I_2$, cover
$\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)}$.* The strict transform of $V(\mathcal I_1)$
is a closed subscheme of $X'$. Since $q$ is an isomorphism over $V$ we have
$q^{-1}(V\setminus U)\cong V\setminus U$ as topological spaces, and the
underlying space of $V(\mathcal I_1)$ contains $\overline{V\setminus U}$; so
$\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)}$ lies inside the strict transform of
$V(\mathcal I_1)$. By
[lemma-nagata-conrad-strict-transform-in-charts], applied to the two
centres $V(\mathcal I_1)$ and $V(\mathcal I_2)$, that strict transform is
covered by the charts $U(s_2)$ with $s_2\in I_2$.

*Step 2: reduction.* By Step 1 the opens $p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$, for
$s_2\in I_2$, cover $p'^{-1}(\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)})$, and

$$
p'^{-1}\bigl(\overline{q^{-1}(V\setminus U)}\bigr)
\subseteq p'^{-1}\bigl(q^{-1}(T_1)\bigr)
$$

because $\overline{V\setminus U}\subseteq V(\mathcal I_1)=T_1$ as sets. So
it suffices to prove, for every $s_2\in I_2$,

$$
p'^{-1}\bigl(q^{-1}(T_1)\bigr)\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))\cap\overline{Y'}
=\varnothing .
$$

*Step 3: an equation for $s_2$ on $\overline Y$.* By hypothesis (3) of
[def-nagata-conrad-disjointness-setup], $p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y$ is
a closed subscheme of $p^{-1}(T_2)$, so $p^{\#}(s_2)\in B$ vanishes on it.
Hence $p^{\#}(s_2)=t_1+g$ with $t_1$ vanishing on the closed subscheme
$p^{-1}(T_1)$, which is cut out by $I_1^2B$, and $g$ vanishing on
$\overline Y$. Write $t_1=\sum_ib_is_{1i}r_{1i}$ with $s_{1i},r_{1i}\in I_1$
and $b_i\in B$. Since $Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ is a schematically dense
open immersion, we get on $\overline Y$ the identity
$s_2=\sum_ib_is_{1i}r_{1i}$.

*Step 4: $s_2$ is a unit where it matters.* The scheme $Y$ lies over
$U\subseteq V$ and $V$ does not meet $T_2$, so

$$
Y'\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))
\subseteq p'^{-1}\bigl(U(s_2)\cap(X'\setminus q^{-1}(T_2))\bigr).
$$

On $U(s_2)\setminus q^{-1}(T_2)$ the section $s_2$ vanishes nowhere, hence is
a unit. Dividing the identity of Step 3 by $s_2$ therefore gives

$$
h:=\sum_ib_i\Bigl(\frac{s_{1i}}{s_2}\Bigr)r_{1i}=1
\qquad\text{on }Y'\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2)).
$$

Each $s_{1i}/s_2$ is a global section of $\mathcal O$ on the chart $U(s_2)$,
by the very definition of the chart algebra
([def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]), so $h$ is a global function on the
open subscheme $p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$ of $Z'$.

*Step 5: passing to the closure.* The immersion
$Y'\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))\to p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$ is quasi-compact, so $h=1$ on the
scheme-theoretic image $\overline{Y'\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))}$ as well
([def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]); and that image is
$\overline{Y'}\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$, because closures commute with
restriction to an open subscheme.

*Step 6: conclusion.* All the $r_{1i}$ lie in $I_1$, so $h$ vanishes on
$p'^{-1}(q^{-1}(V(\mathcal I_1)))\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$. Thus the single
function $h$ takes the value $1$ on
$\overline{Y'}\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$ and the value $0$ on
$p'^{-1}(q^{-1}(V(\mathcal I_1)))\cap p'^{-1}(U(s_2))$, so these two subsets
are disjoint. Since $V(\mathcal I_1)=V(\mathcal I_1^2)=T_1$ as sets, this is
exactly eq:nagata-conrad-disjointness-local.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact opens, let
$p\colon Y\to X$ be separated and locally of finite type with $Y$ qcqs, and
let $f\colon U\to Y$ be a section of $p$ over $U$ whose image is closed in
$p^{-1}(V)$. There is a $V$-admissible blow-up
$q\colon\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ with the
following property. Let $\sigma\colon U\hookrightarrow\widetilde X$ be the
canonical section of $q$ over $U$, let
$F=(f,\sigma)\colon U\to Y\times_X\widetilde X$ be the induced quasi-compact
immersion, and let $\overline{F(U)}$ be its scheme-theoretic image. Then

$$
\overline{F(U)}\longrightarrow\widetilde X
$$

is quasi-finite (locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type and
quasi-compact) and separated.

Neither $U$ nor $V$ is assumed dense in $X$.

## Proof

Choose a finite affine open cover $\{Z\}_{Z\in S}$ of $Y$ and fix one of its
members $Z$. Since $Z$ is affine it is quasi-affine, and the composite
$p_Z\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y\xrightarrow{p}X$ is quasi-compact because $Z$
is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated; so $p_Z$ is quasi-affine as a
morphism ([def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]). Put
$U_Z=U\cap f^{-1}(Z)$, an open of $X$ contained in $U$, hence in $V$, and
quasi-compact because $f$ is quasi-compact. The restriction
$f_Z\colon U_Z\to Z$ of $f$ is a section of $p_Z$ over $U_Z$, and its image
is the trace of $f(U)$ on $Z$, hence closed in $p_Z^{-1}(V)=Z\cap p^{-1}(V)$.

So [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general] applies to
$(U_Z\subseteq V, f_Z, p_Z)$ and produces a finite type quasi-coherent ideal
$\mathcal I_Z$ on $X$ with $V(\mathcal I_Z)\cap V=\varnothing$, an open
$W_Z\subseteq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Z}(X)$ containing the preimage of
$U_Z$, and an $X$-morphism $g_Z\colon W_Z\to Z$ extending $f_Z$ whose graph is
closed in $Z\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Z}(X)$.

*Unlike Conrad we do not replace $X$ by the scheme-theoretic image
$\overline{U_Z}$.* Conrad does so in order to make $U_Z$ dense, which his
quasi-affine case requires; the form of that case proved here
([lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general]) carries no density
hypothesis, so the reduction to the smaller base — and with it the
extension of $\mathcal I_Z$ from $\overline{U_Z}$ back to $X$ and the
ambient closedness of the strict transform — is unnecessary.

Put $\mathcal I=\prod_{Z\in S}\mathcal I_Z$; it is of finite type and
$V(\mathcal I)=\bigcup_ZV(\mathcal I_Z)$ misses $V$, so
$q\colon\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ is a
$V$-admissible blow-up. For each $Z\in S$ the inverse image of
$\mathcal I_Z$ on $\widetilde X$ is a factor of the invertible ideal
$\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$, hence invertible
([lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor]), so the universal property of
blowing up ([thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property]) provides a
comparison $c_Z\colon\widetilde X\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Z}(X)$ over
$X$.

Write $\Omega_Z=\mathrm{pr}_Y^{-1}(Z)\subseteq Y\times_X\widetilde X$, an open
subscheme, and let $\Phi_Z$ be the graph of
$c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)\to W_Z\xrightarrow{g_Z}Z$, a morphism
$c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)\to Y\times_X\widetilde X$ landing in $\Omega_Z$ and satisfying
$\mathrm{pr}_{\widetilde X}\circ\Phi_Z=\iota_{c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)}$. Two things
hold.

1. *$\Phi_Z$ is injective over $\widetilde X$*: this is immediate
from $\mathrm{pr}_{\widetilde X}\circ\Phi_Z=\iota_{c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)}$.
1. *The range of $\Phi_Z$ is closed in $\Omega_Z$*: indeed
$\Omega_Z=Z\times_X\widetilde X$ and
$c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)=W_Z\times_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Z}(X)}\widetilde X$,
so $\Phi_Z$ is the base change of the closed graph of $g_Z$ along
$\Omega_Z\to Z\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Z}(X)$, and the range
of a base change is the inverse image of the range.

Finally, $F(U)\cap\Omega_Z$ is contained in the range of $\Phi_Z$: a point of
it is $F(u)$ with $f(u)\in Z$, so $u\in U_Z$, and there $\sigma$ lands in
$c_Z^{-1}(W_Z)$ and $g_Z$ agrees with $f$. As $\Omega_Z$ is open,
$\overline{F(U)}\cap\Omega_Z$ is the closure of $F(U)\cap\Omega_Z$ inside
$\Omega_Z$, which by (2) is again contained in the range of $\Phi_Z$. The
$\Omega_Z$ cover $Y\times_X\widetilde X$, so the underlying space of
$\overline{F(U)}$ is covered by the finitely many sets $\Phi_Z(c_Z^{-1}(W_Z))$,
each injective over $\widetilde X$ by (1); hence the fibres of
$\overline{F(U)}\to\widetilde X$ are finite. Being locally of finite type
(as a closed immersion followed by a base change of $p$), the morphism is
therefore locally quasi-finite. It is quasi-compact because
$\overline{F(U)}$ is quasi-compact and $\widetilde X$ quasi-separated, and
separated because $p$ is.

attrs.title: The closed graph is quasi-finite over the blow-up, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: quasi-dominations are not
introduced in Lean. The extension statements are proved directly from
scheme-theoretic dominance and separatedness, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated`.

Let $Y\to S$ be separated and let $f\colon U\to Y$ be any $S$-morphism.
Then $(U,f)$ is a quasi-domination of $U$ over $Y$.

## Proof

Take $X=U$ in [def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination]. The open
subscheme $U\subseteq U$ is dense, and the closedness condition asks that
$\Gamma_f$ be closed in $U\times_SY$, which is the separatedness of
$Y\to S$.

attrs.title: A morphism on a dense open of a separated target is a quasi-domination of that open, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be affine, let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open, let
$p\colon Y\to X$ be quasi-affine and of finite type, and let $f\colon U\to Y$
be an $X$-morphism. There is a $U$-admissible blow-up
$\widetilde X\to X$ in which $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense, together with
a quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde f)$ of $\widetilde X$ over $Y$ extending
$f$.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists] there are
an $n$ and a quasi-compact immersion $i\colon Y\to\mathbb A^n_X$ over $X$.
Put $F=i\circ f\colon U\to\mathbb A^n_X$. By
[lemma-nagata-conrad-affine-space-extension] there is a $U$-admissible
blow-up $\widetilde X_0\to X$ carrying a quasi-domination
$(\widetilde W_0,\widetilde F_0)$ of $\widetilde X_0$ over $\mathbb A^n_X$
extending $F$.

Next make $U$ scheme-theoretically dense. By
[lemma-nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup] there is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $\widetilde X\to\widetilde X_0$ in which $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense, and by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp] the composite
$\widetilde X\to X$ is again a $U$-admissible blow-up. Let $\widetilde W$ be
the preimage of $\widetilde W_0$ and $\widetilde F$ the composite; the graph
$\Gamma_{\widetilde F}$ is the base change of $\Gamma_{\widetilde F_0}$ and
hence still closed in $\widetilde X\times_X\mathbb A^n_X$.

Because $i$ is an immersion there is an open subscheme
$U'\subseteq\mathbb A^n_X$ such that $i$ factors as a closed immersion
$j\colon Y\hookrightarrow U'$. Put $W=\widetilde F^{-1}(U')$. It is an open
subscheme of $\widetilde X$ containing $U$, hence scheme-theoretically dense
in $\widetilde X$ and containing $U$ as a scheme-theoretically dense open.
Moreover $\Gamma_{\widetilde F|_W} =\Gamma_{\widetilde F}\cap(\widetilde X\times_XU')$ is closed in
$\widetilde X\times_XU'$.

We claim that $\widetilde F|_W$ factors as $j\circ\widetilde f$ for a
(necessarily unique) $\widetilde f\colon W\to Y$. Indeed, the pullback of
the closed immersion $j$ along $\widetilde F|_W$ is a closed subscheme of
$W$; it contains $U$ as an open subscheme, because
$\widetilde F|_U=F=j\circ f$ factors through $Y$. Since $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $W$, the only closed subscheme of $W$
containing $U$ as an open subscheme is $W$ itself, so the pullback is $W$
and the factorization exists.

Then $\widetilde f|_U=f$, and $\Gamma_{\widetilde f} =(1_{\widetilde X}\times j)^{-1}(\Gamma_{\widetilde F|_W})$ is closed in
$\widetilde X\times_XY$. Thus $(W,\widetilde f)$ is the required
quasi-domination.

attrs.title: Quasi-affine target over an affine base, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open, let
$p\colon Y\to X$ be separated, quasi-affine and locally of finite type, and
let $f\colon U\to Y$ be an $X$-morphism. There is a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $X$ with
$V(\mathcal I)\subseteq X\setminus U$ such that
$\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ carries a quasi-domination
of $\widetilde X$ over $Y$ extending $f$, and such that the inverse image of
$U$ in $\widetilde X$ is scheme-theoretically dense.

As in [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base], $U$ need not be
assumed dense in $X$: the centre constructed below cuts out exactly the
boundary $X\setminus U$, so the inverse image of $U$ becomes
scheme-theoretically dense in $\widetilde X$ in any case.

## Proof

Choose a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i=0}^nW_i$ and put
$U_i=U\cap W_i$, a quasi-compact open of $W_i$, and $Y_i=p^{-1}(W_i)$,
quasi-affine and locally of finite type over $W_i$. Let
$f_i\colon U_i\to Y_i$ be the restriction of $f$.

By [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base] there is, for each
$i$, a finite type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_i$ on $W_i$ with
$V(\mathcal I_i)\subseteq W_i\setminus U_i$, an open
$T_i\subseteq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(W_i)$ containing the inverse
image of $U_i$, and a $W_i$-morphism $g_i\colon T_i\to Y_i$ extending $f_i$
whose graph is closed in
$Y_i\times_{W_i}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(W_i)$.

*Extending the centres.* By
[lemma-nagata-extend-admissible-blowup] each $\mathcal I_i$ extends to a
finite type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J_i$ on $X$ with
$V(\mathcal J_i)\cap U=\varnothing$ whose blow-up restricts over $W_i$ to
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(W_i)$, and does so as a cartesian square.

*The blow-up.* By
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] there is a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K$ on $X$ with $V(\mathcal K)=X\setminus U$.
Set $\mathcal I=\mathcal K\cdot\prod_i\mathcal J_i$, a finite type ideal with
$V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$ *exactly*, and let
$\pi\colon\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ be its
blow-up. Since $V(\mathcal I)=X\setminus U$, the second assertion of
[lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup] makes $\pi^{-1}(U)$
scheme-theoretically dense in $\widetilde X$, hence also topologically
dense; this is the last assertion of the lemma.

Each $\mathcal J_i$ divides $\mathcal I$, so its inverse image on
$\widetilde X$ is an invertible factor of the invertible ideal
$\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$ and is therefore itself
invertible. The universal property of blowing up
([thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property]) then gives a canonical
$X$-morphism $\pi_i\colon\widetilde X\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}(X)$.
Restricting $\pi_i$ over $W_i$ and using the cartesian square of the
previous paragraph, we obtain a $W_i$-morphism
$\rho_i\colon\pi^{-1}(W_i)\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}(W_i)$.

Put $T_i'=\rho_i^{-1}(T_i)\subseteq\pi^{-1}(W_i)$, an open subscheme of
$\widetilde X$ containing $\pi^{-1}(U\cap W_i)$, and let
$\overline f_i\colon T_i'\to Y$ be the composite of $\rho_i|_{T_i'}$, $g_i$
and $Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$. The graph $\Gamma_i$ of $\overline f_i$ is a
base change of the graph of $g_i$ along the comparison morphism of the two
fibre products, hence a closed immersion; so $\Gamma_i$ is closed in the part
$(Y\times_X\widetilde X)|_{W_i}$ of $Y\times_X\widetilde X$ lying over
$W_i$.

*Gluing.* Let $T=\bigcup_iT_i'$, an open subscheme of $\widetilde X$
containing $\bigcup_i\pi^{-1}(U\cap W_i)=\pi^{-1}(U)$. The $X$-morphisms
$\overline f_i$ agree on overlaps: the open $\pi^{-1}(U)\cap T_i'\cap T_j'$
is scheme-theoretically dense in $T_i'\cap T_j'$, both morphisms agree with
$f$ on it, and $Y\to X$ is separated, so
[lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] makes them
agree on $T_i'\cap T_j'$. They therefore glue to an $X$-morphism
$\overline f\colon T\to Y$ extending $f$.

*Closedness of the graph.* The graph $\Gamma_{\overline f}$ is the
union of the $\Gamma_i$, and closedness may be checked on the open cover of
$Y\times_X\widetilde X$ by the parts lying over the $W_i$. So it suffices to
prove that the local extension loci are pairwise compatible:

$$
T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)\subseteq T_i'\qquad\text{for all }i,j,
$$

for then $\Gamma_{\overline f}\cap(Y\times_X\widetilde X)|_{W_i}=\Gamma_i$,
which is closed there. (This step is not formal: a priori
$\overline f_j$ could be defined at points of $\pi^{-1}(W_i)$ where
$\overline f_i$ is not.)

Fix $i$ and $j$ and put $N=\pi^{-1}(U\cap W_i)\cap T_j'$. The two morphisms
$\overline f_i$ and $\overline f_j$ agree on $N$, both being restrictions of
$f$ there, so $\Gamma_j|_N=\Gamma_i|_N$ and in particular
$\Gamma_j(N)\subseteq\Gamma_i$. Since $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is topologically dense
in $\widetilde X$ and $T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)$ is open, $N$ is dense in
$T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)$; as $\Gamma_j$ is continuous,
$\Gamma_j\bigl(T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)\bigr)$ lies in the closure of
$\Gamma_j(N)$. Intersecting with the open
$(Y\times_X\widetilde X)|_{W_i}$, in which $\Gamma_i$ is closed, gives
$\Gamma_j\bigl(T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)\bigr)\subseteq\Gamma_i$. Projecting to
$\widetilde X$ and using that a graph maps isomorphically to its domain
yields $T_j'\cap\pi^{-1}(W_i)\subseteq T_i'$, as claimed.

Hence $(T,\overline f)$ is a quasi-domination of $\widetilde X$ over $Y$
extending $f$.

attrs.title: Quasi-affine target over a qcqs base, $U=V$, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open
subschemes, let $Y$ be qcqs and let $p\colon Y\to X$ be separated,
quasi-affine and locally of finite type. Let $f\colon U\to Y$ be an
$X$-morphism whose image is closed in $p^{-1}(V)$. There is a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $X$ with
$V(\mathcal I)\subseteq X\setminus V$ such that
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ carries a quasi-domination over $Y$
extending $f$.

Neither $U$ nor $V$ needs to be assumed dense in $X$. The only density used
below is that of the inverse image of $U$ in the blow-up of the smaller base
$X^{\circ}$ of Step 2, and that is exactly the scheme-theoretic density which
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-equal-opens] hands back. Note also
that the centre is only required to avoid the *larger* open $V$, which
is what makes this statement stronger than
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-equal-opens] rather than a special
case of it.

## Proof

*Step 1: separating $p(\overline{f(U)})$ from $\overline{V\setminus U}$.*
[lemma-nagata-conrad-case3-disjointness-reduction] gives a $V$-admissible
blow-up $\pi_1\colon X_1\to X$ such that, writing
$p_1\colon Y_1=Y\times_XX_1\to X_1$ for the base change of $p$ and
$f_1\colon\pi_1^{-1}(U)\to Y_1$ for the induced section, the closure of
$f_1\bigl(\pi_1^{-1}(U)\bigr)$ is disjoint from
$p_1^{-1}\bigl(\overline{\pi_1^{-1}(V\setminus U)}\bigr)$.

*Step 2: passing to a smaller base.* The closure of
$f_1\bigl(\pi_1^{-1}(U)\bigr)$ is quasi-compact, so its image under $p_1$ is a
quasi-compact subset of $X_1$, and Step 1 makes it disjoint from
$\overline{\pi_1^{-1}(V\setminus U)}$. So
[lemma-nagata-conrad-case3-smaller-base] applies over $X_1$ and produces a
quasi-compact open $X^{\circ}\subseteq X_1$ containing both
$p_1\bigl(\overline{f_1(U)}\bigr)$ and $\pi_1^{-1}(U)$, with
$X^{\circ}\cap\pi_1^{-1}(V)=\pi_1^{-1}(U)$. From now on we work over $X_1$
and write $U$, $V$, $Y$, $p$, $f$ for their inverse images and base changes
there.

*Step 3: applying Case 2.* Put $Y^{\circ}=p_1^{-1}(X^{\circ})$. The
morphism $Y^{\circ}\to X^{\circ}$ is separated, locally of finite type and
quasi-affine: quasi-affineness of a morphism is stable under base change
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom.of_isPullback`) and under
restricting the base to an open subscheme. Since $X^{\circ}\cap V=U$,
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-equal-opens] applies over $X^{\circ}$
with the single open $U$: there is a finite type quasi-coherent ideal
$\mathcal I^{\circ}$ on $X^{\circ}$ with
$V(\mathcal I^{\circ})\subseteq X^{\circ}\setminus U$, an open
$W^{\circ}\subseteq\widetilde X^{\circ}= \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I^{\circ}}(X^{\circ})$ containing the inverse
image of $U$, and an $X^{\circ}$-morphism $g^{\circ}\colon W^{\circ}\to Y^{\circ}$ extending $f$ whose graph is closed in
$Y^{\circ}\times_{X^{\circ}}\widetilde X^{\circ}$; moreover the inverse image
of $U$ in $\widetilde X^{\circ}$ is scheme-theoretically dense.

Note that it is *not* necessary to replace $Y^{\circ}$ by the
scheme-theoretic image of $f$ here, as [ConradNagata] does. That
replacement is only used to make the graph closed in Step 5, and for that
purpose the closed *subset* $\overline{f_1(U)}$ of $Y_1$ suffices.

*Step 4: descending the centre to $X_1$.* Since
$V(\mathcal I^{\circ})\subseteq X^{\circ}\setminus U= X^{\circ}\setminus(X^{\circ}\cap V)$, the centre $\mathcal I^{\circ}$ is
disjoint from $X^{\circ}\cap V$, so
[lemma-nagata-extend-admissible-blowup] extends it to a $V$-admissible
finite type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_2$ on $X_1$ whose blow-up
$\pi_2\colon\widetilde X_1\to X_1$ restricts over $X^{\circ}$ to
$\widetilde X^{\circ}$, cartesianly. Transporting $(W^{\circ},g^{\circ})$
along that cartesian square — this is the same transport lemma as in the
proof of [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-equal-opens] — gives an open
$W\subseteq\pi_2^{-1}(X^{\circ})\subseteq\widetilde X_1$ containing
$\pi_2^{-1}\bigl(\pi_1^{-1}(U)\bigr)$ and an $X_1$-morphism $G\colon W\to Y_1$ extending $f_1$, whose graph is closed in the part of
$Y_1\times_{X_1}\widetilde X_1$ lying over $X^{\circ}$.

*Step 5: the graph is closed.* Write $\Gamma\subseteq Y_1\times_{X_1}\widetilde X_1$ for the graph of $G$ and put
$N=\mathrm{pr}_{Y_1}^{-1}\bigl(\overline{f_1(U)}\bigr)$, a closed subset.
The inverse image of $U$ is topologically dense in $\widetilde X^{\circ}$,
by the scheme-theoretic density of Step 3, hence also in the open subscheme
$W$; as $G$ agrees with $f_1$ there, continuity gives
$G(W)\subseteq\overline{f_1(U)}$ and therefore $\Gamma\subseteq N$. On the
other hand $p_1\bigl(\overline{f_1(U)}\bigr)\subseteq X^{\circ}$ by the
choice of $X^{\circ}$, so $N$ is contained in the open part of
$Y_1\times_{X_1}\widetilde X_1$ lying over $X^{\circ}$. A subset of a closed
set contained in an open set is closed as soon as it is closed in that open
set; so $\Gamma$ is closed in $Y_1\times_{X_1}\widetilde X_1$.

*Conclusion.* The composite of the $V$-admissible blow-up
$\pi_1$ of $X$ and the $\pi_1^{-1}(V)$-admissible blow-up $\pi_2$ of $X_1$ is
a $V$-admissible blow-up of $X$ by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp]: there is a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $X$ with
$V(\mathcal I)\cap V=\varnothing$ and an $X$-isomorphism
$\widetilde X_1\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Transporting $(W,G)$
along it, and composing $G$ with $Y_1\to Y$, gives the required
quasi-domination of $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ over $Y$ extending
$f$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: quasi-dominations are not
introduced in Lean. The extension statements are proved directly from
scheme-theoretic dominance and separatedness, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_of_isSeparated`.

Let $Y\to S$ be proper and let $(U,f)$ be a quasi-domination of $X$ over
$Y$. Then $U=X$; that is, $f$ extends to an $S$-morphism $X\to Y$.

## Proof

The projection $X\times_SY\to X$ is proper, being a base change of
$Y\to S$. The graph $\Gamma_f$ is a closed subscheme of $X\times_SY$ by
hypothesis, so its image in $X$ is closed. That image is $U$, because
$\Gamma_f\to U$ is an isomorphism. Thus $U$ is a closed subset of $X$
which is also dense and open, so $U=X$. Under the resulting isomorphism
$\Gamma_f\cong X$ the second projection is the desired extension.

attrs.title: A quasi-domination over a proper target is everywhere defined, [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
Let $X$ be qcqs and let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open. There is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $X_1\to X$ in which $U$ is scheme-theoretically
dense. If $U$ is dense in $X$ and $\widetilde X\to X$ is any $U$-admissible
blow-up, the same applies to $\widetilde X$, and the composite
$X_1\to\widetilde X\to X$ is again a $U$-admissible blow-up of $X$.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] there is a finite
type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_0\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with
$V(\mathcal I_0)=X\setminus U$. Its blow-up is $U$-admissible, and $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in it by the second assertion of
[lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup]. Applying this to
$\widetilde X$ in place of $X$ — legitimate because the preserved open of
a $U$-admissible blow-up is again quasi-compact — and composing,
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp] identifies the composite with a
single $U$-admissible blow-up of $X$.

attrs.title: An admissible blow-up making the open scheme-theoretically dense

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: Deligne's disjointness blow-up
is formalized as the single statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup`,
which absorbs this step.

Let $X$ be a scheme and let $Y,Y'\subseteq X$ be closed subschemes with
quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I_Y,\mathcal I_{Y'}$. In
$\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_Y+\mathcal I_{Y'}}(X)$ the strict
transform $\widetilde Y$ of $Y$ is contained in the union of the charts
$U(s)$, taken over all local sections $s$ of $\mathcal I_{Y'}$ on all affine
opens of $X$.

Consequently, if $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ are closed subschemes of $X$ and
$\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\sum_j\mathcal I_{Y_j}}(X)$, then the strict
transforms satisfy $\bigcap_j\widetilde Y_j=\varnothing$.

## Proof

Both assertions are local on $X$, so let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and put
$I=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I_Y)$ and $J=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I_{Y'})$. The charts
$U(s)$ for $s\in I\cup J$ cover $\widetilde X$ by
[prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], since such elements generate
$I+J$. It therefore suffices to prove that $U(s)$ is disjoint from
$\widetilde Y$ for every $s\in I$. On the chart $U(s)$ the strict transform
of $Y=V(I)$ is cut out by the saturation of $I\cdot A[(I+J)/s]$ with respect
to $s$, that is, by

$$
I_s\cap A[(I+J)/s]
$$

formed inside $A_s$
([lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-closed]). Because $s\in I$ the
element $1=s/s$ lies in that ideal, so the ideal is the unit ideal and the
overlap of $U(s)$ with $\widetilde Y$ is empty.

For the second assertion put $I_j=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I_{Y_j})$. The centre
is $\sum_jI_j$, so the charts $U(s)$ for $s\in\bigcup_jI_j$ cover
$\widetilde X$. Fix such an $s$, say $s\in I_1$. The computation just made,
with $I=I_1$ and $J=I_2+\cdots+I_n$, shows $U(s)\cap\widetilde Y_1 =\varnothing$. Hence every point of $\widetilde X$ misses at least one
$\widetilde Y_j$, and the intersection of all of them is empty.

attrs.title: Strict transforms live in the charts of the other centre (Deligne, *Lemme* 0.2), [ConradNagata]

objects.body:
The ideal $\mathcal J_U(T)$ is finite type and quasi-coherent, and its
vanishing set is exactly $T$.

## Proof

An open constructible subset of a spectral space is quasi-compact. Apply
[lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal] to $W=U\setminus T$; its
vanishing set is $U\setminus W=T$.

The $U_i$ form a finite affine open cover of $X$, and $D_X$ is dense in
$X$.

## Proof

The selected witness is supplied by
[lemma-nagata-dense-affine-cover-exists]. Its specification fields say
that the family is finite, consists of affine opens, covers $X$, and has
dense total intersection.

attrs.title: Properties of the selected dense affine cover

objects.body:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and assume that it has finitely
many irreducible components, with generic points
$\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$. There is a finite affine open cover
$(U_1,\ldots,U_n)$ whose total intersection is dense in $X$.

## Proof

For every $x\in X$, apply
[lemma-nagata-affine-neighbourhood-generic-points] to obtain an affine
open containing $x$ and every $\eta_i$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite
subcover. Its total intersection contains the generic point of every
irreducible component, and is therefore dense.

attrs.title: Existence of a finite affine cover with dense total intersection

objects.body:
For an open immersion $j$ (no quasi-compactness is needed), the density
condition in
[def-nagata-dense-compactification] is equivalent to the assertion that
the image inclusion
$j_{\mathrm{im}}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(j)\to\overline X$ is an
isomorphism. Under the resulting identification
$\operatorname{SIm}(j)\cong\overline X$, the factor map
$j^{\mathrm{im}}$ identifies with the original open immersion $j$; in
general, $j^{\mathrm{im}}$ is not an isomorphism.

## Proof

The kernel of $\mathcal O_{\overline X}\to j_*\mathcal O_X$ is the ideal
defining $\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ by
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. It is zero exactly when the
closed immersion $\operatorname{SIm}(j)\hookrightarrow\overline X$ is an
isomorphism, by
`Scheme.isIso_subschemeι_iff_eq_bot`. Finally,
`Scheme.Hom.toImage_imageι` identifies the composite of the factor
map with this inclusion with $j$. This transports $j^{\mathrm{im}}$ to
$j$ when the inclusion is inverted; it does not make the factor map an
isomorphism.

Let $h\colon U\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated with
scheme-theoretic image $X$, and let
$q\colon P\to X$ be flat. Then

$$
U\times_XP\longrightarrow P
$$

has scheme-theoretic image $P$.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-flat-base-change], the scheme-theoretic
image after pullback is canonically the pullback of the scheme-theoretic
image of $h$. By hypothesis that image is $X$, and its pullback along
$P\to X$ is the identity closed subscheme of $P$. Thus the base-changed
morphism is scheme-theoretically dense in $P$.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the Raynaud–Gruson flattening
chain is not formalized. Elimination of indeterminacy is obtained instead
by the route of the chapter *Elimination of indeterminacy after Deligne
and Conrad*, whose output is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`.

Let $q\colon Z\to X$ be flat and locally of finite type, and let $U\subseteq X$
be retrocompact and scheme-theoretically dense. If $q_U$ is locally of
finite presentation and has fibre dimension at most $e$, then $q$ is locally
of finite presentation and every fibre of $q$ has dimension at most $e$.

## Proof

Apply Stacks Project, Tag 081P (Lemma 38.11.2), to $q$ and the
retrocompact scheme-theoretically dense open $U$. The hypotheses are the
flatness and locally-finite-type assumptions in the statement together with
the assumed local finite presentation of $q_U$; the conclusion is that $q$
is locally of finite presentation. With this conclusion established,
apply Tag 081L (Lemma 38.11.3) to the same $q$, $U$, and the integer $e$.
Its relative-dimension hypothesis is precisely the stated bound on
$q_U$, and it concludes that every fibre of $q$ has dimension at most $e$.
Both conclusions are local on source and target, so the affine instances
supplied by the two cited lemmas glue to the assertions above.

Let $f\colon X\to S$ be quasi-compact and let
$h\colon U\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
and assume $h(U)$ is dense in $X$. Suppose that for every valuation
ring $A$ with fraction field $K$, every commutative diagram

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(K)\longrightarrow U\longrightarrow X,
\qquad
\operatorname{Spec}(A)\longrightarrow S
$$

has a unique lift $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X$. Then $f$ is
universally closed. If $f$ is quasi-separated, it is also separated.

The maps in $\mathsf{VP}(h,z)$ form a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Spec}(K'_{h,z})&\xrightarrow{\eta_{h,z}}&T\\
\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow h\\
\operatorname{Spec}(A'_{h,z})&\xrightarrow{\alpha_{h,z}}&P,
\end{array}
$$

and the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A'_{h,z})$ maps to $z$.

## Proof

These are exactly the fields of the witness selected in
[def-nagata-dense-valuation-probe]; nonemptiness is
[lemma-nagata-dense-valuation-probe-exists].

Let $h\colon T\to P$ be quasi-compact, assume its image
inclusion $\operatorname{SIm}(h)\hookrightarrow P$ is an isomorphism, assume
$P$ is affine, and let $z\in P$. There
exist a valuation ring $A'$ with fraction field $K'$, a morphism
$\eta\colon\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to T$, and a morphism
$\alpha\colon\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to P$ such that the generic square
commutes and the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ maps to $z$.

## Proof

Let $Z=\operatorname{SIm}(h)$. The assumed image isomorphism identifies
$z$ with a point of $Z$. Stacks Project, Tag 02JQ (Lemma 29.6.5),
applied to the quasi-compact morphism $h$ and the point $z\in Z$, supplies
a valuation ring $A'$, its fraction field $K'$, a map
$\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to T$, and a map
$\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to Z$ whose generic restriction is the supplied
map and whose closed point is $z$. Composing the latter map with the image
closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow P$ gives $\alpha$, and the generic
commutativity supplied by the theorem is exactly the displayed square.

attrs.title: Existence of a valuation probe through a dense source

objects.body:
For $X_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ and $S\to S_\lambda$, the base change of
$\Delta_{X_\lambda/S_\lambda}$ is canonically identified with
$\Delta_{X_\lambda\times_{S_\lambda}S/S}$.

## Proof

Base change the defining fibre square of the diagonal. Associativity of
fibre products identifies the result with the map sending a point to its
pair with itself, which is the diagonal of the base-changed morphism.

If $f\colon X\to S$ is of finite presentation, then the diagonal
$\Delta_{X/S}\colon X\to X\times_S X$ is of finite presentation.

## Proof

On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq S$, choose a finite
presentation
$B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ for an affine chart
$\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq X$. The corresponding chart of
$X\times_SX$ has ring $B\otimes_A B$, and the diagonal is represented by the
multiplication map

$$
\mu\colon B\otimes_A B\longrightarrow B,\qquad b\otimes b'\longmapsto bb'.
$$

This map is surjective, and its kernel is generated by the finite list
$x_i\otimes1-1\otimes x_i$. Hence $B$ is finitely presented as a
$(B\otimes_A B)$-algebra. Finite presentation is local on source and
target for immersions; a finite affine cover of the diagonal therefore
glues these chart calculations to $\Delta_{X/S}$.

Let $X=U\cup V$ be an open cover over $S$. The pullback of
$\Delta_{X/S}$ to $U\times_SV$ is canonically the map

$$
U\cap V\longrightarrow U\times_SV.
$$

The analogous assertion holds over $V\times_SU$.

## Proof

Both schemes represent triples consisting of a point of $U$, a point of
$V$, and an equality of their images in $X$. The canonical isomorphism is
obtained from the universal property of the pullback.

attrs.title: The diagonal on a mixed open

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Every $i\in F$ satisfies $i\leq u(F)$.

## Proof

Induct on $F$. The empty case is vacuous. At an insertion step, the
selected $d(u(F),i)$ bounds both $u(F)$ and $i$; transitivity and the
induction hypothesis prove the assertion for all old and new elements.

attrs.title: Property of the selected finite upper bound

objects.body:
Every effective Cartier ideal is invertible as an ideal sheaf.

## Proof

The regular local generator gives an isomorphism from the structure sheaf
to the ideal on each member of the defining cover. On overlaps the two
generators differ by a unit, so these local rank-one bases glue.

attrs.title: An effective Cartier ideal is invertible

objects.body:
The morphism $X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)\to X$ is $U$-admissible, and the
constructed strict-transform projection
$q^{\mathrm{el}}\colon Z^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)\to X^{\mathrm{el}}(q,U)$ is
an open immersion.

This is exactly the formalised statement: the identification of the
restriction of $q^{\mathrm{el}}$ over $U$ with the original chosen
isomorphism $q^{-1}(U)\cong U$ is *not* asserted here, because it is
already supplied to every consumer by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement], which identifies the
part of any strict transform lying over the preserved open with the ordinary
base change.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-flattening-ideal], the selected ideal is finite type,
is the unit ideal on $U$, and has open strict-transform projection. The
first two properties make its blow-up $U$-admissible; the last property and
the selected comparison over $U$ identifies the restriction of
$q^{\mathrm{el}}$ with $e_U$, so the named construction has exactly the
open-immersion and prescribed-over-$U$ fields asserted above.

Let $s\colon Y\to Z$ be separated and let $f,g\colon T\to Y$ satisfy
$s\circ f=s\circ g$. If $\iota\colon W\to T$ is scheme-theoretically
dominant and $f\circ\iota=g\circ\iota$, then $f=g$. In particular two
$Z$-morphisms $T\to Y$ into a separated $Z$-scheme $Y$ that agree on a
scheme-theoretically dense open of $T$ are equal.

No reducedness of $T$ is needed: this is the scheme-theoretic analogue of the
classical statement for a dominant $\iota$ and reduced $T$.

## Proof

Passing to $Z$-schemes, the equalizer $E$ of $f$ and $g$ maps to $T$ by a
closed immersion $e$ because $s$ is separated. As $f\circ\iota=g\circ\iota$,
the morphism $\iota$ factors as $\iota=e\circ l$, so the kernel ideal of $e$
is contained in that of $\iota$, which is trivial by scheme-theoretic
dominance. A closed immersion with trivial kernel is an isomorphism, hence
$e$ is an epimorphism and $f=g$ follows from $f\circ e=g\circ e$.

attrs.title: Morphisms into a separated target agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dominant subscheme

objects.body:
The constructed morphism
$\mathsf{ExtBl}_{X,W,U}(\mathcal J)\to X$ is $U$-admissible, and its
restriction to $W$ is canonically the given blow-up
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(W)\to W$.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-extend-finite-type-ideal], the ideal
$\mathcal I_X(\mathcal J)$ is finite type, restricts to $\mathcal J$ on
$W$, and restricts to the unit ideal on $U$. Its blow-up is therefore
$U$-admissible. The open immersion $W\to X$ is flat, so
[thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identifies the pullback of the
constructed blow-up with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(W)$. On an
affine chart, that comparison is induced degreewise by the canonical map
from the pullback of the Rees algebra to the Rees algebra of the restricted
ideal; it sends every standard chart generator to itself. Hence the local
comparisons commute with restriction to basic overlaps and glue to the
stated canonical isomorphism. Over $U\cap W$ both ideals are the unit
ideal, so the same formula is the selected identity of the two trivial
blow-ups. This also verifies compatibility with the chosen admissibility
isomorphism.

attrs.title: Property of the extended admissible blow-up, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
The sheaf $\operatorname{Ext}_{X,W}(\mathcal J)$ is a finite type
quasi-coherent ideal on $X$, and its restriction to $W$ is
$\mathcal J$.

## Proof

The selected ideal is required to have these two properties in
[def-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension]; the witness type is nonempty
by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension-exists].

On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/a])$ of the affine blow-up, the
extended ideal of $I$ is the ideal generated by the image of $I$ in
$A[I/a]$.

## Proof

This is the affine calculation for the image defining
[def-nagata-extended-ideal].

attrs.title: Extended ideal on an affine blow-up chart

objects.body:
For every ring homomorphism $B\to K$ with $K$ a field, there is a
polynomial $B$-algebra $P$ and a surjective $B$-algebra map $P\to K$.
The structural map $B\to P$ is flat.

## Proof

Take the polynomial algebra over $B$ on variables indexed by the underlying
set of $K$ and evaluate the variable indexed by $k$ at $k$. Evaluation is
surjective. This polynomial algebra is a filtered colimit of free
polynomial algebras on finite variable sets, and is therefore flat over
$B$.

attrs.title: A field-valued point has a flat polynomial presentation

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the finite-presentation and
Noetherian descent is done in one step by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation`, so
this stage-by-stage bookkeeping is never carried out.

Let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of rings with colimit $A$. Given
finitely many elements of $A$ and finitely many equalities between ring
expressions in those elements, there exists one stage $i$ and lifts of all
selected elements to $A_i$ for which all selected equalities hold. Once
they hold at $i$, they hold after every transition $A_i\to A_j$.

## Proof

Choose a representative stage for each selected element. Directedness and
[lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] place all representatives at
one common stage. Equality of two representatives in a filtered colimit is
witnessed at a later stage. There are only finitely many equalities, so a
second finite upper bound makes them all true simultaneously. Ring
homomorphisms preserve the equalities at every later stage.
