attrs.title: Lifting étale morphisms along a closed immersion

objects.body:
Throughout the chapter we fix the following data.

- A coefficient category $\mathcal A$, abelian and Grothendieck abelian,
on which $\mathcal A$-valued presheaves on every site of size $u+1$ admit
a left exact sheafification (in Lean the class
`CategoryTheory.HasSmallSiteSheafify`; the small étale sites and
their localizations are of that size). Mathematically this holds for
every Grothendieck abelian $\mathcal A$ of size $u+1$; in Lean it is so
far available only for those concrete over $\mathrm{Type}\,(u+1)$ whose
forgetful functor preserves limits and filtered colimits of that size and
reflects isomorphisms, such as $\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$, see
[rmk-openclosed-universes].
For the two conservativity statements
[lemma-openclosed-point-ulift] and
[prop-openclosed-conservative] we ask in addition that $\mathcal A$
be concrete in the sense recalled in
[rmk-openclosed-universes]; the case of interest,
$\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ for the coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of
the $\ell$-adic formalism, satisfies this.
- A scheme $X$. For a scheme $Y$ we write $\et Y$ for its small étale
site: the objects are the schemes étale over $Y$, the morphisms are
the $Y$-morphisms, and the topology is generated by the jointly
surjective families. We write $\shv{\et Y}$ for the category of
$\mathcal A$-valued sheaves on it.
- A morphism of schemes $g\colon Y'\to Y$ induces an adjunction
$g^*\dashv g_*$ between $\shv{\et Y}$ and $\shv{\et{Y'}}$, with
$$
(g_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(V\times_YY')
\qquad(V\in\et Y).
$$
Here $g_*$ is left exact and $g^*$ is exact. If $g$ is an open
immersion then $g^*$ has in addition a left adjoint $g_!$, the
extension by zero, which is exact, and the unit
$\mathrm{id}\to g^*g_!$ is an isomorphism.
- An open immersion $j\colon U\to X$ and a closed immersion
$i\colon Z\to X$ such that
$$
\operatorname{range}(i)=X\smallsetminus\operatorname{range}(j).
$$
We call such a pair $(j,i)$ a *complementary pair* on $X$. Only
the disjointness of the two ranges is used before
[lemma-openclosed-point-factors]; the covering half of the
condition enters exactly once, in
[lemma-openclosed-point-factors].

For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\et X$ we write

$$
\alpha_{\mathcal F}\colon j_!j^*\mathcal F\to\mathcal F,
\qquad
\beta_{\mathcal F}\colon\mathcal F\to i_*i^*\mathcal F
$$

for the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$. These are
the two maps of [thm-openclosed-exact]; no other map is constructed in
this chapter.

The first two statements say that a sheaf pushed forward from $Z$ has no
sections over $U$, and that everything formal follows from this.
Let $E$ be a field of characteristic zero.

objects.body:
Fix an integer $q>1$ and let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero; the case of interest is an abstract algebraic closure of
$\Qell$. Where the sketch article measures the size of a scalar through a
*universal complex-realization field* and its complex realizations, that
field and its realizations are replaced here by $\Qbar\subseteq\mathbf C$ and
the conjugates of the scalar, because
`AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis` of
`Comparator/Weil/Definitions.lean` speaks about complex roots.

Purity under a single embedding would not suffice here: the reciprocal roots
of $R$ of one prescribed absolute value need not form a conjugation-stable
family, and the factor they cut out need not be rational, which is why
[def-zla-universal-purity] tests every conjugate.

For the rest of this section fix $r\geq0$ and polynomials
$P_i(T)\in\Omega[T]$, $0\leq i\leq r$, with $P_i(0)=1$, and put

$$
O(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq r\\ i\text{ odd}}}P_i(T),
\qquad
E(T)=\prod_{\substack{0\leq i\leq r\\ i\text{ even}}}P_i(T).
$$

objects.body:
The formal proof
(`separationBlowup_disjoint_strictTransforms`) blows up the sum
$\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2$ directly on $X$
(`separationBlowup`) and proves disjointness of the strict
transforms chart-locally, using the chart inclusion
$D_+(b_1+b_2)\subseteq D_+(b_1)\cup D_+(b_2)$ for degree-one sections
$b_i$ coming from $\mathcal I_i$. The Tag 080P preparation inside
$Z=V(\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2)$
([lemma-nagata-separate-closed-data-exists]) and
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-nil-ideal-nilpotent] are not formalized.

A sheaf in the detailed chapters is a sheaf on the *small* étale site of
a scheme $X$, with values in a coefficient category $A$. In Lean this is
`Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A`; the small étale topology is mathlib's
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology`, and its objects are the
schemes étale over $X$. Sheaves are formed on this site and on no other:
the pro-étale site and the fpqc site do not occur in the Lean development at
all. Where an étale cover of $X$ is needed — to say that a sheaf is
locally constant, for instance — it is taken to be a cover in the big
étale precoverage `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etalePrecoverage`, that
is, a jointly surjective family of étale maps $U_i\to X$; this names the
covering families, and no sheaf is ever formed on the big site.

The coefficient category $A$ is not a fixed category in Lean but a parameter,
required to be Grothendieck abelian and, following the convention of the
`SixFunctors` folder, to have $\operatorname{Hom}$-types in the universe
$u+1$, one above the universe $u$ of the base schemes. Predicates involving
finiteness require $A$ to be moreover concrete, finiteness referring to the
underlying type. This convention is stated in the module docstrings of

- `WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/UpperLowerStar/Etale.lean`, which
constructs the pushforward $g_*$ and the pullback $g^*$ between
categories of sheaves on small étale sites, together with the
adjunction $g^*\dashv g_*$, the composition isomorphisms and the
exactness statements; and
- `WeilConjectures/ConstructibleSheaf/Defs.lean`, which defines
the locally constant, finite, finite locally constant and
constructible sheaves on the small étale site.

Both files record that the Grothendieck abelian generality is what supplies
sheafification and the left Kan extensions along base change used to define
$g^*$, and that some of those existence statements are, with current mathlib,
sorried instances rather than proved ones — the small étale site is not
known to be essentially small, only the small affine étale site is. This is
a limitation of the ambient library, not a mathematical hypothesis of the
theory.

No structured gap markers remain. The two former API obligations are
recorded above as explicit interface lemmas whose proofs name the current
Mathlib declarations and isolate the remaining finite-data packaging work.

Fix a complete discrete valuation ring $\Lambda$ with maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m$, put $\Lambda_n=\Lambda/\mathfrak m^n$ for $n\geq1$, and
assume that $\ell$ is invertible on every scheme under consideration. All
schemes in the ordinary finite-level statement are noetherian and
finite-dimensional. The functors are first formed in the ambient derived
categories and are restricted to constructible objects only through the
separately named constructibility inputs.

The coefficient ring of the $\ell$-adic formalism is denoted $\Lambda$, and the
case the detailed chapters are written for is the *finite torsion* one:
$\Lambda=\Lambda_n=\mathbb Z/\ell^n\mathbb Z$, so that $A$ is `ModuleCat`
$\Lambda$, the category of $\Lambda$-modules. This is the instantiation named in the
docstring of `WeilConjectures/ConstructibleSheaf/Defs.lean`, both for
the coefficient category and for the constructibility predicate, and it is the
level at which every statement in the following chapters is to be read. The
chapter on proper base change fixes a complete discrete valuation ring
$\Lambda$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and writes
$\Lambda_n=\Lambda/\mathfrak m^n$; the finite levels $\Lambda_n$ are the finite
torsion rings above, and it is the finite-level statements that correspond to
the Lean code.

Where a chapter needs $\ell$ to be invertible, that is an assumption on the
schemes considered, not a change of coefficients.

objects.body:
In Lean the two conclusions are split into
`ValuativeCriterion.universallyClosed_of_isDominant` and
`ValuativeCriterion.isSeparated_of_isDominant`; both are fully
proved. The ingredients — the valuation probe
(Tag 02JQ, `nonempty_valuationProbe`), the
composite valuation ring (`ValuationSubring.comapResidue`), the
intersection lemma (Tag 052K,
`ValuationSubring.comap_eq_of_le_comap`) and the extension lemma
(Tag 00IA, `ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq`, via
Mathlib's Chevalley extension theorem rather than the Zorn argument) — live
in the `WeilConjectures.Mathlib` helper files. The formalized proof
deviates from the Stacks Project text in two reductions: instead of
replacing $U,X,S$ by their reductions, the morphism $h$ is factored through
its scheme-theoretic image — the factor map `Scheme.Hom.toImage` is
scheme-theoretically dominant with no reducedness hypothesis, and the
valuative data factors through the image because $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a
valuation ring or of a field is reduced
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.le_ker_of_range_subset_support`); and the
polynomial presentation of
[lemma-nagata-field-point-polynomial-presentation] is inlined via
`MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom`. The flat-pullback and reduced-density
inputs ([lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback],
[lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic]) are provided by Mathlib's
`IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant` API.

## Proof

We first verify the existence part of the valuative criterion for $f$.
Start with an arbitrary square

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(K)\longrightarrow X,
\qquad
\operatorname{Spec}(A)\longrightarrow S.
$$

Valuation rings and fields are reduced, so replacing $U,X,S$ by their
reductions does not change this lifting problem. After this replacement,
topological density of $h(U)$ says that the scheme-theoretic image of
$h$ is all of $X$ by
[lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic]. We may also replace
$S$ by an affine open through
which $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to S$ factors; write it as
$\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

Choose an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(B)\subseteq X$ through which
the generic map factors. Choose the polynomial $B$-algebra $P$ and
surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow K$ from
[lemma-nagata-field-point-polynomial-presentation]. The map
$\operatorname{Spec}(P)\to X$ is flat. Therefore

$$
U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(P)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(P)
$$

is scheme-theoretically dense by
[lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback].

Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-valuation-probe] to the point
$\operatorname{Spec}(K)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(P)$. We obtain a
valuation ring $A'$, with fraction field $K'$, whose generic point maps
to $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(P)$ and whose closed point maps to the
chosen $K$-point of $\operatorname{Spec}(P)$. If
$k'=A'/\mathfrak m_{A'}$, this gives a field embedding
$K\to k'$. Choose a valuation ring $A''\subseteq k'$ dominating the
image of $A$, with fraction field $k'$, by
[lemma-nagata-valuation-ring-extension].

Form the inverse-image ring

$$
C=\{a\in A'\mid a\bmod\mathfrak m_{A'}\in A''\}.
$$

By [lemma-nagata-composite-valuation-ring], $C$ is a valuation ring
with fraction field $K'$, and $C/\mathfrak m_{A'}=A''$. Since
$A''$ contains the image of $A$, the map $R\to A'$ factors through
$C$. Thus the generic map
$\operatorname{Spec}(K')\to U$ and the map
$\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to S$ form a diagram covered by the hypothesis.
Let $g_C\colon\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to X$ be its unique lift.

There are now two maps $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to X$: one is obtained
from $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to\operatorname{Spec}(P)\to X$, and the
other by composing $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to\operatorname{Spec}(C)$
with $g_C$. They have the same generic map through $U$ and the same
composite to $S$. Applying the assumed uniqueness to the valuation ring
$A'$ shows that the two maps are equal.

Restrict $g_C$ along the closed immersion
$\operatorname{Spec}(A'')\to\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ induced by
$C/\mathfrak m_{A'}\cong A''$. Its generic point is
$\operatorname{Spec}(k')$, the residue field of the prime
$\mathfrak m_{A'}\subset C$. The preceding equality on
$\operatorname{Spec}(A')$ identifies this generic map with the closed-point
residue map of $\operatorname{Spec}(A')\to X$ and hence with the base
change of the original $\operatorname{Spec}(K)\to X$. Let $x\in X$ be the image
of the closed point. The image of the induced local homomorphism
$\mathcal O_{X,x}\to A''$ lies in the subfield $K\subseteq k'$.
By [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection],
$K\cap A''=A$. Hence the local homomorphism factors through $A$, and
therefore defines the required lift $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X$.
The existence part of the valuative criterion now shows that $f$ is
universally closed.

Finally suppose $f$ is quasi-separated. Then its diagonal
$\Delta_f\colon X\to X\times_SX$ is quasi-compact. A map
$\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to X\times_SX$ is a pair of maps to $X$.
If their common generic restriction factors through $U$, the uniqueness
hypothesis for $f$ forces the pair to be equal, hence to factor uniquely
through $\Delta_f$. Applying the universally-closed part just proved to
$\Delta_f$ and $h\colon U\to X$ makes the diagonal universally closed.
Since every diagonal is an immersion, a universally closed diagonal is a
closed immersion. Thus $f$ is separated.

The case $U=V$ is the only one used in the applications, but the proof does
not go through if $U=V$ is imposed throughout. The extra flexibility is
needed in the general case of the proof of
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination]: there one restricts to
$X_i=\overline{U_i}$ for a piece $U_i=f^{-1}(Y_i)$ of $U$, and even when
$U=V$ to begin with, the open $V_i=X_i\cap V$ can be strictly larger than
$U_i$. This is why
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general] (Case 3) is stated for
$U\subseteq V$ and not only for $U=V$, and why
[lemma-nagata-conrad-disjointness-blowup] is needed to reduce Case 3 to

attrs.title: Why the theorem must allow $U\neq V$

objects.body:
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy] (Stacks Tag 081S) is
formalized along this chapter, not along the module-flattening chain
([lemma-nagata-finite-data-flattening-package] to
[lemma-nagata-dense-open-dimension-package]). The bridge is the
following argument, which uses no further input.

Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open and let
$q\colon Z\to X$ be separated and of finite type with a chosen isomorphism
$q^{-1}(U)\cong U$ over $U$.

1. By [lemma-nagata-conrad-schematically-dense-blowup], replace $X$
by the $U$-admissible blow-up along a finite type ideal with zero scheme
exactly $X\setminus U$, and $Z$ by its strict transform. The new $q$ is
still separated and of finite type and is still an isomorphism over $U$,
and now $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$; in particular the
density hypothesis of [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] holds. The
final centre is recombined with this one by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp].
1. Apply [thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] with $V=U$ and with $f$
the section $U\cong q^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow Z$: it produces a
$U$-admissible blow-up $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ and a
quasi-domination $(W,\widetilde f)$ of it over $Z$ extending $f$.
1. Enlarge the centre from $\mathcal I$ to $\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal I_0$
with $V(\mathcal I_0)=X\setminus U$, and let
$X'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal I_0}(X)$. By
[cor-nagata-blowup-product-common-refinement] it dominates
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, so $W$ pulls back to an open
$W'\subseteq X'$ containing $U$ and $\widetilde f$ pulls back to
$f'\colon W'\to Z$ with $\Gamma_{f'}$ closed in $X'\times_XZ$. Now
$X'\setminus V(\mathcal I\mathcal I_0)=U$, so $U$ is
scheme-theoretically dense in $X'$ and hence in $W'$.
1. The strict transform $Z'$ of $Z$ in $X'$ is, by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], the
scheme-theoretic closure of the part of $X'\times_XZ$ lying over
$X'\setminus V(\mathcal I\mathcal I_0)=U$, that is, the
scheme-theoretic closure of $\Gamma_f$. It is therefore contained in
the closed subscheme $\Gamma_{f'}\cong W'$. So $Z'$ is a closed
subscheme of $W'$ containing $U$ as a scheme-theoretically dense open
subscheme, whence $Z'=W'$ and $Z'\to X'$ is an open immersion.

This is exactly the conclusion of
[lemma-nagata-elimination-indeterminacy]. The two external inputs are
Zariski's Main Theorem, used once in the proof of
[thm-nagata-conrad-elimination] and available in Mathlib as
`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`, and the
immersion of a quasi-affine scheme into relative affine space (Stacks Tag
04II), used in [lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base] and
already formalized as
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_immersion_affineSpace_of_quasiAffine`.

The folder `blueprint/src/version/math/` contains a separate account of
the theory — the ``Route B'' proof spine, which starts from the presentable
category of solid pro-étale complexes and builds the six operations there,
taking the large theorems as black boxes. It is kept as background reading.
It is *not* the convention of this project: it uses a different site and

objects.body:
Throughout this section let $S$ be Noetherian, let $U\to S$ be separated and
of finite type, and fix an open cover $U=U_1\cup U_2$ such that
$U_1\cap U_2$ is dense in $U$. Assume each $U_i\to S$ is compactifiable.

Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$ be a separated morphism
of finite type. Then there are an integer $n\geq0$, a scheme $X'$ over $S$, a
morphism $\pi\colon X'\to X$ and an immersion $i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ of
$S$-schemes such that

1. $\pi$ is proper and surjective, and
1. there is a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ such that
$\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism.

The formalisation makes $X'$, the index set of the homogeneous coordinates of
the ambient projective space, $\pi$ and $i$ four separate definitions rather
than existentially bound data, so that a consumer gets properness, surjectivity
and the immersion property by typeclass inference; all four are read off a
single auxiliary choice, `ChowModification.data`. Following
[def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $\mathbf P^n_S$ is
$\mathbf P(N;S)$ for a finite type $N$ of homogeneous coordinates. Finally,
[lem-chow-graph] needs the covering of Step 1 to be nonempty; this costs
nothing, since $m=0$ happens only for $X$ empty, and one may then replace the
covering by the one-element covering $\{X^{*}\}$.

## Proof

By the standing facts of [sec-chow-conventions] the scheme $X$ is
noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components, and it is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

*Step 1: the cover.* By [lem-chow-affine-cover] there is a finite
affine open covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_m$ whose members all contain the
generic points of the irreducible components of $X$, and
$U:=U_1\cap\dots\cap U_m$ is a dense open subscheme of $X$.

*Step 2: reduction to $U$ scheme-theoretically dense.* Let
$X^{*}\subseteq X$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $U\to X$, as in
[lem-chow-scheme-theoretic-closure]. Then $X^{*}\to S$ is again separated
of finite type, $X^{*}=\bigcup_iU_i^{*}$ is a finite affine open covering with
$\bigcap_iU_i^{*}=U$, and $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $X^{*}$.
It suffices to produce, for $X^{*}$ with the covering $\{U_i^{*}\}$ and the
same open $U$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi^{*}\colon X'\to X^{*}$ and an
immersion $X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ such that $(\pi^{*})^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an
isomorphism; this is exactly what Steps 3–7 below construct. Indeed,
$X^{*}\to X$ is a surjective closed immersion, hence proper and surjective, and
it is an isomorphism over $U$; so $\pi:=(X^{*}\to X)\circ\pi^{*}$ is proper and
surjective, $U$ is a dense open subscheme of $X$, and
$\pi^{-1}(U)=(\pi^{*})^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. We may therefore
replace $X$ by $X^{*}$ and $U_i$ by $U_i^{*}$, and assume from now on that $U$
is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$.

*Step 3: the graph.* Apply [lem-chow-graph] to obtain immersions
$j_i\colon U_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_S$, their closed models $Z_i$, the
scheme-theoretic image $Z$ of $j=(j_1|_U,\dots,j_m|_U)$, the proper
projections $p_i\colon Z\to Z_i$, and the closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$.

*Step 4: the modification.* Put $V_i:=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and
$X':=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$. By [lem-chow-glue] the morphisms
$p_i|_{V_i}$ glue to $\pi\colon X'\to X$ with $\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$, and by
[lem-chow-preimage] we have $\pi^{-1}(U_i)=V_i$ with
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ proper.

*Step 5: $\pi$ is proper and surjective.* Properness is local on the
target by 01W2, and $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ is an open covering with
$\pi^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ proper; hence $\pi$ is proper. In particular
$\pi(X')\subseteq X$ is closed. It contains $U$ because
$\pi|_U=\mathrm{id}_U$, and $U$ is dense in $X$; therefore $\pi(X')=X$.

*Step 6: $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $U$.* Repeat the argument of
[lem-chow-preimage] with $U_i$ replaced by $U$: the identity
$U\to U$ is proper, $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is separated, so
01W6 shows that $U\to\pi^{-1}(U)$ is universally closed and
hence $U$ is closed in $\pi^{-1}(U)$; and $U$ is dense in the open subscheme
$\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq Z$. Thus $U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ and $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is the
identity.

*Step 7: the immersion.* Put $N=\prod_i(n_i+1)-1$. Composing the closed
immersion $Z\to\mathbf P^{n_1}_S\times_S\dots\times_S\mathbf P^{n_m}_S$ of
[lem-chow-graph](1) with the Segre embedding, which is a closed
immersion by [lem-chow-segre], gives a closed immersion
$Z\to\mathbf P^N_S$. The subscheme $X'\subseteq Z$ is open, so the composition
$i\colon X'\to\mathbf P^N_S$ is an immersion. Taking $n:=N$ completes the
proof.

Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$ with $\Lambda$ a finite ring. The
kernel and the cokernel of a morphism between constructible sheaves on
$\et X$, finite direct sums of constructible sheaves, and the middle term of
a short exact sequence whose outer terms are constructible, are
constructible. Consequently the constructible sheaves form a weak Serre
subcategory of $\shv{\et X}$. (The kernel and cokernel statements are
formalised, for any ring $\Lambda$, as are the instances
`IsClosedUnderKernels` and `IsClosedUnderCokernels` of
`Etale.constructibleSheaf`; the extension statement is not.)

## Proof

Let $\varphi\colon\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ be a morphism of constructible
sheaves. By [lemma-constructible-common-refinement] and
[lemma-constructible-of-refines] there is one stratification
$(\iota_k\colon Z_k\to X)_k$ such that all $\iota_k^*\mathcal F$ and
$\iota_k^*\mathcal F'$ are finite locally constant. Since $\iota_k^*$ is
exact, $\iota_k^*\ker\varphi=\ker(\iota_k^*\varphi)$ and
$\iota_k^*\operatorname{coker}\varphi=\operatorname{coker}(\iota_k^*\varphi)$
are finite locally constant by [lemma-constructible-flc-serre], so
$\ker\varphi$ and $\operatorname{coker}\varphi$ are constructible with
respect to the same stratification. The same argument, using exactness of
$\iota_k^*$ and the extension part of [lemma-constructible-flc-serre],
handles extensions, and [lemma-constructible-flc-biproduct] handles
finite direct sums. A full subcategory of an abelian category closed under
kernels, cokernels and extensions is a weak Serre subcategory.

attrs.title: Constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory

objects.body:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: blow-ups are never
base-changed along a flat morphism. Every base-change step the route takes
goes through the universal property
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_blowup` and
the chart pullback squares
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isPullback_blowup$\iota$`
instead.

The constructed comparison $\operatorname{bc}_g$ is an isomorphism over
$Y$.

## Proof

Relative Proj sends the graded equivalence of
[lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees] to an affine-local isomorphism.
Compatibility with degree zero identifies the structure maps, and the
localization cocycle glues the local isomorphisms.

If $\mathcal I$ is a finite type quasi-coherent ideal on $X$, then on
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)}$ is locally
principal, generated locally by a non-zero-divisor, and hence is an
invertible ideal defining an effective Cartier divisor.

## Proof

Work locally on an arbitrary affine open of $X$. Finite type of
$\mathcal I$ gives finitely many generators on that affine, and the
corresponding standard charts cover its blow-up. Use
[lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] and
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]. The local principal ideals
glue because their generators differ by units by
[lemma-nagata-chart-generators-associated].

The constructed maps $\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ and
$\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ are inverse over $X$. Thus the iterated
blow-up is identified with the blow-up of $\mathcal I\mathcal J$.

## Proof

Write $p\colon X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}\to X$ for the composite and
$q\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X)\to X$ for the
product blow-up. The construction of $\Phi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ is
the unique $X$-morphism whose pullback of the tautological invertible
quotient on the product blow-up is the product of the two tautological
quotients on $X_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$. Conversely, the construction of
$\Psi_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}$ first uses the invertible quotient
$q^*\mathcal I$ and then the invertible quotient of the pullback of
$\mathcal J$; their product is the tautological quotient of
$q^*(\mathcal I\mathcal J)$. Thus both composites are $X$-morphisms
pulling back the relevant tautological quotient to itself. Apply uniqueness
in [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] first for the product
blow-up to obtain $\Phi\circ\Psi=\mathrm{id}$. For the other composite,
first apply uniqueness for the $\mathcal I$-blow-up to see that its
projection to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ is the original first
projection. It is therefore a morphism over
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, and uniqueness for the second blow-up
gives $\Psi\circ\Phi=\mathrm{id}$.

Under the data of [def-nagata-blowup-universal-lift], the constructed
map $\widetilde f$ is the unique $X$-morphism from $Y$ to
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ inducing the chosen invertible
quotient. Thus the blow-up is final among such $X$-schemes.

## Proof

Existence is [lemma-nagata-blowup-universal-exists], and uniqueness
among $X$-morphisms inducing the specified quotient is
[lemma-nagata-blowup-universal-unique]. Together these are exactly the
asserted final-object property.

The explicitly constructed factorization
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Nag}}(f)$ is a compactification of $f$. In particular,
every separated finite type morphism to a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme is compactifiable.

## Proof

$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Nag}}(f)$ is the composition of two maps $j_f$ and $p_f$. The first map is a quasi-compact open immersion by
[lemma-nagata-final-open-immersion]; the second is proper by
[lemma-nagata-final-ambient-proper]; and their composite is $f$ by
[lemma-nagata-final-factorization]. These are exactly the fields of
[def-nagata-compactification]. Hence the named construction is a
compactification, and its existence witnesses compactifiability.

With $Z=V(\mathcal I)$ as above, the two constructed comparison maps are
inverse over $X$. Hence the
composite is the blow-up of the finite-presentation center
$Y(Z')=V(\mathcal K(Z'))\hookrightarrow X$, whose support satisfies

$$
|Y(Z')|=|Z|\cup b(|Z'|).
$$

## Proof

Put $X_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$ and
$\mathcal J'=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X_1}$. By the extended-ideal equality,
$\mathcal J'=\mathcal I_E^d\mathcal I_{Z'}$. The product-ideal comparison
[thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal] therefore gives an isomorphism over
$X$

$$
\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J'}(X_1)
\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal J}(X).
$$

Since $\mathcal I_E^d$ is invertible, the invertible-factor comparison
[lemma-nagata-blowup-invertible-factor] gives a canonical isomorphism
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_{Z'}}(X_1)\cong \operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J'}(X_1)$. Their composite is the map
$\Omega_{Z,Z'}$ in the definition; the reverse composite of the inverse
comparisons is the stated reverse map.

For completeness, these maps are the universal lifts for the same quotient:
on the iterated blow-up the product of the tautological invertible quotients
is the tautological quotient of $\mathcal I\mathcal J$, while on the
$\mathcal I\mathcal J$-blow-up its two factor quotients give the tautological
quotients for $\mathcal I$ and for $\mathcal J'$; multiplying by the inverse
of the local generator of $\mathcal I_E^d$ gives the quotient for
$\mathcal I_{Z'}$. Thus each composite is an $X$-morphism inducing the
original tautological quotient. Uniqueness in the blow-up universal
property, first over $X$ and then over $X_1$, makes both composites identities.
The center ideal $\mathcal K=\mathcal I\mathcal J$ is finite type, hence
defines a finite-presentation closed immersion, and
[lemma-nagata-composition-center-ideal] gives its support as
$|V(\mathcal I)|\cup b(|Z'|)$.

Let $S$ be qcqs and let $X$ and $Y$ be qcqs $S$-schemes with $Y\to S$
separated and of finite type. Let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be dense open
subschemes whose open immersions into $X$ are quasi-compact, and let $(U,f)$
be a quasi-domination of $V$ over $Y$ in the sense of
[def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination]. There exists a $V$-admissible
blow-up $\widetilde X\to X$ such that $\widetilde X$ quasi-dominates $Y$ in a
manner extending $f\colon U\to Y$.

## Proof

The morphism $f$ is automatically quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Replacing $Y$ by $Y\times_SX$ we may assume $X=S$; thus $p\colon Y\to X$ is
separated and of finite type and $f\colon U\to Y$ is a section of $p$ over
$U$ whose image is closed in the part of $Y$ lying over $V$.

If $p$ is quasi-affine, this is
[lemma-nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-general]. In general, let
$q\colon\widetilde X\to X$ be the $V$-admissible blow-up produced by
[lemma-nagata-conrad-graph-closure-quasi-finite] and let
$\overline{F(U)}\subseteq\widetilde X\times_XY$ be the scheme-theoretic image
of $F=(\sigma,f)$. That lemma makes
$\overline{F(U)}\to\widetilde X$ quasi-finite and separated, so
[lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite] makes it
quasi-affine as a morphism to $\widetilde X$. (Note that $\widetilde X$ is a
blow-up of a qcqs scheme and is not itself quasi-affine, so the absolute form
of quasi-affineness is not available here.)

By [lemma-nagata-conrad-blowup-base-change-reduction] we may base change
along the $V$-admissible blow-up $q$ without leaving the statement of the
theorem; [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup] keeps $U$ and
$V$ dense. After that base change the scheme-theoretic image
$\overline{f(U)}$ of $U$ in $Y$ is quasi-affine over the base, so
[lemma-nagata-conrad-closed-target-reduction] lets us replace $Y$ by
$\overline{f(U)}$, and we are reduced to the quasi-affine case already
treated.

Let $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$. The restriction

$$
b_{X,\mathcal I}^{-1}(U)\longrightarrow U
$$

is an isomorphism.

## Proof

Cover $X$ by affine opens. Under
[prop-nagata-global-blowup-affine-restrict], the restriction over each
affine is the affine complement isomorphism of
[lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-complement]. These local isomorphisms glue,
and isomorphisms are local on source and target.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: only properness of the global
blow-up is needed, and it is proved directly as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isProper_blowupMap`; the
global blow-up is never exhibited as a projective morphism.

If $\mathcal I$ is of finite type, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}\colon\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)\to X$ is
projective provided that $\mathcal I$ admits a finite global free
presentation, i.e. there are $r\in\mathbb N$ and a surjection
$q\colon\mathcal O_X^{r+1}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I$.

## Proof

The preceding lemma supplies a closed immersion into the single finite
projective space $\mathbf P^r_X$ required by
[def-nagata-projective-morphism]; its structural composite is
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$, so the morphism is projective. Without the displayed
global-generation hypothesis, finite type alone yields the properness
statement below but does not imply projectivity for this finite-projective-
space definition.

If $\mathcal I$ is of finite type, then
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is proper.

## Proof

Apply [lemma-nagata-global-blowup-proper-local] to the affine open cover
of $X$. Each restricted morphism is proper, and
[lemma-nagata-projective-target-local] is the verified target-local
properness lemma (despite its historical label). It follows that
$b_{X,\mathcal I}$ is proper. This argument does not use the unresolved
global projectivity theorem.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the Raynaud–Gruson flattening
chain is not formalized. Elimination of indeterminacy is obtained instead
by the route of the chapter *Elimination of indeterminacy after Deligne
and Conrad*, whose output is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`.

Let $S$ be qcqs, let $V\to S$ be quasi-compact and locally of finite
presentation, let $U\subseteq S$ be a quasi-compact open, and let
$\mathcal M$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module whose
restriction over $U$ is finitely presented and flat over $U$. There is a
$U$-admissible blow-up $S'\to S$ such that the module strict transform
$\mathcal M'$ on $V\times_SS'$ is finitely presented and flat over $S'$.

## Proof

Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-data-flattening-package] to the finite affine
presentations of $\mathcal M$. Its finite composite of admissible blow-ups
is a single $U$-admissible blow-up by
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-comp]. The package proves on each
chart that the strict transform is finitely presented and flat, and the
overlap equations make these local transforms glue.

attrs.title: Flattening a finite-type module by an admissible blow-up, [stacks-project]

objects.body:
The recursively constructed factorization
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)$ is a compactification of $X\to S$.
Consequently $X\to S$ is compactifiable.

## Proof

The final component $h_n$ of the dependent recursive datum in
[def-nagata-noetherian-compactification] has the three fields required
by [def-nagata-compactification], and $X_n=X$. Thus
$\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(X/S)$ is a compactification of $X\to S$. No
later induction theorem is used to define any earlier $\mathsf C_r$.

attrs.title: Nagata compactification over a Noetherian base

objects.body:
Under the preceding hypotheses, the comparison morphism
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ identifies the blow-up of $Y$ in the extended ideal
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ with the strict transform of $Y$: there is an
isomorphism
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)\cong Y^{\mathrm{st}}$
compatible with the projections to $Y$ and with the structure morphisms
to $X$. No finiteness hypotheses on $\mathcal I$ are needed.

## Proof

Write $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ and let
$\Omega\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the open locus over $U$, whose
scheme-theoretic closure is the strict transform
([def-nagata-strict-transform]). Both $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ and the
inclusion of $\Omega$ are cut out by quasi-coherent kernels, and it
suffices to identify the two kernels. The blow-up of
$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ is an isomorphism over the preimage of $U$
([thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]), which identifies $\Omega$
with the preimage $\Omega'$ of $f^{-1}(U)$ in
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$, compatibly with
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ — the two composites into $X'$ agree by the
uniqueness part of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], since both
lie over $U$ where the pulled-back ideal is the unit ideal. The
exceptional ideal is invertible, i.e. locally generated by a
nonzerodivisor, so $\Omega'$ is schematically dense in
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y}(Y)$ (the blow-up part of
[lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-preserves-density]). Hence
precomposing $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ with the schematically dense open
$\Omega'\cong\Omega$ does not change the kernel, and the kernel of
$\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ equals the kernel of the inclusion of $\Omega$.
Since $\psi_{f,\mathcal I}$ is a closed immersion
([def-nagata-strict-transform-blowup-comparison]), it factors as an
isomorphism onto the strict transform, and the stated compatibilities
hold by construction.

The constructed factorization $\mathsf C_{12}(U/S)$ is a compactification
of $U\to S$. Consequently $U\to S$ is compactifiable.

## Proof

By [lemma-nagata-two-open-final-modification], the first map
$j_W\colon U\to W$ is an open immersion and $W\to S$ is separated and of
finite type. It is proper by
[lemma-nagata-two-open-candidate-proper]. The open immersion $j_W$ is
quasi-compact by
[lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to the
triangle $U\to W\to S$. The defining gluing maps give the factorization
equality, so all fields of [def-nagata-compactification] are present.

Let $(j,i)$ be a complementary pair on $X$ and let
$\mathcal F\in\shv{\et X}$. Then

$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*\mathcal F
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha_{\mathcal F}\ }\mathcal F
\xrightarrow{\ \beta_{\mathcal F}\ }i_*i^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow0
$$

is a short exact sequence in $\shv{\et X}$, naturally in $\mathcal F$: the
two maps are the components of natural transformations, so the sequence is a
short complex of endofunctors $j_!j^*\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow i_*i^*$
of $\shv{\et X}$ whose evaluation at $\mathcal F$ is the displayed one, and it
is short exact at every $\mathcal F$.

## Proof

*It is a complex.* By the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ and
[lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar],

$$
\Hom(j_!j^*\mathcal F,i_*i^*\mathcal F)
\cong\Hom(j^*\mathcal F,j^*i_*i^*\mathcal F)=0,
$$

so $\beta_{\mathcal F}\circ\alpha_{\mathcal F}=0$ with no computation.

*After $j^*$.* The functor $j^*$ is exact. Applying it to the complex
and using that the unit $\mathrm{id}\to j^*j_!$ is an isomorphism and that
$j^*i_*=0$ by [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar], the complex becomes

$$
0\to j^*\mathcal F\to j^*\mathcal F\to0\to0,
$$

in which the first map is the identity by the triangle identity for
$j_!\dashv j^*$. This is short exact.

*After $i^*$.* The functor $i^*$ is exact. Applying it and using
$i^*j_!=0$ from [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowershriek] and the counit
isomorphism $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ from
[prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful], the complex becomes

$$
0\to0\to i^*\mathcal F\to i^*\mathcal F\to0,
$$

in which the second map is the identity, again by a triangle identity. This
is short exact.

*Descent of exactness.* Let $M$ be any of the three homology objects of
the complex. Since $j^*$ and $i^*$ are exact they commute with homology, so
$j^*M=0$ and $i^*M=0$ by the two previous paragraphs. The map $0\to M$ is
therefore an isomorphism after $j^*$ and after $i^*$, hence an isomorphism by
[prop-openclosed-conservative], that is, $M=0$. All three homology
objects vanish, so $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is a monomorphism,
$\beta_{\mathcal F}$ is an epimorphism, and $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is a kernel
of $\beta_{\mathcal F}$.

*Naturality in $\mathcal F$.* Nothing is to be proved: $\alpha$ and
$\beta$ are a counit and a unit, hence natural transformations, so the short
complex exists already at the level of endofunctors of $\shv{\et X}$ and the
complex above is its evaluation at $\mathcal F$.

Fix schemes $X,Y$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, and an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$. For each of $X,Y$, choose either its ambient diagram
$\mathcal A_E$ or its constructible diagram $\mathcal C_E$, and denote
the chosen diagrams by $\mathcal B_E^X,\mathcal B_E^Y$. Suppose exact
functors $\Phi_E:\mathcal B_E^X\to\mathcal B_E^Y$ are
equipped, for every $E\subset L$, with exact natural isomorphisms

$$
T^Y_{L/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_LT^X_{L/E}
$$

satisfying the unit, tower, and shift equations. Then they induce an exact
functor on the corresponding common-stage categories. The same statement
holds for exact functors of finitely many variables. Compatible natural transformations,
adjunction units and counits, base-change maps, projection maps, purity maps,
and duality maps descend by the same common-stage construction. If ambient
functors carry the constructible subdiagrams into the
constructible subdiagrams, the descended functor restricts to
$D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$. For $Rf^!$, the coefficient comparison is the mate of the comparison for
$Rf_!$, and its tower coherence is part of the hypotheses.
Lecture 42, Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.2.

For a scheme $Y$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure
$\Qlb/\Ql$, and the common-stage construction of
Definitions [def-qbar-finext-diagram]–
[def-qbar-coefficient-category].
For both the ambient and constructible diagrams, the representative
relation, addition, identities, and composition are well defined. Each
pair category is a $\Qlb$-linear ordinary triangulated category with the
stated shifts and distinguished triangles, and is idempotent-complete.

For every ordinary triangulated category $\mathcal T$ and either choice
$\mathcal B_E(Y)\in\{\mathcal A_E(Y),\mathcal C_E(Y)\}$, exact functors
from its pair category to $\mathcal T$ are equivalent to families of
exact functors $F_E:\mathcal B_E(Y)\to\mathcal T$ equipped with unit-,
tower-, and shift-compatible isomorphisms
$F_LT_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E$.
Every object, morphism, finite diagram, and distinguished triangle in
$D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to one defined over a single
finite coefficient extension after enlarging that extension.
Lecture 42, Theorems 3.12, 4.5, 6.4, and 6.5.

attrs.title: Correctness and universal property of the $2$-colimit

objects.body:
For a scheme $Y$, fix an auxiliary finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$.
Tensoring with $E_Y$ induces an exact equivalence

$$
D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }D^b_c(Y,E),
$$

where the source has the same objects as $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and,
for every $K,L\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$,

$$
\Hom(K,L)[1/\varpi_E]
=\Hom_{D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)}(K,L)
\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E.
$$

Every rational constructible complex therefore admits an integral lattice;
two lattices become commensurable after multiplication by powers of
$\varpi_E$.

For every smooth-proper datum $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ and every auxiliary
finite coefficient datum
$(\ell,\Qlb;E,\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E)$, the structure morphism
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at every finite
coefficient stage, at $\mathcal O_E$, at $E$, and at $\Qlb$, with the
uniform amplitude and coefficient-comparison data required by
Definition [def-exceptional-adjoint-admissible].
Lecture 44, Theorem 6.20, together with the smooth-proper
amplitude and finite-Tor admissibility input made explicit there.

attrs.title: Exceptional admissibility of a smooth-proper structure map

objects.body:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected scheme of pure
dimension $d$ over $\Fq$. Put $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let
$\mathscr X$ be the resulting smooth-proper datum, and let
$P_i=P_i(\mathscr X)$ be the canonical factors of
Definition [def-canonical-cohomological-factors]. Then the following
statements hold.

1. The zeta series has both point-counting descriptions
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\exp\left(\sum_{n\geq1}
\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\frac{T^n}{n}\right)
=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}(1-T^{\deg(x)})^{-1},
$$
and belongs to $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$.
1. The polynomials $P_i$ are the unique polynomials
$$
P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]
\qquad(0\leq i\leq2d)
$$
with $P_i(0)=1$ such that, for every prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
\bigl((\mathbf Z[T]\longrightarrow\Ql[T])(P_i)\bigr)(T)=
\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql)).
$$
They give the rational factorization
$$
Z(X_0,T)=
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
1. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$
and regard $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ inside
$\overline{\mathbf Q}[T]$. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, every
reciprocal root $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ is an
algebraic integer
and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$:
$$
|\tau(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}
$$
for every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\alpha)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. For every ordinary
root $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $P_i$ and every embedding
$\tau:\mathbf Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, one has
$|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$.
1. For every $0\leq i\leq2d$, with $b_i=\deg P_i$, and every
prime $\ell\neq p$,
$$
b_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
\qquad b_i=b_{2d-i},
\qquad b_0=b_{2d}=1,
$$
independently of $\ell$. Moreover
$$
P_0(T)=1-T,
\qquad
P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$
1. If
$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T),
\qquad
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
$$
then $d\chi$ is even and, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$,
$$
P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})
=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}D_i^{-1}P_i(T),
$$
and
$$
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$
for the sign
$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-d\chi/2}
\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}
\in\{1,-1\}.
$$

**Status.** Both Lean statements exist and both proofs are `sorry`.
`weil_conjectures` states clauses (ii), (iii) and
(v) for a smooth, proper, geometrically integral $X_0$, phrased
through the three predicates `IsWeilFactorization`,
`WeilFunctionalEquation` and `WeilRiemannHypothesis`, which are
complete definitions; `zetaSeries_rational` states the rationality
assertion of clause (i) for an arbitrary scheme of finite type over
$\Fq$.

## Proof

The hypotheses make $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ a smooth-proper datum, so all
degreewise factors and Frobenius operators in Definitions
[def-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] and
[def-frobenius-characteristic-factors] are available.

*Clause (i).*
Definition [def-point-count-zeta] is the exponential point-counting
description. Proposition [prop-euler-product] gives the closed-point
Euler product and membership in $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$. Proposition
[prop-integral-recovery] gives the factorization by integral
polynomials and hence $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$.
This proves exactly the two displayed descriptions and both coefficient
claims in (i).

*Clause (ii).*
Proposition [prop-integral-recovery] applies to the fixed datum and says
that the canonical $P_i\in\mathbf Z[T]$ have constant term one, satisfy

$$
\bigl((\mathbf Z[T]\longrightarrow\Ql[T])(P_i)\bigr)(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T)
=\det(1-TF\mid H^i(X,\Ql))
$$

for every prime $\ell\neq p$, are the unique integral family with those
realizations, and obey

$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q(T).
$$

These are precisely all assertions of (ii).

*Clause (iii).*
Fix $0\leq i\leq2d$. Proposition
[prop-arithmetic-roots] applies to the polynomial $P_i$ in the fixed
algebraic closure. It states that every reciprocal root is an algebraic
integer and a $q$-Weil number of weight $i$, with the displayed equality
for every complex embedding. The same proposition identifies an ordinary
root $\beta$ with the inverse of a reciprocal root of this same
polynomial $P_i$, and gives $|\tau(\beta)|=q^{-i/2}$. This proves
(iii) without changing the root terminology.

*Clause (iv).*
Fix an integer $0\leq i\leq2d$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$,
Proposition [prop-integral-recovery] gives

$$
b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}H^i(X,\Ql),
$$

so the left-hand side is independent of $\ell$. Proposition
[prop-duality-reciprocity] gives $b_i=b_{2d-i}$, and Proposition
[prop-endpoints] gives

$$
b_0=b_{2d}=1,\qquad P_0(T)=1-T,\qquad P_{2d}(T)=1-q^dT.
$$

This is exactly (iv).

*Clause (v).*
The definitions of $D_i,\chi,\varepsilon$ are respectively
Definitions [def-determinant-constants],
[def-euler-characteristic],
and [def-functional-equation-sign]. Proposition
[prop-duality-reciprocity] supplies, for every $i$, the asserted
degreewise Laurent reciprocity. Proposition
[prop-functional-equation-parity] verifies that $d\chi/2$ is an
integer. Finally Proposition [prop-functional-equation] proves

$$
\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\},\qquad
Z(X_0,q^{-d}T^{-1})
=\varepsilon q^{d\chi/2}T^\chi Z(X_0,T)
$$

in $\mathbf Q(T)$. Hence all assertions of (v) follow.

The five independently verified clauses are exactly the conjunction stated
in the theorem.

attrs.title: Weil conjectures for a smooth proper variety

objects.body:
Assume every exact terminal input in Appendix [app-gap-ledger], together
with every imported interface whose manifest status is not closed. Then the
ordered S0–S7 argument proves finite-torsion proper base change in
$D^+_c(X_{\mathrm{et}})$; S8 transports the comparison to finite-level
pro-etale objects; and S9–S10 prove the completed comparison under the
displayed perfect-quotient, projection-formula, reconstruction, and
$R\varprojlim$ hypotheses.

## Proof

The detailed construction and every intermediate proof are reproduced in
Chapters [chap-s0-s10] and [chap-compact-support]. Appendix
[app-gap-ledger] records the exact unproved hypotheses, so this theorem
does not promote the historical owner.

Let $B:V\times W\to E$ be a perfect similitude pairing of multiplier $\mu$ for
the automorphisms $F_V,F_W$. Put $b=\dim_EV=\dim_EW$ and
$D_V=\det(F_V)$, and set

$$
P_V(T)=\det(1-TF_V\mid V),
\qquad
P_W(T)=\det(1-TF_W\mid W).
$$

Then, in $E[T,T^{-1}]$,

$$
P_W(\mu^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^bT^{-b}D_V^{-1}P_V(T),
$$

or equivalently

$$
P_W(T)=(-1)^b\mu^bD_V^{-1}T^bP_V(\mu^{-1}T^{-1}).
$$

## Proof

Over an algebraic closure, $P_V(T)=\prod_{j=1}^b(1-\alpha_jT)$ with the
$\alpha_j$ the eigenvalues of $F_V$, all nonzero, and
$D_V=\prod_j\alpha_j$. By
[prop-zla-reciprocal-eigenvalue-pairing],
$P_W(T)=\prod_j(1-\mu\alpha_j^{-1}T)$. Substituting $T\mapsto\mu^{-1}T^{-1}$
and clearing $\prod_j(-\alpha_j^{-1}T^{-1})$ from the product gives the first
identity; both sides have coefficients in $E$, so the identity descends from
$\Omega[T,T^{-1}]$ to $E[T,T^{-1}]$. The second form follows by substituting
$T\mapsto\mu^{-1}T^{-1}$ once more.

For every field extension $K\subseteq L$,

$$
K[[T]]\cap L(T)_0=K(T)_0
$$

inside $L[[T]]$. Explicitly, if $f\in K[[T]]$ becomes the Taylor series of a
normalized rational germ over $L$, then its coefficient sequence has finite
shift span over $K$, and the characteristic polynomial of the shift on that
span constructs a normalized rational germ over $K$ whose Taylor series is
$f$.

## Proof

Let $a$ be the coefficient sequence of $f$, which lies in $K^{\mathbf N}$. A
normalized rational germ over $L$ with Taylor series $f$ supplies an eventual
recurrence for $a$ over $L$ ([lem-zla-germ-recurrence]), hence a finite
bound on $\dim_L\operatorname{Sh}_L(a)$
([lem-zla-recurrence-shift-span]). Any $K$-independent family of shifts
of $a$ has a nonvanishing finite coordinate determinant
([lem-zla-finite-coordinates]) and therefore stays independent over $L$
([lem-zla-det-scalar-extension]); so $\dim_K\operatorname{Sh}_K(a)$ is
bounded by the same number. Now [prop-zla-shift-span-germ] over $K$
produces $A_a,B_a\in K[T]$ with $B_a(0)=1$ and
$f=\tau_K[A_a,B_a]$. The reverse inclusion is trivial.

Let $f(T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ be the Taylor series of a normalized rational
germ over $\mathbf Q$. There is a unique pair of polynomials
$A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$, coprime in $\mathbf Q[T]$, satisfying

$$
A(0)=B(0)=1,
\qquad
f(T)=\frac{A(T)}{B(T)}.
$$

This is the *normalized reduced integral presentation* of $f$.

## Proof

[prop-zla-integral-presentation] produces $A_0,B_0\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with
$B_0f=A_0$; here $A_0(0)=f(0)=1=B_0(0)$. Reducing this fraction by
[prop-zla-normalized-gcd-reduction] gives coprime integral $A,B$ with
constant coefficient $1$ and $A/B=A_0/B_0=f$. If $(A',B')$ is a second pair
with the same properties, then $A'/B'=f=A/B$ and both denominators are nonzero,
so cross multiplication gives $A'B=B'A$; both pairs are coprime and all four
polynomials have constant coefficient $1$, so
[lem-zla-normalized-fraction-unique] over $\mathbf Q$ yields $A'=A$ and
$B'=B$.

Note that $q$ is an isomorphism over $V$, since
$V(\mathcal I_1+\mathcal I_2)\subseteq V(\mathcal I_2)=T_2$ is disjoint from

$V$-admissible blow-up. The set-theoretic inclusion
$p^{-1}(T_1)\cap\overline Y\subseteq p^{-1}(T_2)$ is not enough for what
follows: it is the scheme-theoretic factorization in item (3) that produces the

objects.body:
The formal proof (`exists_lift_blowup` together with
`hom_ext_of_isInvertible_comap`) takes the
Stacks-style hypothesis that the inverse image ideal sheaf of the center is
effective Cartier, and is entirely chart-local: existence is glued from the
universal property of the chart ring $A[\mathcal I/a]$
(`AffineBlowup.chartRingLift`) on affine probes, and uniqueness
follows from chart-ring extensionality
(`chartRingHom_ext`) together with the chart-overlap localization.
The graded-map and tensor-power scaffolding
([def-nagata-blowup-universal-graded-map],
[lemma-nagata-invertible-ideal-tensor-power],
[lemma-nagata-relative-proj-invertible-tensor-powers],
[def-nagata-blowup-universal-lift]) is not formalized.

ValuationSubring.exists_comap_eq.doc:
**Extension of a valuation ring to a field extension** (Stacks Project Tag 00IA):
for every field extension `f : K →+* L` and every valuation subring `A ⊆ K` there is a

valuation subring of `L`.

ValuationSubring.comap_eq_of_toLocalSubr.doc:

Tag 052K): if a valuation subring `B` of a field extension `L` of `K` dominates a
valuation subring `A ⊆ K` — that is, `A ≤ B.comap f` in the domination order of local
subrings of `K` — then `K ∩ B = A`, i.e. `B.comap f = A`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-valuation-intersection`.)

closed subsets `T₁`, `T₂` there are compact opens `O₁`, `O₂` covering the space such

theorem CategoryTheory.exists_mem_forall_exists_linearMap.{v, u, v'} {C : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] (J : CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology C) {Λ : Type v'}
  [Ring Λ] [CategoryTheory.HasWeakSheafify J (ModuleCat Λ)]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (ModuleCat Λ)] {T : C} (M N : ModuleCat Λ) [Finite ↑M]
  (φ :
    (CategoryTheory.constantSheaf J (ModuleCat Λ)).obj M ⟶
      (CategoryTheory.constantSheaf J (ModuleCat Λ)).obj N) :
  ∃ S ∈ J T,
    ∀ ⦃U : C⦄ (g : U ⟶ T),
      S.arrows g →
        ⊥ ∉ J U →
          ∃ f,
            ∀ (m : ↑M),
              (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom (φ.hom.app (Opposite.op U)))
                  ((CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom
                      ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify J ((CategoryTheory.Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj M)).app
                        (Opposite.op U)))
                    m) =
                (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom
                    ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify J ((CategoryTheory.Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj N)).app
                      (Opposite.op U)))
                  ((CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom f) m)
CategoryTheory.exists_mem_forall_exists_.doc:
**A morphism between constant sheaves of modules is locally induced by a linear map**,
in the form of sections: for `φ : M_C ⟶ N_C` with `M` finite and any object `T`, there is a
covering sieve `S` of `T` such that over every member `U` of `S` not covered by the empty
sieve, `φ` sends the constant section `m` over `U` to the constant section `f m`, for a
`Λ`-linear map `f : M ⟶ N`. The map `f` is obtained by lifting the finitely many
sections `φ♭(m)`, `m : M`, to elements of `N` on a common cover; it is linear since
`N ⟶ N_C(U)` is injective.

**A morphism between constant sheaves of modules is locally induced by a linear map**:

AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_properClosedM.doc:
**Step 3 of the proof of Chow's lemma.** An affine scheme `V` locally of finite type over a
Noetherian scheme `S` admits a proper closed model: a closed subscheme `Z` of some projective
space `ℙ(n; S)` with `n` finite, containing `V` as a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme
and proper over `S`.

Indeed, `V` immerses into some `ℙ(n; S)` over `S` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_projectiveSpace`, and this immersion is quasi-compact
since `V` is Noetherian; so its scheme-theoretic image does the job.

resulting common blow-up of `X₁₂` across the open strict transforms.

AlgebraicGeometry.noetherianCompactifica.doc:
**The recursive Noetherian compactification construction**: given a finite family of
affine opens `U` of `X` with dense total intersection, a compactification of every partial
union `X_r = U 0 ∪ ⋯ ∪ U (r - 1)` over `S`, constructed by recursion on `r`.

`X_0` is empty, hence proper over `S`; `X_1 = U 0` is affine, so the affine case applies;
and `X_{r+1} = X_r ∪ U r` is obtained from `X_r` and `U r` by the two-open theorem, whose
density hypothesis holds because the total intersection of the cover is contained in both
`X_r` and `U r`.
(blueprint: `def:nagata-noetherian-compactification`)

approximation, `f` is descended to one of the stages, compactified there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.nagataCompactification_of_isNoetherian` and the compactification is base
changed back to `S`.

AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierCent.doc:
**A closed immersion is an effective Cartier centre exactly when its kernel is
invertible.** Unfolding `Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsInvertible`, the right-hand side is the
affine-local assertion that the defining ideal of `Z` is generated by one non-zerodivisor, so
this is the promised description of (MLCI1) under the correspondence between closed
immersions and quasi-coherent ideals.

The forward direction holds because the kernel does not change under precomposition with an
isomorphism, and the kernel of `J.subschemeι` is `J`. The backward direction produces the
isomorphism from the universal property of closed immersions: `z` and `z.ker.subschemeι` are
two closed immersions with the same kernel, hence canonically isomorphic over `X`.
(blueprint: final assertion of `lemma:nagata-invertible-ideal-effective-cartier`)

**Morphisms of `S`-schemes into a separated `S`-scheme agreeing on a
scheme-theoretically dominant subscheme are equal.** For `S`-morphisms `f g : T ⟶ Y`
into a separated `S`-scheme `Y`, `f = g` as soon as `ι ≫ f = ι ≫ g` for some
scheme-theoretically dominant `ι : W ⟶ T`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated'` with dominance of `ι`
strengthened to scheme-theoretic dominance and, in exchange, the reducedness assumption
on `T` dropped.

  (hU : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι f = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ι g) : f = g
AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isSchemeTheoret.doc:
**Morphisms into a separated target agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dominant
subscheme are equal.** Suppose `f g : T ⟶ Y` agree over some separated `s : Y ⟶ Z`.
Then `f = g` as soon as `ι ≫ f = ι ≫ g` for some scheme-theoretically dominant
`ι : W ⟶ T`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant_of_isSeparated` with dominance of `ι`
strengthened to scheme-theoretic dominance and, in exchange, the reducedness assumption
on `T` dropped.

**Rigidity of morphisms into a separated scheme**: if `Y` is separated over `S`, then
two `S`-morphisms `a b : T ⟶ Y` that agree after composing with a scheme-theoretically
dominant morphism `v : V ⟶ T` are equal. The classical case is `v = V.ι` for a
scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme `V ⊆ T`.

The equaliser of `a` and `b` is the base change of the diagonal `Y ⟶ Y ×[S] Y` along
`(a, b) : T ⟶ Y ×[S] Y`, hence a *closed* subscheme of `T` because `Y ⟶ S` is separated.
As `v` factors through it, its kernel ideal sheaf is contained in the kernel of `v`, which
is trivial; so the closed immersion is an isomorphism, in particular an epimorphism, and
`a = b`. (blueprint: `lem:chow-agree-on-dense-open`)

scheme, let `s` be a finite set of generic points of irreducible components of `X` and let
`x : X`. Then there is an affine open of `X` containing `x` and all points of `s`.

(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-quasi-affine-affine-base`).

Over an affine base, the quasi-affineness of `Y` as a scheme is the same as the
quasi-affineness of `p` as a morphism, so this is the absolute form of the hypothesis.

The proof embeds `Y` into a relative affine space over `X`
(`exists_immersion_affineSpace_of_quasiAffine'`, Stacks Tag 04II), extends `f` there by
`exists_isAdmissible_extend_affineSpace`, makes the preimage of `U` scheme-theoretically
dense by one further blow-up
(`IsAdmissible.exists_comp_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_preimage`), and descends the
extension back to `Y` along the closed-immersion part of the immersion, using that a
morphism agreeing on a scheme-theoretically dense open with one factoring through a closed
subscheme factors through it as well.

**Conrad's Theorem 2.4, Case 3, Step 1**: the disjointness blow-up.

Let `X` be qcqs, let `U ≤ V` be quasi-compact opens of `X`, let `p : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism
from a qcqs scheme and let `f : U ⟶ Y` be a section of `p` over `U` whose image is closed
in `p ⁻¹ V`. There is a `V`-admissible blow-up of `X` after which the closure of the image
of the base change of `f` is disjoint from the part lying over the closure of `V ∖ U`.

The base change is left flexible: `Z'` is an arbitrary scheme over `Y` and over
`(I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowup`, and `Y'` an arbitrary scheme over `U` and over `Z'`, fitting into the two
commuting squares, exactly as in `AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup`.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-conrad-case3-disjointness-reduction`.)

**Elimination of indeterminacy** (Stacks Project Tag 081S; blueprint:
`def:nagata-elimination-indeterminacy`, `lemma:nagata-elimination-indeterminacy`;
proof order item 30).

The proof follows the Conrad/Zariski's-Main-Theorem route: prepare a Cartier boundary
(`exists_admissibleBlowup_cartierBoundary`, Stacks Project Tag 080Y) so that `U` becomes
scheme-theoretically dense, extend the inverse of `q` over `U` to a section over an open
`W` of a second admissible blow-up (`exists_admissibleBlowup_extend_section`, Conrad's
Remark 2.5), compose the two blow-ups (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp`, Stacks
Project Tag 080B, whose support formula shows that the composite centre is still supported
exactly on the complement of `U`), and identify the strict transform with `W`: the graph
of the extension is closed and contains the scheme-theoretically dense `U`-graph, so it
cuts out the strict transform.

AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowu.doc:
**Isomorphism near the closure of a boundary piece** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3W;
blueprint: `def:nagata-isomorphism-near-closure`,
`lemma:nagata-isomorphism-near-closure`; used for the improved comparison projection of
the two-open compactification theorem).

The proof runs as follows. Inside `U`, constructible separation
(`PrespectralSpace.exists_isCompact_isOpen_disjoint_union_eq_univ`) separates `T` from
the complement of the maximal isomorphism open `M` of `q`, producing a quasi-compact
open `V₂` of `X` with `T ⊆ V₂ ⊆ U ⊓ M` and a constructible closed decomposition of `U`.
The boundary-separation blow-up `X₁ ⟶ X` (`exists_admissibleBlowup_disjoint_closures`,
Tag 0F3V) then separates the closure of the inverse image of `T` from the closure of
the inverse image of `U \ V₂`, and a second constructible separation, now in `X₁`,
produces a **quasi-compact** open `A ⊆ X₁` containing the first closure and missing the
second; consequently every point of `A` over `U` lies over `V₂`.

Over `X₁` the canonical lift of `q` is an isomorphism above `V₂`, so eliminating its
indeterminacy (`exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`, Tag 081S)
gives a finite-type centre whose support misses the locus above `V₂`, hence also
`A ∩ π₁⁻¹(U)`. Gluing that centre across `A` and the locus above `U`
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_comap_eq_of_disjoint`, Tag 080M) and composing
with the first blow-up (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comp_base_change`, Tag 080B)
produces a single `U`-admissible centre `K` on `X`, together with identifications of
both `K.blowup` and `(K.comap q).blowup` with their counterparts upstairs.

Finally Tag 080E (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_blowup_comap_iso_strictTransform`)
turns the strict transform of `q` along `K.blowupMap` into the canonical lift
`(K.comap q).blowup ⟶ K.blowup`, and the localization of canonical lifts
(`Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_comm_lift_blowup_comap_opens`) identifies that lift over
the copy of `A` with the open immersion produced by Tag 081S. The neighbourhood `N'` is
the range of the resulting partial section; it contains the closure of the inverse
image of `T` because that closure lies over `A` and inside the (closed, since `q` is
proper) range of the strict transform. No scheme-theoretic density argument is used.

    ∃ (hUW : (TopologicalSpace.Opens.map B.I.blowupMap.base).obj U ≤ W),
      ∃ g,
        ∃ (hg :
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp g p =
            CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp W.ι B.I.blowupMap),
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (B.I.blowup.homOfLE hUW) g =
              CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (B.I.blowupMap ∣_ U) f ∧
            IsClosed (Set.range ⇑(CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift g W.ι hg))
AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowu.doc:
**Conrad's Theorem 2.4, reduced to the base `X`** (blueprint:
`thm:nagata-conrad-elimination`, in the form reduced to the base `X`;
`def:nagata-conrad-quasi-domination`).

Conrad's Theorem 2.4 is stated for a rational map over an auxiliary base `S`; the first
step of his proof replaces `Y` by `Y ×_S X`, which is the reduction to the form stated
here. In the vocabulary of the blueprint the hypothesis says that `(U, f)` is a
quasi-domination of `V` over `Y`, and the conclusion that `(W, g)` is a
quasi-domination of the blow-up over `Y` extending `f`.

Elimination of indeterminacy (Stacks Project Tag 081S,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isOpenImmersion_strictTransformMap`) is
deduced from this statement.

Density of `U` is not used: neither Conrad's Case 3 nor the quasi-finiteness of the graph
needs it. The hypothesis is kept because it is part of the interface consumed
downstream.

**The constructible-boundary separation blow-up** (Stacks Project Tags 080P and
0F3V; blueprint: `def:nagata-separate-constructible-closed`,
`lemma:nagata-separate-constructible-closed`,
`def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`, `lemma:nagata-prepared-boundaries`;
proof order item 36).

The blow-up is the boundary-separation blow-up of the sum of two finite-type ideals
`I₁`, `I₂` extending the vanishing ideals of `T₁`, `T₂` from `U` (Stacks Tags 01PH
and 01PF, `Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_finiteType_preimage_coe_support_eq`); the
closure of the inverse image of `Tᵢ` is contained in the strict transform of `V(Iᵢ)`
(`IsAdmissible.closure_preimage_subset_range_strictTransformMap`), and these strict
transforms are disjoint by `disjoint_range_strictTransformMap_sup`.

**Preparation of a Cartier boundary** (Stacks Project Tag 080Y; blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-cartier-boundary-preparation`; proof order item 24).

AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_fac_or_fa.doc:
A point of `X` with values in a field `K` lies either on the open `U` or on its closed
complement `Z`, as a factorization of morphisms of schemes: any `s : Spec K ⟶ X` is either of
the form `t ≫ j` for a unique `t : Spec K ⟶ U`, or of the form `t ≫ i` for a unique
`t : Spec K ⟶ Z`.

The open half is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.lift`, unique because an open immersion is
a monomorphism; the closed half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.existsUnique_fac_of_field`. What carries the closed half
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.le_ker_iff_range_subset_support`, whose hypothesis
on the source is `IsReduced (Spec K)`; the field hypothesis is used beyond that only for
`Subsingleton (Spec K)`, which upgrades "the closed point of `Spec K` lands in the range of
`i`" to "the whole range of `s` lands in the range of `i`".
(blueprint: `lemma:openclosed-point-factors`)

AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_range_strictT.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_range_strictTransformMap_sup.{u} {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme}
  [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (I₁ I₂ : X.IdealSheafData) (h₁ : I₁.ofFiniteType)
  (h₂ : I₂.ofFiniteType) :
  Disjoint
    (Set.range
      ⇑(AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformMap I₁.subschemeι (I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowupMap
          (I₁ ⊔ I₂).support.compl))
    (Set.range
      ⇑(AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformMap I₂.subschemeι (I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowupMap
          (I₁ ⊔ I₂).support.compl))
AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_range_strictT.doc:
**Boundary separation** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3V; revised blueprint
`lemma:nagata-separate-closed-subschemes`).

The proof is the chart argument of the revised blueprint: the charts of
`Bl_{I₁ ⊔ I₂}(X)` at degree-one elements coming from local sections of `I₁` or of `I₂`
cover the blow-up (`exists_mem_range_chart_sup`), and the strict transform of `V(Iᵢ)`
misses every `Iᵢ`-chart, because on such a chart the extension of the center is
generated by a section of `Iᵢ` (`disjoint_range_strictTransformMap_of_probe`); so the
two strict transforms have no common point.

**Disjointness of boundary closures persists along strict transforms**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-boundary-disjoint-persists`; proof order item 37).

Each strict transform is contained in the full inverse image of the corresponding closed
subscheme.

AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range_of_blowupMap_sup.{u}
  {X Z Y Z' Y' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {p : Z ⟶ X} {f : Y ⟶ Z} {U V : X.Opens} (hUV : U ≤ V)
  {I₁ I₂ : X.IdealSheafData} (hI₂V : ↑I₂.support ⊆ (↑V)ᶜ) (hVU : ↑V \ ↑U ⊆ ↑I₁.support)
  (hYU : Set.range ⇑(CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f p) ⊆ ↑U)
  (hfac : I₂.comap p ≤ (I₁ * I₁).comap p ⊔ AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker f) {r : Z' ⟶ Z}
  {p' : Z' ⟶ (I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowup}
  (hw :
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp r p =
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p' (I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowupMap)
  {fY : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : Y' ⟶ Z'} [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f']
  (hcomm : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f' r = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp fY f) :
  Disjoint (closure (Set.range ⇑f')) (⇑p' ⁻¹' closure (⇑(I₁ ⊔ I₂).blowupMap ⁻¹' (↑V \ ↑U)))
AlgebraicGeometry.disjoint_closure_range.doc:
**Deligne's disjointness blow-up** (Deligne, *Lemme* 0.3; Conrad, Lemma 1.5; blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-conrad-disjointness-blowup`).

Differences from the informal statement: the base change is not required to be the chosen
fibre product — any commuting squares `hw` for `Z'` and `hcomm` for `Y'` will do, so the
statement applies to whatever model of the base change the caller has at hand — and the
scheme-theoretic image of `f'` is expressed as the closure of its range, which is what the
quasi-compactness of `f'` makes it.

AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalRestrictChartA.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalRestrictChartArrowIso.{u} {W S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (w : W ⟶ S)
  {T₁ T₂ : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (j₁ : T₁ ⟶ W) (j₂ : T₂ ⟶ W)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion j₁] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion j₂] :
  CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk
      (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal w ∣_
        AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.opensRange
          (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp j₁ w)
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp j₂ w) w w j₁ j₂ (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id S)
            ⋯ ⋯)) ≅
    CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk
      (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map j₁ j₂ (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp j₁ w)
        (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp j₂ w) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id T₁)
        (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id T₂) w ⋯ ⋯)
AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalRestrictChartA.doc:
The restriction of the diagonal of `w : W ⟶ S` over the chart
`T₁ ×_S T₂ ⊆ W ×_S W` attached to a pair of open immersions `jᵢ : Tᵢ ⟶ W` is the
canonical morphism `T₁ ×_W T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_S T₂`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis.signature: def AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis (q d : ℕ) (P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilRiemannHypothesis.doc:
The Riemann hypothesis part of the Weil conjectures: every inverse root of `Pᵢ` has
absolute value `q^{i/2}`, i.e. every complex root `z` of `Pᵢ` satisfies `‖z‖ = q^{-i/2}`.

AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.signature: def AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation (q d : ℕ) (P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.WeilFunctionalEquation.doc:
The functional equation part of the Weil conjectures: `α ↦ qᵈ / α` maps the inverse
roots of `Pᵢ` bijectively (with multiplicity) to the inverse roots of `P_{2d - i}`.
In terms of the complex roots `z = 1 / α` this says that `z ↦ 1 / (qᵈ z)` identifies the
root multisets of `Pᵢ` and `P_{2d - i}`. It implies the classical functional equation
`Z(X, 1 / (qᵈ t)) = ± q^{dχ/2} tᵡ Z(X, t)` for the associated rational function.

AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt..doc:
**A valuative commutative square through a dense source** (Stacks Project Tag 02JQ):
every point of the target of a quasi-compact dominant morphism is the centre of a valuative
commutative square.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-valuation-probe`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt.signature:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt.{u} {T P : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (h : T ⟶ P) (z : ↥P) :
  Type (u + 1)
AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCommSqWithPt.doc:
A **valuative commutative square centred at a point** `z ∈ P` of a morphism
`h : T ⟶ P`: a valuative commutative square for `h` whose valuation-ring leg takes the
closed point of `Spec R` to `z`. It is the *valuation probe* of Stacks Project Tag 02JQ.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-dense-valuation-probe`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_v.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion_of_isDominant.{u}
  {U X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] (h : U ⟶ X)
  [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact h] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsDominant h]
  (H : AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCriterion.RelativeTo f h) : AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed f
AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_v.doc:
**The dense-source valuative criterion, universal closedness** (Stacks Project
Tag 0894): a quasi-compact morphism satisfying the valuative criterion relative to a
quasi-compact dominant `h : U ⟶ X` is universally closed.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-dense-source-valuative`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_v.doc: The **valuative criterion** for universally closed morphisms.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isSeparate.doc:
**Separatedness of the intermediate scheme** (Stacks Project Tag 0F3U; blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-intermediate-separated`): the two charts of `Wᵢ ⟶ S` are separated and
their overlap is a closed immersion.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_g.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_graph.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
  {O : U.Opens} (σ : AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide u O) : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper σ.graph
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_g.doc:
The graph of the proper extension is proper; in particular its range is closed.
(Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-proper-extension-graph-closed`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isProper_c.doc:
**Properness of the comparison projections** (blueprint:
`lemma:nagata-comparison-projections-proper`): the projection `X₁₂ ⟶ X₁` is a closed
immersion followed by a base change of the proper structure morphism of `X₂`.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.isClosedIm.doc:
**The overlap of the two charts of the intermediate scheme is a closed immersion**
(blueprint: `lemma:nagata-intermediate-overlap-constructible` through
`lemma:nagata-intermediate-overlap-closed`).

The range of the overlap map is the preimage of the closed range of the proper graph
`V ⟶ U ×_S X`, because over the complement of the forbidden boundary the graph passes
through the embedded copy of `O` exactly over `O` (`TwoOpenSide.range_υ`).

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.interior.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.interior.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
  {O : U.Opens} (σ : AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide u O) : σ.X.Opens
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.interior.doc:
The complement of the forbidden boundary, i.e. the locus `Xᵢ°` of the blueprint.
(Blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-intermediate-schemes`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.forbiddenB.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.forbiddenBoundary.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
  {O : U.Opens} (σ : AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide u O) : Set ↥σ.X
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.forbiddenB.doc:
The **forbidden boundary** of a side: the closure in the ambient scheme of the
inverse image under `ψ` of the closed complement `U ∖ O` of its own open. Removing it
yields the intermediate locus `Xᵢ°` of the blueprint.
(Blueprint: `Z̄_{i,j}` in `def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.dense_rang.doc:
**The copy of `U` is dense in the intermediate scheme**: the second chart is the
complement of the forbidden boundary, in which the embedded copy of `O` is dense.
(Blueprint: part of `lemma:nagata-two-open-density-transport`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.comparison.doc:
The **comparison space** `X₁₂`: the scheme-theoretic image of `V₁ ×_U V₂` in
`X₁ ×_S X₂`. (Blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-comparison-space`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.closure_im.doc:
The image in the ambient scheme of a closed boundary locus of `V` meets `V` in
exactly itself: boundary loci are closed in `V`.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.admissible.doc:
**Transport of a side along a `V`-admissible blow-up** of the ambient scheme
(blueprint: `def:nagata-two-open-prepared-boundaries`,
`def:nagata-two-open-improved-comparison`).

The open `V`, the proper extension `ψ` and the embedded copy of `O` transport along the
isomorphism over `V`; density transports because the complement of the center is dense in
the blow-up.

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.Prepared.signature:
def AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.Prepared.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
  {O : U.Opens} (σ : AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide u O) (O' : U.Opens) : Prop
AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.Prepared.doc:
A side is **prepared** relative to the other open `O'` if its two boundary closures
are disjoint. (Blueprint: `lemma:nagata-prepared-boundaries`.)

AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.KeyDisjoin.signature:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.TwoOpenSide.KeyDisjoint.avoids.{u} {U S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {u : U ⟶ S}
